Chapter Five
Frey woke up on sheets so soft they felt like clouds beneath him. The sensation was surreal, the bed unlike anything he’d ever experienced—satiny, smooth, and inviting him to sink deeper into its embrace. He lingered in that hazy space between sleep and waking, luxuriating in the comfort as he stretched lazily.
Then, two things struck him with sudden clarity.
One: He was completely naked.
Two: He was not alone in the bed.
Frey froze, every muscle in his body going still as he registered the warmth of another person beside him. He kept his breathing shallow, not wanting to disturb whoever it was. Opening his eyes slowly, he glanced down and his heart skipped a beat. Cobalt blue ears peeked through a mass of white hair, splayed across bare shoulders—equally naked shoulders.
Jun.
Frey’s mind raced as he tried to process the scene before him. He was in bed with Jun. Not just sharing a bed, but sharing a bed. A flurry of emotions and thoughts surged through him, but before he could react, Jun stirred. The soft sound he made sent a jolt straight through Frey’s core, a mix of panic and something more primal.
A calloused hand trailed up Frey’s bare chest, slow and teasing, sending a wave of heat across his skin. He held his breath, unsure of what to do.
“Mmm, good morning,” Jun murmured, his voice a low purr. He nuzzled his cheek into the curve of Frey’s shoulder, the intimacy of the gesture making Frey’s heart pound even harder. Warmth spread through him, pooling deep in his belly, and he swallowed hard, trying to keep his composure.
“Uh, hi,” Frey managed, his voice coming out hoarser than he intended. He twisted slightly, attempting to create some distance, but Jun only followed, his body pressing closer.
Then Frey felt something warm and wet trace the hollow of his shoulder—a tongue. The sensation sent a shiver down his spine, and he went impossibly still as Jun’s mouth moved lower, leaving a wet trail across his chest. Every touch, every sensation became heightened, and Frey found himself overwhelmed by the closeness, the smell of Jun—his hair, his skin, his sweat, his blood.
The scent of it filled Frey’s senses, and something stirred within him. He could feel the steady pulse of Jun’s heartbeat, the rhythm echoing in his ears, drawing him in. It was intoxicating, the thick and heavy thrum of life so close, so accessible. All he had to do was lean in, press his lips to that tantalising blue skin, and let instinct take over.
To taste. To suck. To devour. It would be so easy.
Frey’s breath quickened, a dark hunger rising inside him. His gums ached suddenly, and he felt the sharp points of fangs pierce his lips. The sensation was new, yet disturbingly natural, as if his body knew exactly what to do. He wanted to sink those teeth into Jun, to taste the life coursing just beneath the surface.
No.
Panic cut through the haze, a sharp realisation snapping him back to himself. This wasn’t him. This wasn’t right. The hunger that clawed at his mind wasn’t his own. He was losing control—he was going to hurt Jun.
With a desperate effort, Frey recoiled, throwing himself backward off the bed. He hit the floor with a thud, the shock jarring him further awake. The sharp ache in his gums receded, the hunger dulling, but his heart still pounded with fear and confusion.
Jun sat up abruptly, his violet eyes wide with surprise. “Frey? What’s wrong?” he asked, concern lacing his voice. He moved to the edge of the bed, reaching out a hand as if to help him up.
Frey scrambled back. Heart pounding.
“I’m sorry, I…” He mumbled, trying to find the words to say. Something was very wrong. Why had he felt like that? There must have been something in his expression, because Jun’s eyes darkened.
“I see.” He said flatly. “The hunger?” Frey shook his head wildly, trying to calm his racing heart,
“I don’t, I, what? Hunger?” He asked, confused. Jun slid off the bed, and stepped towards him, fully nude. Frey kept his eyes to the ceiling.
“Look, if you need to. You can, alright?” Jun murmured in his ear, wrapping his arms around Frey’s torso and extending his neck to one side. Frey was hyper aware of Jun’s heartbeat. The pulse of blood in his throat. He felt himself react, but before his teeth touched the soft skin of Jun’s neck he flung Jun away.
“What the fuck?!” Jun hit the floor head, and Frey was appalled. He hadn’t meant to move him so hard, what was this strength, this speed? He backed up to the wall in terror.
“What am I?” His voice cracked at the words, and Jun paused, rubbing his thigh where he’d banged it. Genuine concern on his face.
“What do you mean?” He asked, “Frey… Are you okay?” Frey sank to the floor,
“What am I?” He repeated, barely a whisper this time.
Frey’s heart raced as he backed up, the cool wall pressing into his bare skin, grounding him as he tried to make sense of what was happening. This realm’s Jun sat opposite him now, a safe distance away, his expression calm but edged with concern. Draped in a dressing gown, Jun looked at him, really looked, and Frey couldn’t help but take in the differences—the scar that cut across his cheekbone, the confidence that radiated from his posture, the lines that marked his face with experience and resilience. He seemed older than the Jun Frey knew, yet somehow just as steady, as warm.
Jun cleared his throat, his voice soft but direct. “Frey, you’re a vampire. Do you… not remember that?”
The words sent a jolt through Frey’s body, his mind reeling. A vampire? It explained the sharp teeth, the strange hunger, the unfamiliar strength that had surged through him. He shook his head, trying to steady his breathing. But how could he explain this without sounding insane?
With effort, he took a deep breath, forcing himself to look up into Jun’s steady gaze. “I’m… I’m sorry, but I’m not your Frey.” Seeing the confusion flicker across Jun’s face, he hesitated, then began explaining everything—the strange barrier, the crossing of realms, the shared consciousness he’d discovered, and his search for his own Jun.
Jun listened without interrupting, nodding along as he took it all in. When Frey finished, Jun looked thoughtful, as if carefully considering the situation. “Alright,” he said finally, his tone calm. “Seems straightforward enough. I’ll just… reach in, like the other Jun did, see if I can find your Jun.” His confidence, his ease with the situation, was unexpectedly reassuring.
Frey let out a sigh of relief. He believes me, he thought, the tension easing from his shoulders. But just as quickly, he noticed Jun studying him, a small, unreadable smile on his lips.
“However,” Jun added, leaning forward slightly, “you probably don’t want to try the same thing with my Frey. He’s… not one for sharing.”
Frey’s eyes widened, and he nodded quickly, though the warning lodged firmly in his mind, impossible to shake. But as soon as he tried not to think about it—like not imagining a pink yeti—the thought dug in deeper. Almost as if sensing this, something stirred in his mind, a shadow, a voice.
Well, well, it purred, deep and sultry, threading through his thoughts with a dangerous edge. What do we have here?
Frey jolted, his stomach twisting. I’m not staying long, he projected, trying to keep his thoughts steady. I’m only here for my Jun. Once I find him, I’ll give your body back.
Why hurry? the voice replied, deceptively gentle, as if speaking to an old friend. Stay a while. We could have some… fun. Frey’s breath hitched as he felt phantom sensations, ghostly fingers stroking along his leg, soft but electric. His skin prickled, and he shivered, trying to shake off the intruding presence.
Jun noticed, his expression tightening slightly. “Ah,” he said with understanding, a wry smile curving his lips. “Well, I’ll try to find your Jun quickly, then.” He closed his eyes, settling into a meditative posture as he began searching inward.
But the strokes along Frey’s leg grew bolder, reaching up his thigh, a dark chuckle vibrating in his head. Frey shot to his feet, desperate to shake off the sensation, his pulse pounding.
Careful, the voice crooned, amused. You don’t know what you’re missing.
Frey clenched his fists, his heart pounding in a mix of embarrassment and anger. Look, I don’t know what you think you’re doing, but I’m here for one reason, and one reason only, he projected, his voice firm in his mind. So stop messing with me.
The voice only laughed softly, a rich, dark sound. Oh, I’m not messing with you. Just enjoying my own body—and who’s to say I don’t get a say in how long you stay? It was unnerving, this smooth, unapologetic darkness that seemed so at ease within him, like an echo of himself that had grown in ways he couldn’t imagine.
Frey felt the walls closing in, the surreal situation pulling him deeper into a strange, shared intimacy with a version of himself he hardly recognized. Focus, he told himself, taking a shaky breath. Focus on finding Jun. That’s all that matters.
Just as he tried to steel his resolve, Jun’s eyes fluttered open, his gaze meeting Frey’s with a mix of sympathy, and sadness. “I’m sorry. He’s not here” .
Frey brushed a shaky hand through his hair, feeling sweat beading on his forehead.
“Okay.” He said, “Thanks.” He desperately tried to ignore what the phantom hand was touching. Teasing. He needed to leave. Frey’s heart hammered in his chest as he tried to find his escape, desperately blocking out the sensations that the other Frey—the vampire—was imposing on him. “G-goodbye,” he stammered, squeezing his eyes shut, mentally searching for any kind of door, a way to leave this borrowed body. The twisted thoughts, the cruel hands that taunted him—it was all too much. He could feel the vampire’s mockery, his disturbing pleasure in Frey’s discomfort.
Oh no, little Frey, came the vampire’s taunting voice, smooth as silk and sharp as a blade. You can’t leave yet.
In his mind’s eye, Frey saw him—a dark, twisted reflection of himself. This Frey was pale, ethereal, with piercing, cruel eyes and a chilling smile that revealed elongated fangs. He was beautiful, but in the terrifying, deadly way that a lightning storm was beautiful—sharp, dangerous, and utterly uncontainable.
Frey’s pulse quickened, and he steeled himself. I’m going. You can’t stop me, he said resolutely.
In an instant, the vampire was there, pressing against him, invading his space. His arm coiled around Frey, holding him firmly in place, their hips brushing as he leaned in, his fingers tangling painfully in Frey’s hair.
Of course I can, the vampire purred, his tone laced with dark amusement. He pulled Frey’s head back, exposing his neck, and Frey’s heart raced as he felt the sharp, ominous pressure of twin fangs grazing his skin.
This isn’t happening. This can’t happen, Frey chanted inwardly, trying to block it out. But he felt the bite, the awful sensation of sharp teeth piercing his flesh, the sickening pull as the vampire drank from him. Even though it was in his mind, the sensation was disturbingly real, as if he were trapped in a twisted, waking nightmare. He squirmed, desperate to break free, terror clawing at him.
Please, he begged.
A sharp, stinging slap snapped him out of it, his head whipping to the side. He opened his eyes, disoriented, to see Jun standing over him, his brow furrowed and his violet eyes blazing with intensity. His hand was still raised, ready to slap him again if needed.
“Frey,” Jun’s voice was steady, firm, slicing through the fog clouding Frey’s mind. “Let him go.”
A mocking, melodic laugh escaped Frey’s lips—not his own voice, but the vampire’s, smooth and taunting. “Oh, but this is new and fun!” he heard himself say, the sound laced with cruel amusement. He barely recognized himself, but he was powerless, watching from within as the vampire spoke through him.
Jun’s eyes narrowed. “Then I’m leaving,” he said, his tone cold. He stood up, grabbed a key from the table, and turned toward the door, clearly prepared to walk away from this twisted version of Frey.
With an unnatural speed, Frey’s body—under the vampire’s control—leaped to block his path, reaching the door before Jun could. “Oh, Jun, don’t be a spoilsport,” the vampire crooned, trailing a hand down Jun’s cheek, a dark glint in his eyes. “We could make it a party.”
Jun’s expression hardened, his scowl deepening. “Maybe I don’t share well,” he replied, and with a swift motion, ducked under Frey’s arm, slipping out of reach.
The vampire let out a frustrated sigh, the shadow of his presence retreating in their shared mental space. Frey felt his consciousness uncoil, slipping back into control as the vampire grudgingly relinquished his hold. Fine then. Leave, the vampire sneered, his voice curling in disdain.
Barely containing his relief, Frey seized his chance, focusing all his energy on the door in his mind. Without hesitation, he threw himself toward it, feeling himself slip through, his heart pounding with freedom as he left the vampire’s grip behind.

Chapter Six
Frey gasped as he came to consciousness, his heart racing, adrenaline still coursing through him from the encounter he’d just escaped. He focused on his breathing, trying to calm himself as he took in his new surroundings. Stone walls surrounded him, with four pillars framing a grand bed, draped in soft cushions and feather bedding. This room, though more luxurious than most inns he had stayed in, felt comfortably familiar—like a high-end room in Keoland, warm and elegant.
Frey realised he was gripping the sheets tightly and forced himself to relax, unfurling his fingers from the fabric. He was alone. Safe, for now. He let himself sit with the quiet, piecing together what he’d just been through.
Two worlds. Each with its own Jun. And the last… Vampire Frey, he thought with a shudder, a manifestation of his darker impulses—resentment, anger, abandonment—all buried deep within him. Is that really a part of me? he wondered. The idea that that version of him could still have a relationship with Jun unnerved him, as if it meant that even the worst parts of him still longed for connection, still reached out to someone who understood him. He didn’t know what that world was like, but he suspected it was harsher and colder than his own, a place where that vampire Frey had learned to wield his darkness with precision.
Frey took a steadying breath, feeling an unexpected pang of loneliness. He needed to find his Jun and get back to his own world, back to the life he recognized.
After a few minutes, he composed himself and got to his feet, surveying the room. Everything was finely crafted—the linen shirt he wore was simple but of high quality, paired with drawstring pants and leather boots. The furniture was solid, finely polished, and luxurious, including a large bureau with parchment and ink, a dark wooden table with ornately carved chairs, and a floor-length mirror standing in the corner. This world’s technology was like his own, but elevated in taste and refinement.
Something golden glinted in the corner of his eye. On the ottoman at the foot of the bed lay a crown, adorned with gems, tossed haphazardly onto the cushion. Frey picked it up, turning it over in his hands. Curious, he stepped to the mirror, setting the crown gently atop his head. It fit perfectly. Grooves were etched into the metal, carefully shaped to accommodate his horns, which he now noticed were carved with intricate floral designs and vines, their tips dipped in real gold.
Just then, a knock at the door startled him. Frey turned toward the large, heavy wooden door, clearing his throat before calling out, “Come in!”
The door opened to reveal an elderly elf woman bearing a silver tray, piled high with fresh vegetables, bread, and cheeses. She moved with quiet efficiency, avoiding eye contact as she crossed the room and set the tray on the table.
“Your breakfast, sire,” she said with a slight bow, her voice formal and reserved.
Frey gave her a warm smile. “Thanks!”
The elf looked momentarily startled by his response, glancing at him as though seeing him for the first time. She gave a deeper bow, murmuring, “At your leave,” before hurrying from the room.
Frey chuckled softly, a quiet huh escaping his lips. He approached the table, and as the scent of fresh strawberries reached him, his stomach let out a loud growl of hunger. Grinning, he dug into the food, savouring each bite of ripe fruit, crusty bread, and creamy cheese. The platter was decadent, and Frey couldn’t help but think, I could get used to this!
As he ate, his mind drifted, curiosity stirring about this version of himself. A crown, servants, all this luxury… Who was he in this world? And what would this Jun be like? He’d had plenty of surprises already, but he couldn’t help the flicker of excitement in his chest. Maybe this world was the one. He considered trying to reach the Frey of this world, but a shudder passed through him, he wasn’t quite ready for that yet.
Frey was midway through spreading a generous amount of cheese onto a piece of soft bread when another knock sounded at the door. He opened his mouth to respond, but before he could say a word, the door swung open, and Jun swept into the room in an obvious huff.
Frey, caught off guard, nearly choked on his bread. Jun? Here? He coughed, struggling to swallow as Jun fixed him with a fierce, unimpressed glare.
“What are you doing?” Jun scolded, his voice edged with exasperation. “Court started ten minutes ago, and you were supposed to be there!”
Still coughing, Frey needed a few moments to catch his breath. When he finally did, he couldn’t help but grin at the sight of Jun—dressed in the most ostentatious robe he’d ever seen. “What in the Gods are you wearing?” he laughed, his eyes widening in delight.
Jun’s gaze turned stormy, and his cheeks darkened to a deeper shade of cobalt, his embarrassment plain as he looked down at his outfit. The heavy crimson robe with black trim swept down to his ankles and matching red leather shoes, clearly tailored for status rather than style—and it clashed horribly with his blue skin.
“What am I wearing?” Jun’s voice pitched in disbelief, and Frey was secretly delighted by the reaction. This, this flustered indignation, felt so much like the Jun he knew. “I’m your court sorcerer, remember? You picked this outfit, you dick!”
Jun crossed his arms, looking even more put out, and Frey’s laughter doubled, the tension from earlier melting away. Seeing Jun like this, familiar and fiery, was an unexpected relief.
Jun huffed and, after a pause, strode to the ottoman, yanking out a bundle of ornate, imperial-looking fabrics. He tossed them in Frey’s direction with a scowl.
“Now hurry up!” he said, his tone veering into a whine. “I hate having to handle the villagers’ petty arguments by myself. If I have to listen to one more complaint about the price of manure alone, I swear I’ll fireball the whole kingdom.”
Frey looked down at the fabric in his hands. It was as elaborate as everything else in the room, richly embroidered with intricate designs that matched the lavish decor around him. A court outfit, he realised, suddenly aware of the weight of the title that came with it.
Still grinning, he looked up at Jun, who was impatiently tapping his foot, clearly waiting for him to get dressed. Frey held up the garment, eyeing the extravagant details. “So… I’m a ruler here, then?” he asked, unable to mask the curiosity in his voice.
Jun’s expression softened, though only slightly. “Ruler, king, tyrant, take your pick,” he said with a smirk. “Now stop stalling. We have a court session to survive.”
Frey pondered whether he should own up now, but then figured it might be fun to play at King for the day. He dressed quickly, feeling the heavy fabrics settle on him in a comforting manner.
“Alright,” he said, adjusting the crown on his head. “Let’s go deal with manure and keep the fireballs at bay.”
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
As they walked side by side through the palace corridors, Frey couldn’t help but mull over the ordeal he’d just endured in the courtroom. After two gruelling hours of addressing complaints that ranged from unrealistic marriage demands to appallingly naïve financial decisions, he felt drained. What was I thinking?! he groaned inwardly. How did his other self handle this? And worse, how many times had he sent Jun out like a magical handyman to deal with every minor inconvenience in the kingdom?
Magic, it seemed, was a rare gift in this world—something only a few wielded. He’d picked up on that from the villagers’ insistence on sending out his wizard for every little problem, which only made him more irritated on Jun’s behalf. Jun, for his part, had merely rolled his eyes and seemed bored by the spectacle, confirming for Frey that this was a regular occurrence.
Once the session finally ended, Frey sighed in relief, his legs heavy as he made his way back to the bedroom. He idly wondered if the maid from earlier might bring more strawberries—he could use a reward after all that.
“Well, that was… different,” Jun remarked, breaking the comfortable silence as he strolled beside him.
Frey shot him a sidelong glance. “What do you mean by that?” He reached up, tempted to remove the heavy crown; the ache in his neck was only growing.
Jun arched a brow, a knowing smile tugging at the corners of his mouth. “You’re normally a bit more… diplomatic,” he said carefully, amusement flickering in his eyes.
Frey cringed, feeling a twinge of self-consciousness. “Maybe I just didn’t feel like it today,” he muttered, trying to shrug it off, though part of him thought he’d done a decent job of it all.
Jun let out a laugh, a warm, rolling sound that softened his usually guarded expression. “Keep it up, and we might be done in half the time tomorrow. Maybe we could actually go out and do something fun for a change.” He twirled a spark of magic around his fingers, weaving it across his knuckles with practised ease.
Frey watched, captivated by the way Jun handled the magic with such confidence. There was a comfort, a natural ease in the way Jun wielded his magic here that Frey hadn’t seen in his own Jun. Seeing it sparked a pang of longing in his chest. He searched within himself, trying again to find his own magic, but there was nothing. The spark that should have been nestled in his core simply wasn’t there. Perhaps, he thought, only one Frey in the universe gets magic.
This realisation brought him back to the purpose of his journey. He took a deep breath, gathering his courage. “Hmm, about that. Can we talk?” he asked.
Jun’s carefree expression faded, replaced with concern as he turned to him. “Is something wrong?”
Frey’s fingers clinked against the crown as he scratched his head, feeling suddenly nervous. “Nothing’s wrong!” he said quickly, hoping to dispel any worry. “I just… need to talk to you about something. Can we go back to my room?”
Jun paused, the spark of magic vanishing from his hand as he studied Frey’s face. After a moment, he gave a small nod. “Of course.”
They walked in silence back to the room, Jun glancing over now and then, concern still lingering in his gaze. Once they were inside, Frey felt the weight of the crown more keenly than ever and set it aside on the bed, letting out a sigh of relief.
Jun leaned against the table, crossing his arms, his expression soft but focused. “Alright, what’s up?” he asked, his tone gentler now.
Frey took a deep breath, steadying himself before meeting Jun’s gaze. “I’m… not the Frey you know,” he began, choosing his words carefully. “I come from a different realm, and I’m here searching for… my Jun.” He hesitated, gauging Jun’s reaction. “The Jun I know was lost in a different world. I followed him, trying to bring him home.”
Jun blinked, his cobalt eyes narrowing in thought as his expression shifted from confusion to cautious understanding. “You’re… from another realm?” he asked slowly, his tone curious rather than accusatory.
Relieved that Jun was at least listening, Frey nodded and explained everything—how he’d ended up here, the strange doors, the encounters with other versions of himself and Jun, and his increasingly desperate attempt to find his way back to his own world. He didn’t leave anything out.
When he finished, Frey sat back, watching Jun closely. The sorcerer hadn’t interrupted once, letting Frey tell his story fully. Jun’s face was thoughtful, his eyes distant as he processed the information. After a long minute, he finally spoke.
“How many doors did you say there were?” He asked, his voice calm.
Frey felt a flicker of relief at being believed, then thought for a moment. “I’m not sure,” he admitted. “As far as I could see… A few thousand?”
Jun nodded, rising to sit at the table. He grabbed a piece of parchment and a quill, beginning to scribble something down in a flowing runic script that Frey didn’t recognize. Frey raised an eyebrow.
“So,” Jun said, without looking up from his writing, “your plan was to just… venture through every single door and hope for the best?”
Frey frowned, defensive. “Well, yeah. I figured I’d find Jun eventually!”
Jun sighed, the corner of his mouth twitching upward in a hint of amusement. “I’m sorry to say that your Jun isn’t here with me. But, you said you have four days,” he pointed out, “and based on what you’ve told me, each visit can last anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. Let’s say, for the sake of argument, an average of two and a half hours per visit.” He continued scrawling as he spoke. “If you were to check every single door, it would take you one hundred and four days. Without sleeping.”
Jun looked up at Frey, one eyebrow raised. “Your plan is stupid.”
Frey bristled, crossing his arms. “Well, what was I supposed to do? I had to try!”
Jun rolled his eyes, but there was a tenderness in his expression—a small smile that radiated familiarity and affection. It caught Frey off guard, and a blush crept up his neck. He hadn’t asked about the relationship between this world’s Frey and Jun, but that smile told him everything he needed to know.
Jun sighed, shaking his head fondly. “What am I going to do with you?” He pushed back from the chair and walked over to Frey, stopping just in front of him. Frey blinked as Jun reached out, placing a hand gently on his chest.
Startled, Frey’s breath caught in his throat. “What are you—?”
“Shh,” Jun murmured, his focus intense. The warmth of his hand seeped through Frey’s shirt, and a faint tingle spread beneath his skin. Frey became acutely aware of his heartbeat, rapid and strong, and the way Jun’s face was so close to his own, his violet eyes narrowed in concentration.
Then Frey felt it—a faint tug, a subtle hum of magic just beneath the surface of his awareness.
“What’s that?” he whispered, awe creeping into his voice.
Jun pulled back, his hand dropping, and gave Frey a confident smile. “You and I are connected,” he said simply. “I wasn’t sure if it was just this world, but it seems it’s more than that.” His smile softened, becoming something warmer, almost reverent. “In every world, you and I are connected. I’d hesitate to call it soulmates—it’s something deeper.”
Frey glanced down at his chest, and for a moment, he thought he saw it too—a thin, golden thread, gossamer and shimmering, extending out from his heart. It pulsed faintly, reaching toward Jun like a living thing.
“We’re connected?” he asked, his voice hushed.
Jun reached up and patted his cheek gently, his touch grounding. “Yes. And I think you can use this connection to find your Jun. I’ve felt it—your thread is similar to my Frey’s, but there’s a subtle difference. If you concentrate, you should be able to feel it too. It might take a couple of tries, but eventually, it’ll guide you to the right door.”

Jun half-jogged down the tunnel, anxiety coiled tight in his bones.

Star knew. That was the thing that kept snagging at him, a burr he couldn't shake loose. Star had known what might be waiting in these mines — fire giants, or worse — and he'd gone anyway. Run ahead with that long-legged goliath stride, impatient and restless and utterly certain the others would catch up, because they always did. He'd taken Brian Styles with him. Brian Styles, who was a duck, who had no say in the matter and no capacity to protect himself, tucked under the arm of someone who'd already decided his own momentum mattered more than the team's.

Star had left them.

Jun understood, intellectually, that Star wasn't cruel. He was just — like this. Antsy. Forward-moving. Probably already rounding the next bend, feathers ruffled, wondering irritably what was taking them so long. And despite knowing full well that Star had gotten himself into this, Jun would go. He was already going. They were stronger together; that was just fact, simple as arithmetic, and Jun couldn't unknot himself from that truth even when he wanted to.

So why wasn't Frey running?

"Come on, Frey." He heard the whine in his own voice and couldn't help it. Every second they spent ambling was a second Star and Brian Styles spent alone in the dark with whatever was lurking in these tunnels. "Come on, please—"

But Frey sauntered. That was the only word for it. He had apparently made some ironclad vow never to run into a mine, and he was honouring it with the serenity of a man on a Sunday walk. Jun wanted to grab him by the collar. He wanted to explain, calmly, that this was not the moment for a principled stance about running.

He was being weird. Frey was being weird. Jun filed that away and tried to force himself to breathe.

They're fine. They're strong. When it actually matters, they don't go headlong into danger.

He slowed his steps to match Frey's. Told himself he overworried. Told himself Star was probably fine, probably bored, probably wondering where they were with his big arms folded and one eyebrow raised.

Then the arcane thread snapped.

Jun recoiled as though he'd been struck. The polymorph had been running quietly in the back of his mind the whole time — a gentle, constant reassurance, like a hand on his shoulder. Brian Styles is here. Brian Styles is safe. He hadn't even fully registered how much he'd been leaning on it until it was gone. Not released. Not gently dissolved. Cut. Something had hit Brian Styles hard enough to kill a duck.

Ducks were not, admittedly, the sturdiest of creatures. But still.

"Polymorph dropped." His voice came out higher than he intended. "Something hurt Brian Styles — we need to go, now, Frey—"

"Maybe it was a rock," Frey said, and very gradually increased his speed.

Not enough.

Jun's mind ran ahead without him. What if they were already too late. What if Star, enormous and reckless and stupidly brave, was bleeding out on the stone floor right now. What if Brian Styles — Brian Styles who had no say, who had been carried off as a duck — was already dead. They had no healing magic but Frey and Jun. Goddamn Star for being reckless.

Goddamn Frey for treating this like a stroll.

Goddamn Jun for what he was about to do.

The nervous energy that had been gnawing at him all tunnel-long condensed into something clean and purposeful.

Jun ran.

Behind him, distant already, he heard Frey call his name.

He didn't stop.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~FREY~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Fizzy often used this time to tinker with new gadgets, Jun read his trashy romance novels, Star practised storytelling and could often be heard repeating sentences over and over emphasising different words for effect. He was three hours into the five hour shift and the temptation to peek at their ‘very dangerous, incredibly powerful’ cargo was getting to be too much.

Eddie had warned them intensely about the box and what it contained. It's a killer. A monster. Transport it and drop it off. That's all. Don't even think about messing with it.

It was a simple transport job. One where they didn't need to fight anybody or get into any messy business at all, for which the payment was ludicrous. This only served to pique Frey's interest more.

How dangerous could the thing inside be, really?

"Just a peek…?" He warred with himself, Eddie said it was dangerous, but Eddie said everything was dangerous. He wouldn't even play barrel bounce with them. The lizard was probably being overly cautious. Plus, it had been hours and he was going out of his mind. He hated the nav watch.

Side-eying the door to the bridge, which remained closed and silent just like it had the last three hours, Frey rose from his chair and crossed the deck to the table with the box. He bit his lips in anticipation, it was too late to back out, his mind had been made. He was simply too curious. Wiggling his fingers in anticipation he flicked back the little brass clasp and…

Frey faded away.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~JUN~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Thinking furiously, Jun backed away. He was frenzied but his threats were empty, and the creature knew it too... Jun could never willingly hurt Frey. He had to buy time… Quickly, Jun began making the somatic gestures to initiate the spell to restrain a foe. He needed something that could hold Frey in place whilst he sought help.

However, the creature simply laughed in Frey’s voice and faster than Jun could react, he was slammed into the wall. His hands yanked painfully above his head, and held against the metal, tight in a crushing grip that rendered his fingers immobile.

“Ah ah, not this time, spellcaster.” Frey taunted with manic eyes and a wide smile that contorted his face unnaturally. Jun squirmed but continued trying to cast, hissing the verbal components of his spell to subdue the tiefling. He couldn’t finish casting, as the creature wearing his friend’s body lunged forward and captured Jun’s mouth on his own.

Jun was stunned. ‘Not like this!’ he thought, fear overtaking his thoughts as his ability to defend himself was taken away. Without his hands, without his voice, he wasn’t a powerful caster, he was just a person… A person too weak to fight back against the grip on him.

Fear radiated off Jun as the creature occupying Frey’s body shoved his legs between Jun’s, forcing his step wider, pressing him hard against the wall. Jun knew he was panicking, as he desperately tried to break the grip on his fingers, twisting his head wildly to escape the assault on his mouth. It was futile. He wasn’t strong enough. Tears dripped down his face as he screamed into Frey’s mouth.

As their lips stayed locked and Jun's hopeless struggle continued, he saw a single tear rolled down Frey’s cheek. With a moment of horrifying# clarity Jun knew that Frey was watching, powerless himself to stop what was happening. They were both trapped in their own nightmare.

The deep torturous kiss seemed to be never ending and Jun could feel his own efforts to resist dwindling with each successive failure. He clenched his eyes shut and willed it to be over quickly.

Then he heard a loud banging at the door, which reignited his will to struggle.

A booming voice came from the other side of the door, "Look you two! I don't know what you are doing in there. But it doesn't sound good for my ship. And I don't like things that aren't good for the ship." There was a moment of silence followed by some agitated whispering. Then the voice came again. "I will give you until the count of three and you either open the door or I kick the door down."

Jun's heart raced. He'd never been happier for Star's meddling protectiveness over his ship. If anyone could overpower this Frey wannabe it was him. "ONE!" The large bellow rang through the room.

Jun felt the lips that had been pressed so hard against his pull back, but still remaining mere inches away a single strand of saliva still connecting them. Jun's brow furrowed as he looked with a glare of pure detest at the being inhabiting his friend’s body, who was torturing them both.

"TWO!" Star's voice rang again.

"Looks like we have guests." Frey sneered, placing his finger under Jun's chin, forcing him to face him directly. "You'd best be on your best behaviour. Otherwise I might have to make a mess."

"THREE!"

With the final count, Jun felt Frey’s grip between his fingers tighten as the imposter yanked them both backward, tumbling to the floor. Frey's back was to the doorway as the door burst open. This meant Star and Fizzy who were looking concerned above the broken door couldn't see the knife Frey slid from his pocket. But Jun could.

"What is going on here! Are you fighting?!" Star shouted, taking in the two men lying on the floor. Frey smiled viciously down at Jun and poked his own knife into his own chest. The message was clear. He was going to kill Frey.

Choking on saliva and trying not to gag, Jun smiled up at his crew mates.

"Aha… Sorry, we got caught up…" Frey jabbed the knife deeper into chest, piercing through the fabric of his flight suit and into his rose coloured skin. A drop of blood welled and soaked into the white fabric as Jun struggled to find the words, "Wrestling. We're wrestling.."

Star heaved a sigh of relief, "You owe me a door. Keep the noise down. And Jun,you sound like a little crying girl." Then he turned and left.

Jun couldn't help the small noise of terror escaping his mouth. He flinched as Frey sneered above him and pressed the knife deeper.

Fizzy hesitated in the doorway, worry etched on her face. "Your eyes are red, Jun, are you okay?" He gulped and nodded. Frey snarled,turning to look at Fizzy over his shoulder.

"Jun likes it when we get rough. You wanna fucking leave? Or stay and watch the show?" He bent down and kissed Jun roughly on the mouth.

"Ugh," Fizzy tutted and left, taking Jun's hopes with her.

Frey leered down at Jun when he heard the footsteps fade away. Shifting the knife up towards his neck, he leant in close and bit sharply on Jun's jaw.

"Now, where were we?"

He moved along Jun's jawline and up his cheek making tiny sharp bites; Jun winced with every touch. When he finally reached Jun's lips Frey bit down hard into his bottom lip. Jun felt the sharp teeth piece his skin; the taste of copper filled his mouth as blood began to well. Jun let out a muffled cry.

Happy with the fact that as long as there was a dagger to Frey’s neck Jun would refrain from resisting; the entity pulled back, chuckling with an unsettling malevolent look in his eyes.

"What shall we do next…Hmm?" He asked as he brought his thumb to the mark he had left, pressed hard and began to spread Jun's blood across his lips. "Killing you will be fun, but I want to make it last, you're too delicious." Finishing the full circuit of Jun's lips Frey leaned back slightly tilting his head to regard his work. Clearly pleased with himself, he placed the blood soaked finger in his mouth and sucked it clean. Jun grimaced at the way Frey's eyes were scanning over him as he did it.

As the sensation of Jun's blood spread across his tongue, the real Frey reeled in disgust. “Stop it. Stop it! Stop it!!” But he knew he was powerless to do anything. The longer this thing was controlling him the more he could feel its thoughts mingling with his own. His consciousness pushed to the back, further away from control.

As he watched his own hand caress Jun’s chest, slowly edging towards Jun’s quivering neck.

Freys horror grew as the intrusive thoughts sparked loudly again. Violent thoughts. He didn’t want to be forced to see his own body to commit such unspeakable acts, to see his own hands hurt the person he cared for most, but he had no control. He couldn't shut his eyes or look away. The realisation that he was causing Jun’s pain, that his body was being used as a weapon to control and Jun, filled him with a gut wrenching sense of dread and self-loathing. This was all his fault. His curiosity had gotten the better of him, and now Jun was hurting for it.

“Please, please stop! Don’t hurt him anymore.” Frey begged in his mind, “I’ll do whatever you want, just please, stop hurting him.” From deep within himself Frey heard the voice gleefully echoing through the darkest parts of his skull. “Why would I ever do that? You're both so much fun.” With that Frey felt his fingers tighten around Jun's neck pushing him into the ground. The movement caused the blade against Frey’s neck to cut into his skin, leaving a small nick that ran red. Several droplets dripped onto Jun's tear-soaked face as the dark entity rose above him.

"Please…" Jun whispered, "just let him go." If Frey had control of his body, he would have recoiled. He's not thinking of himself. He's not defending himself! Jun please, please do something. Hurt me, kill me, don't let this happen.

However, all that Jun heard was Frey's voice darkly laughing at him. The hand around Jun's neck squeezed and Jun gasped. His survival instincts kicked in as his air supply cut off and he thrashed under Frey's body driving the knife tip deeper into Frey's skin. The drops of blood flowed quicker onto the elf, mixing with Jun's own, painting a gory tableau on his face.

Truly panicking now, gasping for air, Jun's hands rose to his neck, trying desperately to claw Frey's off, but his strength was waning.

“Stop it! You're killing him!” Frey screamed and begged. He couldn't do anything but watch in horror as the fight faded from Jun. His arms dropped limply to the floor as his eyes lost focus.

But still the entity in Frey held on. It waited until the resistance from Jun ceased completely before rising to his feet, standing tall over the broken sorcerer.

"Might have got carried away there. I never learn not to be too rough with my toys. Now, I need to do something about that door…”

In the mess, Fizzy sat at the carbon table and poked angrily at the gizmo in front of her with her screwdriver. Across the room Star the culinary whirlwind danced around in the kitchen, throwing various chopped vegetables into a steaming pot. He considered a green plant that had been growing in the far back of the refrigeration unit, gave it a cautious sniff then tossed it into the pot as well.

“Ugh!” Fizzy blurted, tossing the gadget aside. “What the fuck is up with those two?!”

“Which two?” Brian Styles asked as he entered the room. He assessed the people within, “Frey and Jun? I assume? There’s a great deal ‘up’ with them.” He took a seat at the table and retrieved the discarded gizmo and eyed it with interest.

“She’s talking about the fact they finally fuckin’.” Star leered, “Seems like Fizzy's a bit jealous." She gave him a disgusted look.

“Go fuck yourself Star.” But she paused, contemplating, “I know they’ve been giving each other moon eyes for months, but something didn’t seem right. Jun looked, I don’t know… Scared?”

Star laughed, “Little baby man is scared of his own shadow! Maybe Frey's got a wild side. Fear could be the price of admission.” He stopped, cogs whirring almost audibly in his brain. “Wait, if Frey’s bumping uglies. Who’s watching the navcomm?”

Rolling her eyes with an air of exasperation, Fizzy shook her head. "Seriously, Star? That's your prime concern right now? What if something's wrong with them? Frey was mean to me..."

“He’s always mean! If you’re so bothered you go and interrupt them again. Don’t blame me if you get squirted on though.”

Brian Styles, sensing the opportunity for action and possibly an escape from the conversation, rose from his seat, "I'll keep watch on the Bridge," he said, and left.

Fizzy huffed and picked up her gizmo again. “So disgusting, Star,” she muttered under her breath as Star studied the concoction in his pot and wondered whether it was meant to be purple…

Jun's head lolled as his consciousness slowly crept back. His sight was blurred, he felt nauseous, and his head pounded worse than any hangover he had ever experienced. He tried to reach up to steady himself but found he couldn't move his arm. Panic surged as he attempted to take a deep breath, only to find his lungs starved for air. His heart raced, and his mind raced even faster. Fear gripped him as he realised he had been bound and gagged. His hands and wrists were tied behind his back crushing his fingers and restricting his movements. He couldn’t cast spells like this. He was trapped, unable to move or even cry out. The weight of the situation pressed down, and a rush of helplessness consumed him.

As his vision gradually began to clear; his surroundings were still hazy. He could tell he was still in his quarters at least. Out of the corner of his eye he could make out an indistinct figure by his sink. That must be Frey, but he couldn’t be sure, he looked different. Jun started to strain against his bindings, his determination to break free renewed. The muffled sounds of his own breathing and the racing of his heart echoed in his ears, a constant reminder of the perilous situation he found himself in. Hearing Jun’s movement, the blurred presence turned and approached him.

“You’re finally awake!” The figure clapped their hands together with glee. “I’m so glad I didn’t break you for good. Now we can play some more.”

As Frey stepped into Jun’s field of view and his appearance became clearer, Jun knew for certain that this was not the tiefling he knew and loved. Gone was the air of innocence and vibrancy that often-surrounded Frey. In its place was an aura of intensity, an unfamiliar edge that seemed to radiate from his very presence. The Frey that stood in front of him now was the opposite of the Frey he knew. Instead of his customary pastels and oversized flight suit, he now sported Jun’s black bootcut trousers that accentuated his legs. A short leather jacket hung open on his frame, revealing a bare chest underneath. His typically unruly white hair was slicked back, giving him a more polished and intense appearance.

Seeing Jun regard him warily, a smile spread across Frey's face. “Hope you don’t mind, I borrowed some clothes. They're a bit short.” He stated, pointing down to where the bottom of the trousers only just met the tops of his boots. “But I think I pull it off.” he gave Jun a small twirl “What do you think?”

Unable to respond verbally, Jun glared daggers and tried once again to loosen his bonds. Frey's demeanour shifted, a wicked pout taking over his expression. "Oh, you're being so mean, playing hard to get," he commented with a twisted grin. "And after I made myself look so nice for you, and I fixed the door." Jun's gaze followed Frey's gesture, his wardrobe now blocking the doorway, leaving him trapped within the room.

"Now we won't have any more rude interruptions," Frey declared. His smile carried a sinister edge.

He closed the distance between them and got down onto the floor, straddling Jun and letting his full weight press down on his legs. Jun tried to shift away but there was nowhere to go as his back pressed up against the wall behind him. Reaching out towards Jun, Frey began to trace his fingers along the bruising on Jun’s neck with a threatening pressure. Even with the intense stare of his assailant, Jun couldn’t help his eyes drifting down to Frey’s bare chest boldly exposed between the lapels of his open jacket.

Now that he was only a breath’s distance away from him Jun could see clearly the white faded scars that he knew were scattered across Frey’s torso, like cracks in pink porcelain. It had taken Frey months to feel comfortable enough to show his scars, and trust Jun with the story behind them, of a life that was left far behind and a painful past he’d rather forget.

How dare this imposter flaunt them as if they were nothing? Jun was incensed. It intensified his resolve to break free and confront the imposter who dared to trample over what they had shared.

Frey's eyes locked onto Jun's gaze as he noticed him regarding the scars on his chest. His sinister smirk deepened and a malicious glint danced in his eyes. He could see the anger radiating from Jun, and he revelled in it.

“Oh Jun.” He taunted, “Why would you want to protect something that’s already so broken. This body’s damaged goods!”

Looking down at his own chest, Frey delicately traced his fingers across his scars. "So much suffering written here," he mused, his voice taking on a contemplative tone. "My host must be very familiar with receiving pain…" He let out a soft chuckle. Suddenly, Frey's eyes lit up with a spark of inspiration. Slowly, he raised his fingers to his lips and pressed a lingering kiss against the tips."But you know," he purred, studying his broken finger as if deep in thought, "Pain can be such an intimate thing. A connection between two people that goes beyond the surface."

Suddenly, Frey flicked his eyes up, looking past his hand and back at Jun.

"Why don't I make us match?"

His hand shot out to grab Jun's shirt, fingers twisting around the fabric, his touch almost bruising as he yanked at the material. With his other hand, he withdrew his knife from his belt and the blade glinted as it slid underneath Jun's shirt, a menacing gleam dancing across its edge. With a swift, precise motion, he sliced the fabric apart, leaving a clean and deliberate divide in its wake.

The cut fabric revealed Jun's bare chest, and Frey fought to suppress an excited shiver.

Violet eyes stared at Frey with defiance. The tears that streaked Jun’s cheeks earlier had now dried, giving way to a smouldering anger. The creature in Frey’s body licked his lips in anticipation as his fingers twitched on the knife handle. The anticipation of twisting that anger back into pain and terror was intoxicating. Slowly, he pressed the tip of the blade against Jun’s sternum. There was a slight flinch as the metal bit into the skin. He withdrew slightly to see the crimson bubble and well where the blade had touched. Gleeful now, Frey pressed down again, harder. Beneath the gag Jun couldn’t hold back from groaning in pain. It only fuelled the creature’s excitement and his eyes were wild with excitement. He slid the blade in deeper, agonisingly slow, with each gasp and twitch the steel went in further…one, two, three, four, five… Jun’s eyes clenched shut and he turned his head away, unwilling to look at the metal embedded in his skin. Sweat dripped down his face as he clenched his teeth at the slow and careful assault. Frey twisted the angle of the blade and drew it sharply across the right, carving a bloody stripe across Jun’s chest.

“Look at you…” Frey murmured, rocking back on the balls of his feet. The strip of skin on Jun’s chest bled heavily, dripping down his torso and soaking into his pants and the floor. He pressed his hand into the blood, caressing Jun’s saturated abdomen.

Frey smiled, licked the tip of one his fingers and then dragged his bloodied hand across Jun’s face, smearing his skin and hair. “Beautiful…” He whispered. “I really wish you didn’t have such a dangerous mouth, I’d love to hear you scream.” He took his bloodied hand and grabbed Jun by the chin, forcing him to look at Frey. Jun, panting beneath the gag, glared silently, willing, begging with his eyes, please Frey, please come back to me.

With its gaze still fixed intently on Jun, the entity let the blunt edge of the dagger rest on Juns' collarbone. Taking delight as it watched Jun’s eyes dilate with fear at every slight movement. Slowly it began to trace across the bone leaving a thick red smear across his clavicle.

"Where next?" Frey mused.

He lightly traced the blade over Jun's chest, not cutting his skin but close enough so that Jun felt it's cold tip hovering over him. Without warning

Frey unleashed a flurry of strikes, his dagger slashing into Jun's flesh again and again. Blood bloomed from the gashes painting a gruesome picture.

Jun bit down hard into the gag trying to suppress the pain as his skin screamed in agony. He could feel his warm blood trickle out of every burning cut. He'd lost a lot of blood and he was starting to feel light headed as his vision began to darken around the edges, Jun began to find it difficult to keep his head upright.

As if sensing his weakness the being edge towards Jun allowing their torsos pressed together, supporting Jun's weight and bathing Frey’s front in a crimson wash.

"Ooh are you getting tired already." It moaned "such a shame, I have so many other games we could play."

Frey's fingers threaded through Jun's hair, crimson streaks marking their passage. Progressing to the back of Jun's head, he seized a handful of hair, pulling it taut; prompting a wince from Jun.

"Maybe it's time to swap places." Frey whispered into Jun's ear, his voice carrying a sinister undertone. "It's not really fair if Frey doesn't get to bleed too."

The sinister resonance of Frey's laughter reverberated through the dimly lit room, intensifying the gravity of the situation. Jun's senses, once dulled, now surged back to life with a fierce urgency. His struggle against the restraints became a desperate dance, each muscle protesting against the cruel confinement.

Frey, seemingly amused by Jun's renewed resistance, continued his taunts with a self-satisfied grin. "Not so tired after all, huh?" he jeered, relishing in the psychological torment. "Or maybe you're just jealous that I want a taste of your man."

Jun's eyes blazed with a mixture of anger and helplessness. The ragged gasps escaping through the gag caused his Adam's apple to bob in an erratic rhythm, a physical manifestation of the emotional turmoil and defiance coursing through him.

Frey eyes glinted as he watched Jun's struggle with delight. Gently, he extended his hand towards Jun's neck, his thumb tracing the rise and fall of Jun's Adam's apple. As Jun’s breath began to steady Frey sharply dug his thumb into Juns throat. Jun gasped as the pressure on his neck increased and his blood ran cold as his airways closed up.

Just as the lights began to burst across Jun's darkening vision, a sudden release of pressure around his throat allowed him to draw ragged, desperate breaths. His ears echoed with Frey's malicious laughter, each tone more haunting than the last, a cruel soundtrack to Jun's struggle for air. The relief was only temporary, a momentary pause in the torment that left Jun both grateful for the breaths he could take and anxious about what would come next. His saving breaths were short lived as Frey once again plunged his thumb into Jun's neck, giggling manically.

As Frey released his grasp once more, he raised the blood soaked dagger; Pausing over Jun's chest. Jun's breath quickened, his pulse echoing in his ears.

The entity's voice dripped with cruelty as it uttered chilling words to Jun. "Try not to wiggle too much. We wouldn't want me to pierce your heart. Then you'd bleed out all over the place, and we wouldn't be able to have any more of our little… fun." Each word hung in the air, a malevolent promise that sent shivers down Jun's spine.

The tip of the blade dug in as Frey started etching an intricate sigil over Jun's heart. The dagger's cruel touch carved into his flesh, each stroke sending waves of excruciating pain through him. There was a grim elegance to the entity's movements, a disturbing grace in its malevolent artistry.

As the sigil neared completion, Jun's body convulsed involuntarily. Muffled cries of agony escaped him, and his eyes pleaded with the entity, a silent plea for mercy. The room echoed with the sounds of his torment.

“What do you think, Fizz? Culinary mastermind, right?” Star grinned from ear to ear as he dropped his spoon into his now-empty bowl of broth. Fizzy gave him a pained smile as she swallowed down the viscous lumpy liquid in her own bowl. While Star’s enthusiasm for cooking for the crew was commendable, his skills left much to be desired.

“It’s… an experience.” She said, putting her diplomacy skills to good use, staring down at the remains of the inexplicably purple broth in her bowl (with seconds still in the pot if she wanted…) and wished she’d skipped out on the meal, just like Frey and Jun…

Surely they couldn’t still be…busy? It definitely wasn’t like Jun to miss a meal, even despite knowing it was Star’s turn to cook. The elf had no gag reflex and would eat anything put in front of him with a genuine smile and gratitude. Should she go and check on them?

Interrupting her thoughts, Brian Styles entered the kitchen, holding the cargo Eddie had commissioned them to deliver.

“Whoa, what are you doing?” Star exclaimed, looking at the box in Brian Styles's hand. “What are you bringing that in here for?! It’s meant to have a bomb in it or some shit.” Then Fizzy noticed something odd.

“Brian Styles, did you open it?” Brian Styles placed the box on the table, where everyone could clearly see that the latch was undone. He shook his head.

“Not me. I just noticed it now.”

As if frozen in time, Star's annoyance gave way to an eerie stillness. Fizzy looked at him in confusion. “What’s wrong?” He moved to open the box despite shouted protests from the other two.

It was empty.

“Fizzy.” Star said in a low voice, heavy with gravity ,“I need you to get on the Comm unit to Eddie. Find out exactly what we were transporting.” His tone was urgent and she nodded in swift acknowledgement, “Brian Styles. Get your hammer and those manacles we picked up from Saltmarsh.” Without a word, Brian complied, questions stifled by the seriousness etched across Star's face. Fizzy gasped as the pieces slid into place.

“You don’t think… Frey?”

Star and Brian Styles exchanged a quick look before nodding in agreement, urgency lending an air of focus to their actions. The realisation that something was dreadfully wrong with Frey propelled them into motion.

The hallways of the ship were eerily quiet as they strode towards Jun's quarters, each step feeling heavy with tension. Brian Styles darted off to the cupboard they used as their makeshift armoury to retrieve a pair of steel manacles they’d picked up the last time they were planetside, just in case. Star was pulling on his powerglove as he strode towards Jun’s room ahead of the group. Cursing himself for dismissing Jun’s earlier expression, for not putting more thought into why Frey wasn’t at his post (the guy was flaky, but he took his job on the ship seriously), and for not listening to Fizzy.

Fizzy followed closely behind, anxiety and worry evident in her expression as she tried to reach Eddie on the Comm unit, with no response.

“Stupid fuckin’ Lizard.” Star growled, worry manifesting as anger. “Why’d he give us a fuckin’ box with a fuckin’ ghost in it.” Fizzy looked at him in alarm and continued dialling Eddie, leaving him messages trying to convey the urgency.

They reached the door to Jun's room and paused for a moment, exchanging another glance, each sharing their concerns without needing to voice them. Then, with a nod, Star reached forward and tried pushing the door open. It didn’t budge. There was something heavy blocking it. Inside, they heard motion, footsteps and laughter.

“Get outta the way!” Star snarled as he shoulder rammed the door. It wasn’t easy, but the object behind the door shifted just enough that it could squeeze inside. Followed closely by Brian Styles and Fizzy.

What they saw made their hearts sink.

Jun sagged on the floor on the back wall, bound and gagged, his shirt was torn open and his front was covered in blood. His head hung down limp, unconscious.

But what drew their attention even more than Jun’s battered form, was Frey – or rather, the being that occupied Frey's body – kneeling over him with a twisted grin on his face, bloodied knife in his hand pressed against Jun’s chest be as he was midway through carving a sigil into the blue-tinted skin.

Star's knuckles whitened as his fists clenched, his gaze narrowing with a mix of anger and concern. Brian Styles tensed, the manacles gripped tightly in his hand. Fizzy's breath caught in her throat, her fingers still clutching the Comm unit.

"Get away from him!" Star's voice was a fierce growl as he advanced into the room, fists raised threateningly.

Frey turned to face them, the same sinister smile lingering on his lips. "Ah, I thought I’d have longer… but no matter, you’re just in time for the show."

Brian Styles moved to flank the entity, his body tense and ready for action. "We're not here for a show," he stated coldly.

The Comm unit in Fizzy’s hand buzzed and she lifted it to her ear. Her voice trembled as she relayed the situation, "Eddie, the thing in the box. We think it did something to Frey. What do we do?!”

Frey's eyes flickered between them with calculating cruelty.. He watched with a sinister satisfaction as Fizzy's hope dwindled with the negative response from the other end of the Comm unit.

"How rude of me, I haven't even introduced myself. I'm the new and improved Frey. Call me... Well, call me Frey actually. I rather like the name." The entity said.

Star's lips curled into a sneer. “Gonna call you dead if you don’t let go of ‘em. Why’d you wanna live in Frey anyway. He got nothing going for ‘im. Not even strong, like me” As he spoke Brian Styles edged closer, as Frey’s eyes snapped across to him, the android moved in. Frey dropped the knife and moved and locked lips with the motionless Jun. With inhuman speed Brian Styles grabbed the tiefling, putting Frey into a headlock and dragging him away from the unconscious elf.

Star jumped in to help restrain Frey as he began thrashing and yelling incoherently, and Fizzy moved forwards to tend to Jun’s wounds.

“Stop! Stop!” Frey screamed, Star clasped one of the manacles around his wrist and cuffed the other end to the sturdy pipe for the heating unit. He and Brian Styles stepped back and watched as Frey thrashed and cried, disturbed by the display coming from their normally composed friend, before he was possessed.

“That was too easy…” Star said, his frustration evident, “Always said Jun should take combat lessons, he’d get overpowered by rabbits.” He stepped up and glared at Frey, “You better get your act together. There’s nothing you can do at this point. Pathetic ghostie.” Brian Styles hummed in concern as Frey’s thrashing slowed down, panting and sobbing he turned to them.

“I’m not a ghost! I’m me! I’m me! Whatever it was! I’m me again! It’s gone!” Star laughed in his face.

“No way. You're gonna wait right there until Eddie tells us how to exercise you or something.”

“Exorcise.” Brian Styles said quietly. Star looked at him perturbed.

“‘S’what I said.” He replied, confused. Frey stared at them in dawning horror.

Meanwhile Fizzy was putting pressure on the wound on Jun’s chest, her hands trembling as they worked. She removed the gag and bindings on his hands,Grimacing at how swollen his fingers were from behind tied so tightly.

“Oh Jun,” She cried, feeling guilty she hadn’t acted on her own concerns. There was too much blood, too many wounds. She didn’t know where to begin first. There was a first-aid kit under Jun's sink, and she rushed to retrieve it, administering as much aid as she could through her tear-blurred vision.

Beneath her ministrations, the blue-skinned elf began to stir, groaning and twitching.

“Jun?” Fizzy called out, gently touching his cheek. “Jun, wake up now, you’re safe.” Grimacing, Jun’s groggily opened his eyes looked at her blearily. “What? Frey?”

Fizzy managed a strained smile through her worry. "We've got Frey. He's tied up. He can't hurt you now." Jun's response was unexpected.

"No, it's not him... it's not—Aaaargh!" Jun cried out in pain, doubling over in agony. Fizzy recoiled, uncertain what to do. Star and Brian Styles were watching them,

“What’d you do??” Star demanded, leaving Frey and striding towards Jun. The elf curled into himself as far as his bonds let him, clearly in agony. He fell to his side, and Star caught him. Star’s eyes were wide.

As Jun continued to suffer, a low, guttural growl emanated from him—a sound he had never made before. "GET OUT!" he roared, his voice filled with anguish. Fizzy flinched and backed away. Behind them, Frey was screaming in horror. “It’s in him! It’s in him!”

The crew stood paralyzed by the horrifying spectacle before them. Jun's body began convulsing, his limbs spasming and contorting in an unnatural dance of suffering. Fizzy, snapping out of her stupor, knew they had to act quickly to prevent Jun from harming himself.

"Hold him down!" she shouted urgently. Brian Styles and Star reacted, rushing to Jun's side and using all their strength to restrain his seizing limbs. Frey, now forgotten in the chaos, remained bound to the post, his terror-stricken eyes locked on the unfolding nightmare.

Then, just as suddenly as it had begun, Jun's thrashing ceased. He lay motionless on his back, his eyes snapping open, but they were no longer the familiar shade of violet. Instead, they had turned obsidian, swirling with mesmerising patterns of colours that seemed to dance within the depths of his gaze. The room felt heavy with an intense pressure, the tangible manifestation of Jun's magic.

"GET. OUT." a deep voice using Jun’s mouth cut through the stillness. With a powerful surge of energy, his body convulsed once more, his head arched back in a twisted rictus, and his mouth opened wide. From within him, a dense cloud of inky black smoke billowed forth, filling the air with an unsettling presence.

Exhaustion wasn't the word. Frey felt tiredness deep in his bones, in his muscles, in every nerve and inch of him screaming to lie down, to close his eyes and stop. He'd only felt this particular kind of tired in one other place.

The other mine.

He scowled and hitched his pack higher on his back. His body was wrecked, but his mind was electric, screaming at him that he was in danger, that he was back, and he had made himself a vow that he would never sleep underground. He didn't know if he could cope waking up to stone ceilings and dark, dusty air. He wasn't sure he could survive that again.

He wanted Eddie. He wanted his mum.

But he was grown now. He was a strong adult. He had lived through horrors, had fought monsters, had won. He hadn't let anything defeat him before, and he wouldn't let this. So he smiled through the tension, fronted like a madman, whooping and cheering as he blew out walls and destroyed machinery. He was walking a knife's edge, and then he'd turned around from killing a dwarf and seen Jun get eaten. Seen him die, and that had tipped his composure clean over the edge.

Now, as they walked and freed the little svirfneblin, unchaining slaves, Frey's eyes were raw. His emotions were raw. He needed to sleep. He couldn't sleep. He wouldn't sleep until he saw sky, until he saw a horizon stretching out ahead of him.

Jun, sweet Jun, noticed. He'd picked up on Frey's tension, which was surprising given that the elf was wound just as tight himself. Only Star seemed to be genuinely enjoying any of this. Brian Styles remained, as always, inscrutable.

"I could - if you wanted," Jun offered, his words halting and careful. "I have my dream cloak. I could cast sleep. You know, if you're struggling to fall asleep."

Frey laughed, short and humourless. He wasn't struggling to fall asleep. He was struggling to stay awake. And he would keep struggling, as long as he could.

Jun let it go. He lay down and closed his eyes.

Frey watched him for a moment, then turned away. There were ways to keep busy. Ways to stop his eyes from drooping... drooping...

He was on his knees. He didn't know when that had happened. There were arms around his shoulders, lowering him down.

"No," he murmured, weakly. His eyes were too heavy to open. Exhaustion had claimed him, his body had simply had enough.

"Shh. Just rest."

And, gods help him, he did.

A boot connected with his side. Soft enough not to hurt, but not gentle by any definition of the word.

"Hey. Enough sleeping. We've got places to be."

Star kicked him again. Frey opened his eyes, bracing himself for the stone ceiling, but instead his vision was filled with Star's big blue face, brows drawn into a scowl. Oddly, it was better.

"Ugh. Personal space," Frey muttered, dragging a hand across his face.

He was still in the mine. But the tension, the misery, the dim lamplight was gone. Jun had cast dancing lights, and the round space they'd found hummed with brightness. A huddle of delighted gnomes had set up a makeshift table and were squabbling cheerfully over a cache of faintly bioluminescent mushrooms. Jun sat among them, the corners of his mouth glowing softly where he'd clearly been eating some. Nearby, the gnomes were enthusiastically offering mushrooms to Brian Styles, apparently undeterred by the fact that the warforged could not physically eat..

The atmosphere was warm.

Frey didn't feel completely restored, but the bone-deep exhaustion had lifted somewhat. His eyes were still gritty, his muscles slow to wake, but he felt the familiar thrill of magic humming in his core. Replenished. He was going to be okay.

He wiped the sleep from his eyes and stood. Star stepped back and gave him a look.

"Good. Time to go." A beat. "Don't eat the mushrooms. They taste like ass." He glanced over at their glowing elf. "...Unless you're into that."

Frey picked up his pack and moved past the goliath without a word. But something had loosened in his chest. He'd known, somewhere, that resisting sleep had been irrational, and now, lighter for having slept, the mine felt slightly more manageable. Still awful. Still wrong. But manageable.

And he had his fireball back.

They didn't take long to pack up, and then they were moving again, the svirfneblin leading them through tunnels toward their village. Long passages with branching paths every few miles, then fewer, then further apart still. The group's banter filled the silence, daft speculation, light-hearted bullying, and it settled something in Frey that he hadn't realised needed settling.

Brian Styles led the way, which should have been absurd given he was the only one among them who couldn't see in the dark. But his oar glowed brightly, a steady beacon cutting through the black, and somehow it suited him.

As the hours stretched, the chatter tapered. Boredom settled in. And then Frey noticed: they hadn't passed a branching path in a long time. The tunnel went on and on, unbroken. Even by his experience, experience he hated drawing on, hated anyone knowing about, this was wrong.

"This isn't normal," he said.

No one responded. The others kept walking, eyes forward.

"Hey." He said it louder. "This isn't normal."

Something stopped him. A chain, cuffed around his wrist.

He reached with his other arm. Manacled too.

He spun to follow the chains but they stretched upward into the dark, further than his darkvision could reach. He pulled. They didn't give.

He shouted. He screamed. The group kept walking, their shapes shrinking as the darkness swallowed them, as the edge of his vision claimed them one by one. They didn't turn back.

They left him.

Alone.

Chained.

In a mine.

"Please."

He knew that voice.

The overseer. The one from when he was young. The one who had tormented him, hurt him, laid the lashes across his back. The one who laughed as his mother starved.

"Come here, Frey."

The chains kept pulling.

The explosion was deafening. Louder than anything he'd ever heard. The walls shattered. Heat scorched his skin.

But the chains weren't pulling anymore.

The voice had stopped.

Silence.

"...Baby?"

Her hair was charred. Her skin was cracked and bleeding. But her eyes, soft and lovely, the same eyes he'd missed every single day, found his.

Frey dropped to his knees beside her. He could barely see through the tears.

She smiled at him. A broken, gory thing, her burned lips splitting as she did, blood spilling down her chin.

"My baby," she said softly. In pain. In love.

This was why he'd learned magic. So he'd never have to watch someone die in front of him and be helpless. So he'd never have to feel this. But his core was empty. No warmth. No glow. Just his mother, bleeding to death in his arms, because of his own spell.

He was still singing when the light left her eyes.

"Frey, you're dreaming. Please — look at me—"

A hand touched his shoulder. Frey flung back without thinking, felt his fist connect, heard the crunch of bone and cartilage.

Jun stumbled, hand flying to his nose, blood streaming freely.

"Jun?" Frey's voice came out strange. Hollow.

Jun cast a small healing spell, fixed his nose, and looked at him with eyes that were already grieving.

"Frey..." Jun said quietly.

"Heal her." His voice cracked clean in half. "Please."

Jun moved without another word. He knelt beside her, placed his hands gently on her shoulder. The soft yellow glow of healing magic bloomed from his palms.

She didn't move.

"Again," Frey whispered.

Jun did it again.

She stayed still.

"She can't leave me." Frey curled inward, his whole body folding around the grief. "She can't leave me alone—"

Warmth settled over him. Jun's arms, pulling him close and holding fast.

"You're not alone," Jun told him, fierce and quiet and certain. "I'll never leave you."

Frey let himself be held. He stayed there until his breathing evened out, until the frantic hammering of his pulse slowed, until the dream's edges began to blur and the cold reality of the present crept back in around them.

"Dream?" he murmured into Jun's shoulder.

Frey braced for it.

"I was seventy-two when my mum died," Jun said quietly.

Frey said nothing.

"A grown man. But in that moment—" Jun huffed a small breath that wasn't quite a laugh. "All I wanted was for her to tut at me, call me emotional, and then fix everything the way she always did."

The silence between them settled differently now. Jun leaned back, dragged a hand across his face, then pulled an expression of mild disgust when it came away bloody from his nose.

"It's been years," he continued, staring at his hand. "I've learned not to expect to see her face when I wake up.
