"I know you're used to being the strong one," Jun continued, his voice a soothing melody. "But it's okay to have moments of weakness, you don’t have to hide it. I’m here with you.”

Frey felt a lump forming in his throat, and his eyes welled up with tears. He hadn't realised how much he needed someone to understand, to see through his façade of confidence. Jun's words were a balm to his wounded spirit, a reminder that he didn't have to be perfect all the time.

"Thank you," Frey whispered, his voice trembling. "I... I don't know what's come over me."

Jun gave Frey's shoulder a reassuring squeeze and a light kiss on his forehead, "That's alright. We're a team, remember? We're here for each other, through the ups and downs. You've been there for me countless times, and now I want to be here for you."

Frey nodded, the tears now flowing freely down his cheeks. Jun didn't shy away from the display of vulnerability, instead, he pulled Frey into a warm embrace, letting him cry. Frey buried his face in Jun's shoulder, feeling the comfort and support of the arms around him.

In that quiet alcove of the bustling spaceport, Jun held Frey, and as the minutes passed, the chaos of the world outside faded into insignificance, replaced by the reassuring presence of a friend.

PART TWO - FREY’S FUCKING DEAD EDITION.

Jun felt empty. The thrum in his veins that he associated with the constant energy of his magic was missing. Locked away behind the inlaid manacles clasped around his wrists. He hadn’t known there were items capable of suppressing magic, but the fact that the slavers who had captured him and Frey had some, meant they were in trouble.

Six days they had sat in the cell. He and Frey had been snatched when they were on a market excursion, Jun because magic was a powerful commodity, and Frey because… well the way some of the slavers had leered at him, didn’t bear thinking about.

It had taken Jun some time to get used to the heavy manacles on his wrists. The loss of his magic was an unsettling discomfort, and when he tried to channel, it caused him so much agony he’d thought he was dying. Frey had been terrified out of his mind. The panic attack he’d experienced from being captured and helpless had been the worst he’d ever felt, and Jun had been too delirious with pain to help him through it.

Now they were bored. The adrenaline of fear had long since worn off. There was the ever present feeling of unease, they knew they were headed to an unsavoury destination, but they were grateful they’d been held in the same cell at least. They shared comfort, made innumerable fruitless escape plans and spent hours holding each other, hoping that the rest of their crew were hot on their tail.

They’d tracked the time and days by the frequency of meals, and the pangs of hunger from their stomachs. Frey estimated it had been around six days. Early in the morning on the seventh day they heard a distant commotion on the ship.

Frey was a light sleeper, he was alert and standing at the first sound. At their end of the ship there had been little to no noise, only the clicking footsteps as their jailor brought their meals. This was new. He shimmied Jun’s shoulder, who grumbled “Bzuh?”

“Shh, listen!” Frey hissed. Jun sat up blearily and cocked his head. The commotion sounded like explosions? Gunfire? And shouting-

“That’s Star!” Frey whooped, “I’d recognise that big doofus’s yell anywhere!” He turned to Jun, matching the elf’s hopeful smile with his own, “The bastards found us!”

Frey dashed to the door panel and began banging on it. “We’re in here!” he yelled, “We’re here!”

The gunfire and shouting got closer, and then the door panel shhkked open to reveal Brian Styles decked in full combat gear and holding a beastly plasma rifle. He paused and looked at the two,

“We need to leave.” He said. Frey grinned,

“Nice to see you too!” He grabbed Jun’s hand and left their cell. Jun laughed in relief. He hadn’t wanted to consider too much what future lay in store for them at the hands of their captors, but he had never been so happy to see the android.

“Where’s Star and Fizzy?” He asked as they dashed through empty corridors,

“Fizzy has planted a large explosive on the exterior of this ship. Our plan is to get onto the escape shuttle and then Fizzy will blow it up. She is waiting on the Leviathan. Star should be clearing the way to the exit.” Brian Styles told them in a steady tone. “We need to hurry. We deployed decoys across the ship but they will not last long.”

As if Brian Styles had jinxed them, the moment they turned the corner, they found themselves face to face with three slavers. The slavers were armed, but Brian Styles, ever the efficient android, opened fire first. His plasma rifle discharged with a deafening roar, bolts of searing energy lancing out and striking two of the slavers square in the chest. They crumpled to the ground, their weapons clattering beside them.

Frey and Jun didn't waste any time. Frey sprinted forward, grabbing the fallen slavers' weapons and tossing one to Jun. The remaining slaver, clearly taken aback by the sudden assault, fumbled for his weapon but was too slow. Jun and Frey fired in unison, their shots hitting the slaver, and he joined his comrades on the cold metal floor.

"Nice shooting," Frey said, patting Jun on the back. Jun grinned, “All that practice with you is paying off!”

Brian Styles nodded in acknowledgment and led the way, following his mental map of the ship toward the hangar bay. The sounds of gunfire and shouting continued to echo through the corridors, but they pressed on. The situation was tense, and they knew they had to reach the escape shuttle before the slavers overwhelmed them.

Finally, they reached the hangar bay, a cavernous chamber filled with various spacecraft, cargo crates, and flickering overhead lights. At the far end, bathed in the eerie glow of the hangar's dim lighting, was the escape shuttle they had been hoping for. Its sleek design and pristine condition stood in stark contrast to the chaos surrounding them. It was their freedom, and it was so close.

Star was engaged in a heated firefight with a group of slavers who were attempting to block their path to the shuttle. His energy shield crackled as it absorbed incoming fire, and his booming laugh filled the hangar as he dispatched slavers with his colossal fists.

"Haha! Found you fuckers! Get over here!" Star called out, gesturing for them to join him.

Brian Styles provided covering fire, making precise shots that incapacitated the slavers who dared to approach them. Frey and Jun dashed towards Star, taking cover behind some cargo crates.

"We need to clear a path to the shuttle," Star grumbled as he punched another slaver, sending him sprawling.

Frey nodded, his eyes scanning the hangar for more threats. "I'll cover while you and Jun make a run for it." Star frowned, assessing the danger, then gestured at Jun.

“Can you, you know, whammy them?” He wiggled his fingers indicating magic. Jun looked at his manacles, still restricting his magic, and shook his head. Star clearly didn’t understand, but he glanced at the iron bounds and accepted Jun’s assessment. He held Jun by the bicep, “We run then.” He gave a count of three crates, nodded at Frey and Brian Styles who took position to provide covering fire. Brian Styles withdrew a flash bang grenade from one of the many pockets on the cloak he loved and launched to towards the remaining slavers, who were creating their own barricade of cover.

Jun, his eyes streaming from the blinding light, was pulled into a run by Star, his other arm firing wildly at the slavers. They were halfway across the hangar when the slavers retaliated with a grenade of their own. Jun heard Star's yell cut off as it exploded in front of them.

The world spun as Jun saw stars. He lay on his back, ears ringing, and the side of his face burning. Pain coursed through his body. A weight pressed down on his chest, and when he lifted his head, he saw Star, his skin blackened and raw, half-lying on top of him, shielding him from the brunt of the explosion.

Star's eyes, once brimming with life, were now glazed with pain. Distant screams echoed, but Jun was too dazed to react.

Star.

Star was dead?

Hands gripped him from behind, tugging him free from Star’s smouldering body. Jun turned and saw Frey yelling something in his face, but he couldn’t comprehend what was happening. His legs wouldn’t move. His cheek burned. Frey slapped him, and the world slammed back into clarity.

"Jun, move! JUN, MOVE!" Frey implored, forcefully dragging Jun to his feet. Jun stumbled, his legs unsteady, and Frey's arms supported him as they staggered away. Meanwhile, Brian Styles had abandoned cover, discharging his plasma rifle recklessly, an aura of anger and ruthlessness enveloping the typically composed android.

Jun's heart wrenched as he watched another grenade land behind Brian Styles. He tried to shout a warning, but time itself seemed to slow to a crawl. The explosion claimed Brian Styles, tearing him into pieces. His signature cloak, tattered and fragmented, landed before Jun and Frey.

“What do we do? What do we do?!” Frey was screaming. He tried to pivot them to get behind the nearest cover but his body suddenly jolted.

Time slowed. Jun watched in wide eyed terror as Frey crumpled slowly to the ground. A bullet hole ripped through his chest. The tiefling stared blankly as he landed face first on the metal floor.

Jun, still reeling, dropped to his knees, oblivious to the approaching slavers. Their weapons had fallen silent; the threat had been extinguished.

“Frey, oh no, Frey” Jun wailed, lifting his beloved and cradling him in his lap. Frey coughed, a trickle of blood escaping his lips, tracing a crimson path down his chin. He gazed at Jun, his eyes revealing his terror and agony. Jun sobbed and cupped Frey's cheeks, attempting to conjure his magic, but only pain coursed through him, choking his desperate incantations.

“Hey… you’re okay, you’re alright.” He whispered, tears falling freely as he choked on the words. Frey gasped, his body convulsing one last time. His eyes, once pleading, faded into emptiness…

“No, no no no Frey, no.” Jun begged, clutching the tiefling's limp hand, his world crumbling around him.

Gradually, Jun became aware of the looming presence of the slavers surrounding him, just as a brutal backhand across his face sent Jun sprawling across the cold metal floor.

“What a shitstorm you’ve put us through, elf.” A nameless slaver spat down at him, then gave an ugly smile. “At least you’re still breathing though. You’ll fetch a good amount of credit. Shame about the devil though.”

Jun struggled to draw breath, his mind a whirlwind of disbelief and despair. He clenched his fists, desperately searching for any lifeline.

Brian Styles’ cloak. His communicator. With tears and snot staining his face, Jun crawled toward the tattered fabric, his movements desperate and pitiable. He reached for the Comm Unit. He could hear the slavers laughing at his misery, but he didn’t care.

Finally, with all the determination he could muster, Jun pressed the button. His voice quivered, yet he tried to maintain composure.

“Fizzy, we’re free and clear.”

The response was lost in the eruption as the walls of the hangar bay exploded around him.

The walk back to the inn was quiet, interrupted by the chatter from Jun’s teeth as he shivered in the night air.

The group entered the inn through the massive hole gaping through the wall, smiling sheepishly at [name] who looked confused, doubting her own memory that she’d seen them leave, and why were two of them wet through?

Frey shot her a wink as they trudged up the stairs. Jun rarely felt tired, but today had really been a long one. He was glad of the chance to rest before they had to continue up the mountain.

He waved Star and Brian Styles off into their room as he went along the corridor to the room he’d claimed as his. Whilst the tent they used on the mountain had been warm enough, especially with so many bodies crammed together one of which was a genuine actual tiger. He was definitely looking forward to a mattress, soft sheets and the ability to sprawl. He was lost in thoughts, eagerly anticipating stripping his clothes off and letting them air out whilst he rested.

Which was why, when he went to shut the door behind him and Frey was stood there grinning, Jun was speechless.

“What, did you forget Star was a cheapskate?” Frey laughed at Jun’s expression, “Scoot out the way, you and I are roomies tonight.” He slipped under Jun’s arm holding the door and whistled at the room.

“You didn’t shut the window on the way out!” The tiefling scolded, and Jun grimaced, remembering the less than elegant departure from the room…and his faceplant into the snow. The room was frigidly cold, as the winterchill blew in from the open window, and a small drift of snow settled on the floor below the cill. Frey strolled across the floor and pulled the window shut. “That’s better, but it’s still cold as fuck in here.” His lips curled downwards in a cute frown, and Jun quickly looked away.

There was only one bed in the room. Despite the below zero temperature it looked soft and padded, with two layers of blankets and a thick quilted duvet. The pillow looked plush and padded. Jun looked at it longingly, especially when the tiefing flung himself backwards onto it and bounced on it a couple of times.

“Aaaahhh” Frey groaned, falling back onto the duvet and closing his eyes… He paused, opening one eye and peering at Jun who was still standing in the doorway. A smirk curled his lips. “Dibs.”

Jun nodded and looked around the sparsely decorated room. A table with a wooden chair, a chest of drawers. A thin rug. He sighed and took off his cloak, folding it up to create a makeshift pillow. He headed towards the rug and was proud he only hesitated for a second before lying down, trying to resist shivering.

Frey’s head popped over the bed, dominating Jun’s field of vision.

“I thought you would have put up more resistance than that!” He said with a wink. Jun raised an eyebrow.

“Is there any point in me trying to resist?” He asked, and Frey grinned.

“Probably not, but it’s no fun if you just give up straight away! You didn’t even try! You could have suggested tossing a coin, or taking turns or sharing. And the bed is soooo comfy, but it looks like you want to sleep on the floor!” Jun sighed,

“Do you want to toss a coin?”

“Nope!”

“How about we take turns?”

“Nope!”

“How about we share?”

“Is that what you want?”

Jun’s brain short circuited.

“I-uh…” yes I do. Yes I want to share. “We could, I guess, if you didn’t mind?” Frey smiled sweetly,

“I don’t mind.” Jun sat up cautiously. He suddenly felt very vulnerable lying on the floor with Frey looking over him, and very aware of the other man’s gaze. He was grateful for the curse turning his skin blue, so it wasn’t so apparent the tops of his ears were flushing.

Frey watched him with a beguiling smile, his face giving nothing away but a sweet smile. Jun struggled to find the right words.

“I would prefer to sleep on the bed.” He said carefully, Frey’s dark eyes flashed and his smile grew marginally wider.

“With me?” Jun became hyper aware of his racing heart.

“With you.” He said and tried to control his breathing. There was a pause, their eyes were locked, then Frey jumped up and swept the covers aside.

“Come on then!” He laughed, “Don’t be shy, it’s not like we haven’t shared a sleeping space before.”

No, Jun thought, but we’ve always had the others too. It’s never been just us… but he didn’t say anything. He sat on the edge of the bed and panicked. With trembling fingers he unlaced and then kicked off his boots, then he shifted and slid under the covers...
cdz5j250qa1n:
Loke sighed wearily as he etched his sloping signature onto the bottom of a sprawling report. The document, a testament to bureaucratic labour, seemed to stretch endlessly across 12 pages of minuscule text. He deliberately avoided glancing at the final page number. Once the report was marked and dispatched to the archives, he reluctantly shifted his attention to the next item on his seemingly endless to-do list, only to find the task count had increased rather than diminished…

He sighed as his heart ached for simpler times—back when he and his small militia patrolled a tranquil rural planet and their biggest concerns revolved around lost livestock or drunken brawls. Now, as one of the heads of the Intergalactic Imperium police force, those idyllic days felt like distant echoes.

His tablet flickered to the next assignment, and the growing number only deepened his frustration. He desperately needed an assistant. He was going to be swallowed by the ever-expanding workload. Wistfully, he felt a pang of regret for how his career had spiralled beyond his wants.

He reluctantly opened the next report. 17 pages this time. Gods give him strength.

Suddenly, a shiver ran down Loke's spine, alerting him to another presence in the office. Without diverting his gaze from the report, he instinctively reached for his blaster, pointing it at the intruder. Jun, with hands raised in surrender, hurriedly spoke, "Sorry! Sorry! Didn’t mean to startle you!"

Loke scowled, swiftly rising from his seat, closing the blinds and ushering Jun into a chair, hidden from casual view. "This is a military station, and you're the most wanted man in the Universe! What are you doing here?" Loke hissed, but then worry knotted his stomach. "Did something happen to the others?"

Jun's troubled expression confirmed that something was wrong, but he answered "No, they're okay, and I mean to keep it that way," he replied slowly. Loke stayed silent, waiting for more… Hesitantly Jun continued, "I'm here to turn myself in, Loke. I can't keep putting them in danger."

Loke, torn between concern, justice, and worry, nodded, contemplating the implications. "You know what that means, right?"

"I know. I'm going to face execution or lifetimes in a prison planet, but I was hoping—if I came quietly—they would have some leniency," Jun admitted, studying his fingertips. Loke watched him cautiously, knowing the power those fingertips held, and the lives they had taken…

But then he considered all the lives they had saved.

He grudgingly acknowledged, "There might be something I can do, but it might not be a pleasant alternative to death." Jun wiped his eyes and stood, and Loke was struck by the elf's unexpected height.

"I've done terrible things," Jun said resolutely, "I don't deserve any light treatment. I've earned whatever punishment is coming my way." He removed his jacket, placing his blasters on the floor, signalling his readiness for arrest. "But, please, could I ask one more favour? Can Fizzy's crimes be placed solely on my shoulders? She shouldn't be held accountable for what we did. And... could you watch out for the others?"

Loke, scowled and retrieved handcuffs from his belt. "I'll do what I can," he said gruffly. The metallic click echoed through the room as the restraints locked onto Jun's wrists. Loke's weathered hand rested on Jun's arm in silent reassurance.

"Are you ready? Once we go through that door, there's not much more I can do for you. I'll petition to have you sentenced to imprisonment rather than execution, but I can't guarantee it will work."

Jun avoided eye contact, his gaze fixed on the looming door. "I'm ready."

Loke steeled himself. There was no reason to delay any longer. Guiding Jun toward the door, he swung it open, unveiling the office's wider chaos and the imminent tumult that would follow. In the midst of the ensuing turmoil, he couldn't shake the thought, ‘who's going to watch out for you, Jun?’
cu3b2eilqa1r:
For all the ghosts

It had been a gruelling day. That wasn't unusual for Jun lately, but today's bleakness cut deeper than usual. The whole camp, convinced that their riches outweighed their lives, had armed themselves in defiance. They didn’t cower. They took aim. They fired. They died.

A familiar numbness settled over him as he went through the motions. Take the key out of the leader’s pocket. Retrieve the scrip he’d been sent for, a handful of papers one could hardly believe was worth dying for. Eyes forward. Return to the ship. Ignore the bodies. Don’t look at the bodies. Don’t memorise their faces. Don’t imagine their lives, hopes, dreams, loves…

Open door to his shuttle. Get into the pilot seat and initiate launch protocols. Don’t think about the massacre left behind. Be grateful that Fizzy wasn’t with him for this one.

One hour into the flight, Jun noticed the blood spatters on his shirt. He had enough time to engage the autopilot before diving to the washroom to throw up. He gasped, leaning against the metal rim as his stomach twisted. With a shaky hand, he flushed the evidence away and let his head fall back against the wall with a quiet ‘thunk’.

Why did they choose to resist? Idiots. And now they were dead idiots.

A beep from his comm unit jarred Jun from his spiralling thoughts. It was Ruohan demanding a status update. With a resigned sigh, Jun typed back:

On my way back. Secured the notes.

A pause, then Ruohan replied.

And the offenders?

Tears stung Jun’s eyes. He wiped them away bitterly.

Dead

Good. There’s another assignment for you. If you’re late, I’ll send the girl instead.

A headache began to gnaw at Jun's temples. He returned to the cockpit and increased the autopilot’s speed. Another beep. This time, it was Fizzy, checking in. Ignoring her would only make her worry. He typed a quick reply.

Job’s done. I’m okay.

He saw she was typing something in response but he shut his comm unit off. He couldn’t handle seeing her reply right now. He wasn’t okay. He was a far sight from okay, but he didn’t know what else to do. Ruohan was despicable. He was a fucking slithering worm of a person. But he paid well, and they were desperate for the money.

Seven months ago they had nothing but the clothes on their back, a dismantled cyborg and a drowning grief. They’d found an engineer on Aurora who said he could put Brian Styles back together again, but it was going to cost. This was the quickest way to get the funds. He didn’t have a lot of time. Every day they delayed, was a day Frey and Star fell further away from him.

Against his will Jun’s hands flipped over the comm unit, and deft fingers peeled away the case. They’d lost everything in the explosion. None of the tech on their ship could be redeemed.

Despite the urgency and need to scrounge every penny, with the first few credits they’d earned Jun had secretly visited a back-alley Mindsage. He’d envisioned the best image of Frey he could, one where the tiefling was sitting in the dining room, leaning back on the chair with his feet on the table. His eyes were creased with laughter and his tongue was sticking out. His hair was tousled and his cheeks were flushed. It had been just a normal day, but that was the moment Jun had really, truly seen Frey for the beauty he was.

The Mindsage had captured this image onto enchanted paper, draining Jun’s wallet completely. He’d gone hungry that night, and the night after, but he had secured this one picture.

It was this picture he slid out from under the case on his comm unit, creased and fading through repeated handling. He held it with trembling fingers. The pad of his thumb tracing the line of Frey’s cheek.

“I’m going to find you.” Jun whispered. No matter the cost, even if he had to damn himself in the process, he would find Frey.
emjb77bdqa20:
Kick at the Darkness

The deafening sound of munitions fire reverberated through the hold of The Leviathan, piercing the air with a deadly symphony, threatening to overwhelm Jun’s concentration. He stood at the back of the hanger, arms raised in focus as he layered spells on top of his allies, a shield to slow bullets, bull's strength and enhanced speed. This was normally something he could do easily on one target, but today he’d doubled up and had twinned the spellwork onto the heavy hitters in the team, Brian Styles and Star. It was taking all his focus, and he felt the magic straining within him, but if they failed here, it would mean death.

In the midst of the firefight, chaos reigned as the empowered Star and Brian Styles charged through their assailants like angry rottweilers. Star’s gauntlets punctuated the gunfire with deafening thunder as he pummelled the pirates who’d dared try to steal their ship. Together, their coordinated assault and calculated strikes were testament to their battle-hardened expertise and they made progress in pushing the pirates back. Star yelled a fierce war shout as he caved in another skull.

To Jun’s left and right, Frey and Fizzy provided much needed cover, using their laser rifles with deadly accuracy. The pirates were faltering under the barrage of the two big hitters cutting through their forces, but slowly, they were beginning to realise that trying to take down Brian Styles and Star was not going to work. They needed to either retreat… or disrupt the spellcaster.

The magical strain was nearly too much. Jun’s vision was tunnelling slightly, but he held onto the grip of the spells. Not much longer and Brian Styles and Star would clean up and they’d be safe. He felt the impact of each bullet hitting the shield, and he gave it much more energy. Normally the spells could last only a minute, but he’d pumped more power into it, his mind fully focussed, leaving his body vulnerable. He trusted that Fizzy and Frey would look after him, as he looked after Brian and Star.

BANG.

Jun jolted as a large impact struck him from the side. His hold on the spells faltered slightly but he maintained focus. But then Fizzy's voice pierced through the chaos, a desperate cry for help.

“FREY!”

Jun’s attention returned to himself and found that he was on the floor. A body lay on top of his and a mop of white hair covered the face. Frey! His face was buried in Jun’s chest and he lay unmoving. Jun struggled to comprehend what had happened, but then he saw red blossoming through the back of Frey’s jumpsuit. Blood.

Fizzy was staring at the blood on Frey’s jacket, but a roar from Star had her refocusing her laser rifle. She fired with reckless abandon. Jun knew he couldn’t drop the spells on his allies, the subsequent backlash would leave them in danger, especially when there were a half a dozen pirates left, but Frey had been shot!

“Frey!” Jun cried, as his partner lay unmoving on him, Frey had clearly pushed him out of the way of a bullet, taking it for himself. Jun put shaky hands on the wound, feeling hot and slippery as he tried to put as much pressure as possible. The bolstering spells in his mind faltered as he felt the turmoil of decision. He could heal Frey, but then Star and Brian Styles could get hurt. He could keep the spells up, but then Frey was dying…

Distantly he could hear his allies, fighting with renewed vigour to neutralise the remaining threats. The crackling energy of blasters and the dull thuds of hand-to-hand combat echoed through the ship, each moment crucial.

Frey lay on Jun’s legs, his breathing shallow, hands lying limp by his side. His jumpsuit was now a gory red as the wound pulsed blood. Too much blood. His face, turned to the side, once a vibrant pink complexion, was pale, and his lips had lost all colour. His eyes creased in pain as he stared to the side.

Jun's eyes welled with tears as he took in the sight, his voice trembling with a mixture of fear and determination.

"No, goddamnit Frey," Jun whispered, his voice filled with an unyielding resolve. "I can't lose you. Not like this.” He made his choice. “I’m sorry.” and he let the spells go.

Beyond the makeshift barricade he heard Star’s warshout cut off with a sharp gasp of surprise. Jun felt a stab of guilt, but had to trust that they’d be okay with Fizzy’s support. Frey would not be okay.

With a quivering hand, Jun reached out and placed it on Frey's back, his fingers tracing the contours of the man who he’d become so close to. The man whose smile lit up his day.

The man who’d taken a bullet for him.

The man he… loved?

Jun dipped into his magical wellspring to pull healing energy out and direct it into Frey. This was something he did often, his teammates often bore cuts, bruises, scrapes in their day to day. But the magic did not come. He’d spent it all.

“No!” Jun growled in frustration. Beneath him, Frey’s breathing became fainter.

There must be something he could do! He couldn’t lose Frey. Then Jun had an idea.

Drawing upon the wellspring of his own life energy and the depths of his magic, Jun began channelling his own life essence into Frey's wounded form.

At first, nothing seemed to be happening. Jun felt a strain as his magic pulsed through his fingers, but the wound remained open, more blood coated his hands.

Frey's eyes drifted closed.

No. NO. It wasn’t enough. Jun gave it more. Poured more life energy into it. His veins felt hot, and his chest felt hollow, empty, but he gave it more. Frey wouldn’t die. Jun wouldn’t let him.

A warmth spread through his fingers, and a thin strand of light connected from his tips with Frey, transferring the life energy needed. It wasn’t enough. He was still going to lose Frey.

Jun grunted in discomfort. Frey’s eyes opened in both concern, his voice strained as he called out to Jun. "Stop... no stop, it's killing you." Jun was heartened, was it working?

He refused to give up, his determination unyielding. It wasn’t enough yet.

The strand of light grew, spreading a web across Frey’s back, evolving into an intense, blistering heat that consumed both Jun and Frey. Jun felt sweat drip down his face, as the hollowness in his chest began to spread to his limbs, but it wasn’t enough yet, Frey still wasn’t out of danger. He saw white veins of magic crawling across his hands, his body weakened as he willingly poured his life magic into the one he... loved.... He loved Frey.

Through the haze of exertion, Jun managed a soft smile, his gaze fixed upon Frey's lips, pleased to see the pink tinge return. "I won't let you go," he whispered, his voice filled with a mixture of exhaustion and affection. "You're worth it." His hand trembled as he cupped Frey's cheek, thumb stroking the skin softly.

As the last remnants of Jun's life energy poured into Frey the wound began to close, his breathing steadied, and colour returned to his cheeks. The life force that Jun had willingly shared with him had done it. He’d saved Frey.

Yet, as Frey's strength returned, he realised the toll it had taken. He gently clasped Jun's trembling hand, his voice was filled with anguish and gratitude. "No, why did you do it"

Jun's body slumped, his breath shallow and laboured, but a serene smile graced his lips. "I did it, Frey. I saved you."

Positions reversed, Frey twisted so Jun was lying on the floor instead. Tears streamed down his face as he held Jun close, his voice choked with emotion. "You idiot, Jun. I can't lose you either."

In that moment, Jun's eyes fluttered closed, his strength depleted. He had given everything he had to save the one he loved. Frey held him tightly, and sobbed. The firefight raged on, but in that corner of the ship, time stood still.
f6edtz6zqa4z:
The rain had turned the landing bay into a mirror, neon stars smeared and fractured across the durasteel floor. Sirens wailed somewhere deep in the station’s spine, distant and grieving, like an animal mourning its dead. Bodies lay scattered across the bay, still smoking, still warm—too many to count.

Bounty hunters.

Each of them had chased the same hope: the one job that would set them free. Each of them had believed the rumours were exaggerated. Each of them had learned, too late, what it meant to stand before the Tempest.

Frey couldn’t move.

He’d heard the stories. Fizzy had told him, voice trembling, that Jun was different now. That the incident had changed them all. Frey knew what change felt like. He carried it in the ache of healed wounds, in the quiet flinch that never quite left him. The worst thing in his life had already happened, and he had survived it.

But this—

The man Frey loved fought to protect.
The man standing before him killed because he believed it was the only way the universe would leave Frey breathing.

They stood pressed together in the echoing dark, close enough that Frey could feel Jun’s heart hammering through his chest. Jun’s jacket was still warm from spellfire. Power clung to him, sharp and electric, but beneath it Frey felt the familiar tremor—the barely contained fear Jun never admitted to. His eyes glowed too brightly, arcane lines fracturing the violet Frey knew by heart.

Jun looked at him like a storm looks at the ground it’s about to strike.

The sirens drew closer. Ships gathered. More men came to die for a bounty Jun had never asked for.

“Step aside, Frey,” Jun murmured. His voice was gentle, and that made it worse. “I don’t want you to get hurt.”

Frey swallowed. “Let’s leave. Please. Jun, we still can.”

Jun’s gaze never wavered. “They won’t stop.” His fingers twitched, already reaching for the magic. “It will only take a moment. Wait for me on the shuttle.”

Frey stepped into him, closing the distance until there was nowhere for Jun to look but at him. He grabbed Jun’s jacket, fisting the fabric like a lifeline.

“No,” Frey said, the word trembling but unyielding. “I’m not waiting for you to come back broken.”

Jun stilled.

“We’re going to get our farm,” Frey whispered, voice cracking. “You promised me. You said we’d grow old together. You said we’d wake up sore and laughing and plant roses even though neither of us knows how to keep them alive.” Tears blurred his vision. “You said you’d read to me when my hands hurt too much, and I said I’d pretend not to notice when you reread the same page because you like the sound of my breathing.”

Jun’s breath hitched.

“But you can’t give me that if you’re dead inside,” Frey said. “Kill the Tempest. Please. Let Jun live.”

Jun stared at him like Frey had just handed him something unbearably fragile.

Frey’s lungs burned when the words ran out. He sagged forward, forehead pressing into Jun’s collarbone. Tears soaked the fabric of his jacket. His fingers ached where they clung, terrified that if he let go, Jun would slip back into the storm and never come home again.

Jun closed his eyes.

The air thickened. Magic surged, wild and aching, like grief looking for a place to land. Frey felt it coil around them, felt the familiar terror—this was where Jun disappeared, where love lost to necessity.

Then Jun leaned down.

His forehead rested against Frey’s, their noses brushing, breath mingling.

“I don’t remember when it stopped being me,” Jun whispered. His voice was small now, stripped bare. “The Tempest doesn’t feel fear. He doesn’t feel it when I imagine you alone. He doesn’t wake up screaming because he can’t close his eyes without seeing you bleeding in the fire.

Frey lifted his head. He cupped Jun’s face like he was something precious, something breakable. “But I need you,” he said softly. “Even when it hurts. Especially then.”

The sirens screamed closer. Drones swept past the bay, lights carving them into silhouettes. Somewhere above, the galaxy reached for Jun again, demanding sacrifice.

Jun let out a broken laugh. “They’ll never let us be happy.”

“Then we’ll steal it,” Frey said, leaning forward until their foreheads touched again. “Just enough. Just us.”

Jun inhaled—slow, shaking—and something finally gave way. The light in his eyes dimmed, unraveling like thread pulled too tight for too long. The crushing weight lifted. The Tempest receded, not destroyed, but held at bay by something older and softer.

Jun pressed his hands over Frey’s heart, eyes closed, memorizing the rhythm. “If I choose this,” he said, “I have to live with the fear. With the guilt. With loving you so much it hurts.”

Frey smiled through tears. “That’s living.”

Jun kissed Frey’s brow, lingering. Then his mouth traced Frey’s temple, his cheek—small, reverent kisses, like he was memorizing him in case the universe tried to erase him again. Finally, Jun wrapped his arms around Frey and turned them both, placing himself between Frey and the coming fire.

Jun whispered a spell that sounded like a vow.

The magic gathered—quiet, careful, threaded with restraint and love. Not a storm. A shelter.

The world folded.

When Frey could breathe again, the air was dry and warm. Dust clung to his knees. Stars shone unfamiliar overhead.

Planet Yeosang.

Jun sagged in his arms.

Frey caught him, sinking to the ground, holding him as if the act alone could keep him alive. He laughed and cried helplessly, pressing his face into Jun’s hair.

“Hey,” Frey whispered. “I’ve got you. I’ve got you.”

Jun looked up at him, eyes dull with exhaustion, but soft—so unbearably soft. “You’ll stay?” he murmured.

“Always,” Frey said.

Jun smiled, faint and real. “Then I think… I can try.”

And for the first time since the Tempest had been born in fire and grief, Jun allowed himself to imagine a future not measured in bodies—but in mornings. In gardens. In a man who loved him enough to stand in front of a storm and ask him to come home.

The strain in his arms woke Frey up. Disoriented he tried to move and found himself shackled to a wall by two thick iron manacles around his wrists. Instantly aware he stumbled to his feet as much as he could within his limitations and looked around. He was in a large stone room, a dungeon. The floor and walls were stone and lined with pairs of shackles bound to castiron rings in the stone. They were all empty apart from the one in front, where Jun was similarly bound and watching him.

"What the fuck...?" Frey asked, Jun smiled grimly.

"No idea, I've not been awake long. Can you break free?" Frey studied the manacle on his wrist, the clasp looked solid. With a swift thrust he yanked his arm as far forward as he could. The manacle pulled taut on his wrist, but remained sturdy. Taking the chain in both hands and planting his feet against the wall, Frey tried again, using all his strength. At the wall some dust shifted, but otherwise the loop remained intact. Breathing heavily, Frey conceded that he wasn't going to be able to break free.

His eyes met Jun's across the dimly lit chamber. The elf's eyes had lost a bit of sparkle, and his smile faltered.

"Well, that's plan A busted." Jun said.

Suddenly, the heavy wooden door creaked open, revealing a figure that exuded malevolence and sadistic pleasure. Frey cursed. It was Skirrin.

The older vampire sauntered into the room with a cruel smile, his eyes gleaming with a twisted delight. The air grew thick with tension as he gazed at the two captives.

"Well, well," Skirrin sneered, voice dripping with malice. "Look at this lovely reunion. I've heard tales of your treachery, Frey, and I must say, the opportunity to punish you brings me immense satisfaction."

Frey's gaze hardened, his eyes smoldered with a mix of rage and determination. "Do whatever you want to me," he spat, defiance lacing his words. "But leave Jun out of this. He has nothing to do with our past."

Skirrin's grin widened and he stepped closer to Jun, long finger tenderly tracing his face as Jun recoiled. "Ah, but that's precisely why I've chosen him," Skirrin taunted, his voice laced with sadistic glee. "You see, Frey, I want you to watch as I drain him, drop by precious drop. I want to revel in your despair."

Frey's body tensed, muscles straining against his restraints, his eyes blazing with an intensity that bordered on madness. "Don't you dare," he seethed, his voice trembling with rage. "I'll fucking kill you!"

Skirrin laughed, a chilling sound that echoed through the chamber. "Oh, how entertaining," he chuckled. "But first, let's enjoy the spectacle, shall we?"

As Skirrin turned back to Jun, a mix of fear and determination flickered within Jun's eyes. He refused to show weakness, even in the face of imminent torment. He met Frey's eyes, and Frey could see the silent plea in them before Jun took a deep breath and turned back to his captor, gaze unwavering.

Skirrin turned to Frey as his bony fingers stroked Jun's face, tenderly caressing from his jawline up to his hair. Fingers turned strong as he gripped Jun's hair and wrenched his head to one side, exposing his neck.

Frey's struggles intensified, his eyes burning with an untamed fury. "Don't you do it!" He screamed. "You leave him alone!" The chains strained against his desperate attempts to break free, his mind consumed by a maddening desire to protect Jun at any cost.

Skirrin gave Frey a big smile, exposing the sharpened fangs beneath bloodless lips. Then quick as a flash he turned back and bit deep into Jun's neck, eliciting a gasp of pain.

As Skirrin's fangs sank deeper into Jun's neck, an intense agony surged through Jun's body. The torment intensified with each passing moment, an uncomfortable sucking feeling, with each heartbeat he could feel the lifeforce leaving him. Jun gritted his teeth, refusing to succumb to the overwhelming pain. He knew that showing weakness would only feed Skirrin's sadistic pleasure. He clenched his eyes shut and attempted to shove Skirrin off, knowing how futile his attempts would be.

Across the room, Frey yelled incoherently and strained against his restraints, his muscles bulging with exertion. The chains that bound him dug deeper into his flesh, crimson rivulets streaming down his arms. But no matter how hard he fought, they held him captive, his desperate attempts at liberation in vain.

Skirrin reveled in the spectacle, his eyes gleaming with malicious delight. The room pulsated with a twisted energy, tainted by the suffering he had orchestrated. With each drop of Jun's blood that coursed down his throat, Skirrin grew stronger, his power and sadistic glee escalating.

Jun's face began to lose colour which caused Frey's struggles to grow even more frantic, fueled by a maddening rage that threatened to consume him. The sound of metal scraping against stone filled the chamber as he fought against the unyielding chains, his hands bloody and raw. But the restraints held firm, mocking his defiance.

Desperation gripped Jun as he watched Frey's futile attempts at freedom. He knew that time was slipping away, that Skirrin would not stop until his life force was extinguished. He could no longer feel his fingers and his legs were unsteady. His vision was showing spots on the edges, but in the face of such despair, Jun's will held strong, refusing to break under the weight of their tormentor's sadistic games.

Through gritted teeth, Jun turned his gaze back to Skirrin, determination burning in his eyes. "Is this the best you can do?" he spat, his voice laced with defiance.

Skirrin's cruel laughter echoed through the chamber, his eyes ablaze with malice. "We shall see, little hunter," he taunted, his voice laced with a sadistic edge. "But for now, I adore your suffering and the agony it brings to your beloved."

Frey roared with a primal ferocity. "You will pay for every drop of blood you take from him. I will tear you apart, piece by piece!"

As Skirrin resumed his deadly attack, Jun fought against the encroaching darkness, summoning every ounce of strength he had left. He locked eyes with Frey, silently urging him to hold on, to keep fighting whilst his own body was failing him. His heart ached at the helplessness etched on Frey's face, eyes burning with a mixture of fury and desperation, tears mingling wiht sweat as he strained against his restraints.

"Let him go, please!" Frey's voice trembled with a raw, primal rage. "Do what you want to me, but let him go."

But despite his efforts, Frey's struggles against the unyielding chains yielded no results. Each attempt to break free only served as a painful reminder of his helplessness, fueling his rage with a bitter frustration. He could only watch helplessly as Jun's eyes fluttered shut, body held up in Skirrin's grasp as the other vampire drained him.

Agonising seconds later, Skirrin pulled back from Jun, now motionless, and dropped him limply to the floor. He turned back to Frey and smiled, using the back of his sleeve to wipe Jun's blood from his chin.

"There now," He said, "This has been infinitely more satisfying than hurting you directly." He licked his lips, "and no wonder you keep him around, he's delicious," Frey roared in anger,

"You'll regret this. You're gonna die slowly." He promised, but Skirrin only laughed in response.

"I don't think so, I'll see you later Frey" and with that, he left, leaving Frey alone with Jun's body.

Once Skirrin left the room, the rage, the anger, the adrenaline drained out of Frey. The furious tears which had streamed from his eyes trickled again, as he fell to his knees and sobbed. Chains clinking as he put his face in his hands. Just that morning, he and Jun had argued and Frey had said he thought it was best they didn't see each other again... But not like this.

Suddenly facing the reality that he wouldn't see the slight uplift of Jun's mouth as he tried to hide a smile, the crease next to his eyes when he gave a rare, true smile... That he would never see the way his lips whispered his name..

Frey's body racked with relentless sobs, he knew this was what Skirrin wanted, wanted to see him brought low. But there was no reason to pretend he was strong anymore. His strength was slumped against the wall ten feet away.

"...ey." The noise was so slight at first Frey didn't hear it over the sound of his own heart breaking, but then it came again, light as a feather, "...Frey."

Jun.

It was Jun.

He was still alive!

"Jun!" Frey forgot he was shackled until the chains pulled taut as he leapt across the room. He growled in frustration at being unable to reach.

Infinitesimally slowly, Jun turned his head from where it had been laying squashed against the floor. His face was drawn and sallow, high cheek bones jutting prominently, but his eyes were still so alive.

"Frey..." He whispered with the revenance of a prayer. Frey sobbed again, the relief and terror overwhelming his throat.

"Jun, hold on okay. I'm going to get you out of here. You're going to be fine, okay baby." He promised breathlessly. Jun's eyes met his and he turned his lips slightly and with great effort, moved his head in the echo of a nod.

"I know... Frey." Energy spent, Jun's eyes fell closed of their own accord and prompted Frey into action. His wrists were raw and bloodied, if he hadn't been able to slip free of the shackles before, when he thought Jun was going to die, he wouldn't be able to do it now. He could try and brute force the shackles four times, once for each of his wrists and then Jun's as well... Or he could find an alternative.

"Think! Frey, godsfucking dammit" He cursed at himself. He couldn't concentrate with Jun's labored breathing occupying his eardrums, each breath a grain of sand dropping through a sand timer. He needed to be quick, Jun didn't have long. With a groan of frustration Frey dropped his head in his hands and brushed his hair back, and his fingers brushed against the earring in his right ear causing it to tingle, a tiny resonance that normally irritated him.

A sudden realisation struck him—he possessed a unique ability that might just give them a chance to break free.

He’d often used the murmurations in his voice to charm his victims, it was an ability he had honed over the years, and he had known some older vampires who were able to kill a person outright, just by changing the subliminal tone of their voice. He’d rarely used this function of his voice, but if he matched the frequency of the shackles just right, he just might be able to break them apart.

Summoning his focus, Frey took a deep breath and steadied himself. He closed his eyes, allowing the power within him to surge forth. As he exhaled, a resonant hum filled the air, emanating from the core of his being.

Harnessing the vibrations within his voice, Frey directed his power towards the manacles. He modulated the burr, aiming to find the resonant frequency of the metal. Slowly, he increased the intensity, his voice vibrating with a power that surpassed the physical.

Across the room, Jun groaned and Frey sent out a silent apology. The sound must be agony for his ears, but it was better than what awaited them if they didn’t escape…

As the vibrations cascaded through the shackles, cracks appeared along the surface of the iron. The room filled with a cacophony of creaking metal as the manacles began to weaken under the strain. Frey's determination surged, his voice intensifying in tandem with his resolve.

With a final, forceful crescendo, a hairline crack appeared in the shackle, and Frey used his other hand to snap it in two. His head was pounding and his throat felt like it was full of glass. There was a warm wetness on his top lip. He wiped it away and the back of his hand appeared crimson. A small cost. One he would pay over and over if it meant saving their lives.

Now he had done it once, it was quicker for him to find the right vibration to shatter the second manacle, which was cloven in two much quicker than the first. The blood from his nose was more than a trickle now so he stuffed his shirt into one nostril. He didn’t have time for this.

Staggering to his feet and across the room he cradled Jun’s body in his, grateful for the chance to hold him again. Jun was cold, lifeless, but there was a faint heartbeat in his chest and that was enough to spur Frey on.

Breaking two more shackles from Jun’s wrists caused Frey to cry out as his head and throat lanced with pain. but with a gentle touch, he removed the restraints from Jun, careful not to cause him further harm. Jun's eyes flickered open, a glimmer of recognition shining within them.

"Stay with me, Jun," Frey urged, breathing heavily, his voice filled with a mixture of relief and urgency. "We're getting out of here.”

Despite being on the verge of death himself, Jun’s brows furrowed in concern and a shaky hand rose to touch Frey’s lips, which were now gory from the torrent of blood coming from his nose. “Don’t worry about me,” Frey smiled, and winced as his skull pounded in response.

He hooked his arms under Jun’s legs and neck, cradling his body close. Jun’s head lolled into Frey’s shoulder. Unsteadily, he rose to his feet. They weren’t out of danger yet.

The heavy wooden door which Skirrin had entered from was unlocked, and Frey carefully opened it to reveal a dimly lit stone corridor.

Frey peered cautiously into the corridor beyond. It appeared to be empty, devoid of any immediate threats. He knew time was of the essence, so he took a deep breath, mustering his resolve, and stepped out into the corridor.

Moving swiftly and silently, Frey navigated the winding passageways, his senses on high alert. He held Jun close to his chest, protectively shielding him from any potential danger. The flickering torchlight cast eerie shadows on the cold stone walls, adding an unsettling atmosphere to their escape.

With each passing corridor, Frey's determination grew stronger. He refused to let Skirrin's sadistic games claim their lives. He had to find a way out, a way to ensure their survival.

Finally, after what felt like an eternity, Frey spotted a narrow staircase leading upward. A glimmer of hope sparked within him as he ascended the steps, his steps quick and purposeful. The sound of his heart pounding in his ears, mixed with the distant echoes of his own footsteps, heightened his sense of urgency.

At the top of the stairs, Frey pushed open a heavy wooden door, revealing a moonlit courtyard beyond. The cool night air greeted him, a welcome respite from the suffocating darkness of the dungeon. The scent of damp earth and freedom filled his nostrils, revitalising his spirit.

Frey carefully laid Jun down on the ground, making sure he was as comfortable as possible. He pressed a tender kiss to Jun's forehead, leaving a bloody smudge on the pale skin, before turning his attention to the surroundings. The courtyard appeared to be deserted, the only sounds being the rustling of leaves in the gentle breeze.

Taking a moment to steel himself, Frey used the last of his energy to race towards a nearby gate, and with a powerful kick, he sent it crashing open, splintering under the force. They needed to be quick now, the noise was likely to attract attention. But they were nearly out, the path to freedom lay before him, a glimmer of hope in the moonlit night.

Returning to Jun's side, Frey carefully scooped him up once more, cradling him in his arms. He felt Jun's faint heartbeat against his chest and soft breaths, a fragile reminder of the life Frey was fighting to preserve.

With steady determination, Frey carried Jun through the broken gate and into the unknown. The world outside awaited them, full of uncertainties and dangers, but also the possibility of healing and a chance to rebuild what had been shattered.

As they disappeared into the night, Frey's grip was gentle as he cradled Jun’s body, but his heart was full of rage.

Frey would return, and Skirrin would pay.

It all went wrong so fast! An ice storm battering the ships in the distance. Fires. Elementals??

They’d gone in to help. Of course they had. They were the ‘heroes of Saltmarsh’. Not only that, they had a duty to these merchants who had accompanied them on this dangerous venture.

The scene was overwhelming—a multitude of injured, dying, and lifeless bodies, and Jun, just one man, grappling with the immensity of the crisis.. The first mate began breathing agonally in his arms. He had only seconds left to live. Jun gritted his teeth. He was just one man, but he was here, and he was going to do his fucking best to save who he could. Casting a quick cure wounds to the man in his arms, Jun looked around, quickly assessing who he could save, and who it was already too late.

Jun shut his eyes as darkness closed in.

Frey.

Jun took a deep breath.

It was inevitable. Everything ends someday. Even the brightest stars burn themselves out. They knew. They knew they couldn't carry on forever. But they hoped for a quiet end.In the stillness of space, they'd gaze through the ship's window, exchanging soft kisses and envisioning their future.Planet side, a house, a garden, growing their own vegetables, their only notoriety being the goat chewing through her rope again. They'd smile, stroking skin in between soft kisses and plan how they'd decorate. Frey would demand lavish, Jun would want simple, they'd compromise on imaginary wallpaper and tchotchkes, spending thousands of credits on cream curtains and a high pressure shower.

However, the reality is never what one hopes for. It ended, not with a bang, but with a whimper. A persistent cough. Then Frey struggled to catch his breath running from guards, a run that normally he could do effortlessly.

Jun insisted on seeing a doctor. Of course he did. Frey said it was a cold, an annoying one, but it would go away soon enough. Jun dragged him, complaining all the while, to an Outer Planet Quack, one who wouldn't immediately ring the capital, but had a halfway decent clinic and an x-ray machine.

Cancer. That was the diagnosis. Likely caused by toxic dust in the mines all those years ago. Prognosis was grim. The symptoms had progressed too rapidly. He had weeks, maybe months. “I'm sorry.” The doctor said, wringing his hands, terrified of misplaced wrath from the Siren and Tempest.

He was right to fear. Jun's anguish erupted violently and the clinic bore the brunt of his despair. Frey, ever the counterbalance, silently transferred a generous sum to the terrified doctor, offering gratitude amidst the wreckage. Each step back to their ship was punctuated by Frey's labored breaths, a haunting metronome counting down his remaining days.

Frey wasn't scared of death. Nobody in this line of work could afford to be. They nearly died every other week. But on top of being the most destructive force in the universe, Jun was also capable of healing. Gunshots, concussions, breaks, sprains and nosebleeds, Jun could lay his hands and mend anything. But this was a wound which he couldn't fix.

Desperation propelled them across galaxies. Frey suggested they buy their dream house, live quietly for the remainder of his days, and pass away in the arms of his lover.. but he knew that couldn’t happen.

Jun was stubborn.

Jun was out of his mind in love.

Jun would never give up on Frey.

So Frey carried on.

They raided hospitals, plundered medical facilities and kidnapped doctors. They sought out temples, consulted shamans, druids, priests, faith healers, anyone who claimed to heal, to help. But they all said the same. It couldn’t be cured. With each successive failure, Jun unraveled further. Every day his desperation manifested in volatile magical outbursts, his magic teetering on the edge of chaos. Frey noted with grim humour, he was the one who was dying, but Jun was burning away.

In his obsession, Jun grew reckless. He abandoned caution, neglecting to mask their ship's signature, choosing direct routes over concealed paths. So in the end, when a fleet of capital warships had them surrounded, Frey wasn't surprised in the least. He placed a weak hand on Jun's shoulder, as the other man began tapping into his magical core, to fight, to flee. Jun stopped, met his calm gaze. Frey gave a weak smile.

“Maybe, it's better this way?” He said, watching the boarding tunnel slowly descend towards them.

Jun's jaw tightened, a storm of emotions warring within. Then it softened, the tempest had passed, and he once more resembled the man Frey had fallen in love with.

"Your taste in home decor was atrocious anyway," Jun replied, a ghost of a smile playing on his lips. He pulled Frey into a fierce embrace, the two men holding onto each other as their last lifeline in the universe. Frey inhaled deeply, savouring the familiar scent of rhubarb.

As the warships closed in, Jun gave Frey one last kiss on the cheek. Drawing upon the depths of his being, he unleashed his Magic, a supernova of raw energy, a cataclysmic farewell that illuminated the void.
