In the dimly lit, repurposed garage which served as the base of their underground operation, Yunho sank onto their old ratty sofa with a sigh.

Stacks of boxes filled with surveillance equipment, forged documents, and various supplies were scattered throughout the space, barely leaving room for the worn-out sofa and a battered wooden table littered with blueprints and plans.

The dim, flickering light overhead cast eerie shadows on the peeling walls, where tattered posters of rock bands clashed with printed maps highlighting the city's most secure facilities. The musty scent of old books and dust permeated the air, a stark contrast to the high-tech surveillance gear that lined the walls, monitors displaying feeds from hidden cameras planted across the city. If a guardian were to walk in, there would be enough evidence here for instant execution.

He and Jongho had just concluded a quick debrief with Hongjoong, where they’d reported their day’s observations for the police force and guardians. It was surprising to Yunho just how emotionally draining it was, to pretend to be emotionless. He was glad of a break. He and Jongho weren’t due on shift until the next morning.

Jongho joined him on the couch, the strain in his eyes revealing the stress he was feeling, although the younger man would never say it out loud. Yunho gave him a weary smile and clapped a hand on his knee. They’d head back to their rented apartment soon.

The quiet moment however, was short-lived. The peace of the dimly lit warehouse was shattered by the blaring scanner, an old police radio they had repurposed for their own use. Its sudden, piercing alert jolted them into action, shattering the silence that had settled over their hideout. Jongho frowned, “Never a moment’s peace,” He grumbled, but Yunho shushed him, sitting up to listen to the tinny voice.

"Support needed. Sector 3 uncovered an underground fighting ring. Situation escalated, two casualties requiring an ambulance."

Jongho's brow furrowed. "You think Wooyoung and San…?" Yunho mirrored his concern.

"We should at least check it out."

Thankful that they hadn’t had the chance to remove their police attire, they grabbed their badges, and activating the squad car's siren, they raced to the scene.

Upon arrival, they found that the worst of the chaos had subsided, and the crowd had dispersed. Yunho approached an on-site officer and inquired, "What happened here?"

"Fighting ring," the officer explained. "Thugs pummeling each other for money. It drew a large crowd tonight, one of the fighters happened to be the son of a prominent figure. Thrillseekers. He’ll be detained and reprogrammed. Same for the man he nearly killed. We’ve apprehended nearly twenty people tonight.”

Yunho nodded in comprehension, struggling to keep his face blank. This was bad news.

Jongho elbowed him in the side and Yunho followed his gaze where a white van was parked up at the far end of the street.

“Thank you for the information.” He nodded to the officer and walked a short distance away to speak quietly with Jongho.

“That’s their van!” the younger man hissed, confirming Yunho’s fears that their two members were at the ring tonight. Had they been arrested?

“We need to wait a minute,” he murmured back. “Enforcers will be watching.” The two retreated back to their car to wait with bated breath for the enforcers to finish packing up their vans. Thankfully, the people who were cuffed and shoved in the back of the vans didn’t look familiar, giving hope that Wooyoung and San had escaped.

A tense hour later, Yunho felt it was safe enough to approach the white van. They got closer carefully, and Jongho knocked on the back.

Silence… Then,

“Fuck off!" It was Wooyoung.

Jongho whispered, "It's me!" There was a brief pause, then the door creaked open, revealing a grim sight. Wooyoung, pale, shaky with his shirt covered in blood. Jongho's eyes widened as he demanded, "What happened? Are you alright? Where's San?"

Before he could answer, Yunho pushed Jongho into the van, following behind and closing the doors. “Are you okay?” He asked, looking Wooyoung up and down.

Wooyoung glanced down at his ruined expensive shirt, and his hands which were stained brown, "It’s not mine." he confessed. "I fucked up."

Yunho looked around the van, terror building in the absence of their friend. One who would have never left Wooyoung alone in this state. He gripped Wooyoung’s arm and asked quietly, “Where’s San?”

Wooyoung wouldn’t meet his eyes, "He's at the hospital... He was one of the fighters tonight."

Yunho's confusion deepened. "What do you mean, one of the fighters? When we divided roles, it was agreed you’d arrange fights and bets, and San would be your backup."

Wooyoung nodded, "Yeah, but then we realised we could make more money if we didn't have to pay off a fighter. It was San's idea. He volunteered." His chin lifted with a hint of pride. "And he’s good at it too! Our earnings nearly tripled since he started fighting."

Yunho's frown deepened. "Does Hongjoong know about this? We're on the brink of infiltrating the Academy, and we can't afford to have San injured."

The other man sank his head again, moving his hand out of Yunho’s grasp to hug himself tightly. "No, nobody else knows. We thought we could handle it ourselves and that it wouldn't interfere with the main operation, we’ve been doing pretty well, just a few bruises here and there, but the guy tonight was something else. He was feral."

Jongho's eyes bore a mixture of concern and frustration. "That was really stupid. Didn't you think that it would only be a matter of time before he got really hurt?"

Despite his growing frustration, Yunho managed to maintain a calm demeanour. "Not now Jongho, Right now, our priority is San. What happened?”

Wooyoung's voice quivered. "The original plan was for San to participate in three rounds and then intentionally lose at the end. The other guy was some hotshot, we’d have made enough that San wouldn’t need to fight again! But then, something wasn’t right. The guy was on something. I should have called it off early, even if it meant losing the money. But I didn't, and then, when San went down, the other guy just wouldn't stop..." A choked sob threatened to escape, and Yunho pulled him into a hug.

"I tried to stop him," Wooyoung cried, "but that's when the police arrived. It was chaos...

I couldn’t move San, he wasn’t conscious and I couldn’t carry him…They were coming for us, I had to go." Tears welled up in his eyes as he admitted the worst, "I left him there."

Yunho froze. Frustration and terror welling up behind him. What could they do. He’d been worried that they’d been captured, but this was so much worse. San was seriously hurt, possibly dead. He zoned out for a second and came back to see Jongho clenching his fists silently. He knew Jongho responded to stress with anger and Wooyoung was already punishing himself. As the oldest, he needed to take charge, but they couldn’t do it alone. He took a deep calming breath.

“We need to let Hongjoong know. I know we agreed on radio silence for safety, but that’s past now. We need help. Let’s go back to your apartment and everyone can meet us there.” Wooyoung froze, and Yunho picked up on it immediately,

“What’s wrong?”

Wooyoung wouldn’t meet his eyes again,

“We uh, we left the apartment. We’ve been living in the van.” Before Yunho could speak again he said, “Hongjoong said we needed as much money as possible right? The rent was draining cash so it was cheaper this way, and you know, makes us harder to pin down.” He gestured to the mattress and piles of clothes, “it’s actually not that uncomfortable once you get used to it.”

Yunho pinched his fingers to the bridge of his nose and raised a hand before Jongho could say anything.

“Our place then. Come on, I’ll drive.” He clasped a hand to Wooyoung’s shoulder, “I won’t say it wasn’t stupid, but it’s going to be okay.”

Chapter Two

Wooyoung paced nervously in the dimly lit warehouse, his steps echoing in the tense silence that gripped the room. As Yunho and Jongho made the urgent call to summon the rest of the group, the palpable sense of urgency hung heavy in the air.

Seonghwa and Yeosang arrived first, their faces etched with concern. Nobody had told them the details of what was happening, only that it was urgent. Their eyes were questioning but Wooyoung shook his head.

A couple of minutes later the door burst open and Mingi strode in. “This had better be important.” He demanded, “This is putting everything at risk by us all being here.” He gave a silent headcount,

“Where’s San and Hongjoong?” He asked. Seonghwa and Yeosang watched curiously, eager to know the answer as well. Yunho bit his lip,

“Hongjoong will be here in a few minutes,” Mingi nodded, clearly waiting for Yunho to say more, when the older man didn’t say anything, Seonghwa, eyes wide, prompted,

“And San?” Wooyoung worried at his nails. Yunho replied,

“We need to wait for Hongjoong,” Mingi scowled,

“Where is San?” He demanded, louder. He moved up until he was in Wooyoung’s space. “Whose blood is that!?” His voice cut through the anxiety-filled atmosphere like a sharp blade.

Wooyoung hesitated for a moment, then, swallowing hard, he admitted. "We need to wait for Hongjoong," his voice cracked on the last word. Silence hung in the air like a heavy weight, Suddenly he was beset by noise as Mingi, Seonghwa and Yeosang all spoke up at once demanding answers.

The cacophony of emotions threatened to spiral out of control until Hongjoong's arrival.

When Hongjoong walked in, a hush fell over the room, and all eyes turned to him. Mingi had Wooyoung’s collar in a tight grip.

“Put him down Mingi.” Hongjoong said calmly. He wasted no time and directed everyone to the table where they sat, stood or perched. “You wouldn’t call us together like this for nothing, Yunho. What’s the matter?” He looked around, silently doing a headcount, then his mouth curved downwards and he looked at Wooyoung.

Haltingly, Wooyoung recounted what he had told Yunho and Jongho. Mingi growled and Seonghwa’s knuckles were white as he gripped the edge of the table. Yeosang stared down, lost in thought as he likely imagined hundreds of outcomes. Hongjoong didn’t move, but his mouth stayed set in a frown.

“...And then these two came to the van.” Wooyoung finished, picking at a bit of skin on his nails until it bled. He sat tense, expecting a verbal blow from Hongjoong, but to his surprise, Hongjoong's response was different.

Their captain’s voice was steady as he said, "Okay, we need to be clear on the facts here. San is either in the hospital, the reprogramming centre, or the morgue." His words hung in the air, heavy and foreboding. Wooyoung flinched, his heart sinking. He knew he wasn't the only one grappling with the possibility of San being gone, but having the idea given voice was painful.

Hongjoong continued, "We need a plan. First, we have to find out where he is. The hospital is most likely, and most preferable, so we’ll check there first."

He turned to Jongho and Yunho and asked, "Do you have any IDs or credentials that can help us gain access?"

Wooyoung felt confused. Where was the castigation? Why wasn't Hongjoong putting him to the lash for what he'd done? He'd expected to be punished by their leader, who was normally quick to scold.

Jongho nodded.

Unable to contain his anxiety any longer, Wooyoung shot up from his seat, his voice edged with urgency. "I need to go too," he declared, his eyes fierce. "I need to get San."

Hongjoong half-shook his head, initially about to refuse, but something in Wooyoung's expression must have changed his mind. "Alright," he conceded. “Given what you’ve said, he’s likely too injured to be sent to the reprogramming centre, but that could change at any time. Go quick, get in and look around. If he’s fit to move, get him out, if not, get yourselves out. Don’t take chances, you hear me?”

As Wooyoung changed out of his shirt Hongjoong stepped in close, and began helping with the buttons. His eyes bore into Wooyoung's, filled with a mix of concern and sternness.

"I need you to be careful," he warned in a low voice. "We don't know what we're walking into at the hospital. There may be an armed guard on him. Keep your head down, stay out of trouble." Wooyoung opened his mouth to respond, but Hongjoong held up a hand, silencing him. "There's time for flagellation later. I know why you did it, and I can't say it wasn't a mistake, but punishing you won't get San back. We need you to be okay." He pulled Wooyoung into a hug, holding him close. Wooyoung finally let the tears fall.

The hospital was a labyrinth of sterile corridors and hushed conversations. Jongho and Wooyoung had taken precautions to blend in. Jongho had donned a white lab coat, holding a clipboard as he walked briskly and with purpose. Wooyoung had chosen the role of a visiting family member, carefully keeping his face blank as he followed.

After discreetly flashing Jongho's forged ID badge to access restricted wards, they began their search. The hospital was sprawling, and they needed to be careful not to draw any unwanted attention.

They continued their search, peeping into wards to look for a familiar face.

However, each dead-end they encountered added to their growing anxiety. The hospital was teeming with patients and staff, making it difficult to narrow down their search.

As they approached the end of another hallway, Wooyoung spotted a nurse's station with a computer screen displaying patient information. He pulled Jongho’s sleeve,

“Jongho, look!” The younger man followed his gaze, and nodded. There was only one nurse on duty, with a shared glance, the two men knew just what to do.

Wooyoung approached the nurse, remembering which department was furthest away from their current location., “Excuse me, I’m a bit lost... I’m looking for the phlebotomy department. Can you help?” The nurse nodded and began recounting directions through the labyrinthine hospital while Wooyoung feigned increasing cluelessness. She eventually drew him a map which they both leaned over, Wooyoung subtly positioning them both so her back was to the terminal. With lightning fingers Jongho leaned over and searched for new admissions to the trauma unit.

Seconds felt like hours as the computer processed the request. There! An unknown subject had been processed into the hospital three hours ago. Jongho closed the window and stepped away and around the corner, flashing Wooyoung a quick thumbs up. Wooyoung smiled at the nurse, took the hastily drawn map and left.

They finally made it to the hospital room on the top floor, Wooyoung’s heart pounded with a mix of fear and relief. Relief that they’d finally found San, fear about what condition he was going to be in.

They turned the corner into the room and there, unconscious on the sterile white hospital bed, was San. The man, normally so full of life and energy, was terrifyingly still.

He was pale, nearly as white as the bleached bandage wrapped around his head. His black hair was shorn on one side, and the right side of his face was swollen and discoloured purple and green. The webbing of bandages continued on his chest and disappeared under the blankets. The heart monitor attached to his finger tip beeped consistently. A shiny pair of manacles encircled his left wrist, locking him to the rail.

He was alive.

However, the sight of his best friend cuffed to the bed, attached to a web of machines sent a shiver down Wooyoung's spine.

A surge of feelings overwhelmed him, and a sob wracked his frame as he staggered to San's bedside. Unbidden, tears streamed down his cheeks.

“Oh San,” Wooyoung sobbed, “I’m sorry!” But there was no response.

Wooyoung leant forward and rested his head on San’s hand, softly pleading for him to wake up.

Jongho, ever the pragmatic one, assessed the situation quickly. His eyes fell on the medical chart at the foot of the bed, and he grabbed it, looking it over as quickly as he could.

“Is he okay?” Wooyoung asked, it was a foolish question, clearly he wasn’t okay. Jongho frowned and pursed his lips.

Jongho opened his mouth to reply but footsteps approached from outside. His eyes darted to the door and Wooyoung felt a surge of terror. He knew what Jongho was going to say and he wasn’t ready to leave yet. Not so soon after finding San. He shook his head and gripped San’s hand tighter, shaking him,

“San! Wake up, wake up please!” Wooyoung begged.

Jongho’s voice was a hushed, urgent hiss as he spoke, "We can't stay here. San's in no condition for them to move him yet, but we have to go."

It was the second most painful decision he’d ever had to make, and Wooyoung's heart ached as he tore himself away from San's side, squeezing the unresponsive hand once more before letting go. They couldn't afford to be caught here, and they needed time to plan their next move. With one last, lingering look at San’s unmoving form, Wooyoung followed Jongho as he darted out of the room, leaving San behind for the second time that night.

The hospital corridor felt cold and unforgiving as Wooyoung followed behind Jongho to the exit, their footsteps echoing with the weight of their unspoken fears. They had seen San, confirmed his condition, and now they had a mission to rescue him.

They would come back for him; they had to.

Back at the dimly lit warehouse, the group huddled together to formulate their rescue plan. Once Wooyoung and Jongho confirmed San’s location, Hongjoong’s mind had gone into overdrive. This was where their captain excelled and Wooyoung watched feverishly as Hongjoong outlined his plan. It wasn’t perfect, but time was not on their side, not if they wanted to retrieve San before he was well enough to be sent to the reprogramming centre. Wooyoung glanced at the clock. 6am. It had only been 8 hours since this nightmare started, but it felt like days. His eyes itched and he could see the tension and exhaustion on the rest of the team’s faces, but they wouldn’t give up or rest, not until San was back with them.

Each member knew their role, and the tension in the room was palpable. Mingi, their resident distraction expert, was tasked with creating chaos outside the hospital. He would draw the attention of law enforcement away from the hospital.

Yeosang was to hack into the hospital's computer systems and disable the video cameras. He was also going to trigger alarms at different points within the hospital to disguise their real target.

Hongjoong, their sharpshooter, would find a vantage point in a nearby building with a clear line of sight to the corridor. He’d mapped the escape route using servicing corridors and a service elevator which lead to an underground garage where Seonghwa would be waiting with an escape vehicle. He hoped they wouldn’t need sniper cover, but it was always better to prepare for the worst.

Before separating, they stood in a circle, each consciously aware of the gap created by their absent member. Hongjoong looked each of them in the eyes. “We’re going to bring him home.” He promised.

With renewed determination, Wooyoung followed at a careful distance as Yunho and Jongho, both wearing their officer uniforms strode through the hospital corridors. He felt the chain cutters poking into his hip under his oversized shirt as he retraced their steps to San’s room. They were going to bring him home.

However, when he reached San's hospital room on the top floor, his confidence was shattered.

The bed was empty. The IV stand lay toppled on the floor, and there were traces of blood on the sheets. The heart monitor wailed a constant unending drone.

Panic seized Wooyoung, and the room felt too cold, too empty.

"He's gone," Yunho whispered,

"By himself?" Wooyoung asked, his mind racing to comprehend the situation. “We thought they wouldn’t take him yet!”

"I hope so," Yunho replied with a sense of urgency. "Anyone taking him won't have his best interests at heart. We need to find him."

Just as the gravity of the situation sunk in, another alarm pierced the air, and a masked enforcer appeared at the door.

"Who are you?" he demanded, reaching towards his hip for a laser rifle.

Jongho acted swiftly, dashing forward knocking the enforcer unconscious before he could reach hsi weapon. There was no time to waste.

Yunho urgently radioed Hongjoong, his voice laced with desperation. "Hyung, he’s not here! Tell me you see him!"

Hongjoong's reply was quick but filled with concern. "What do you mean? There's commotion—" His voice cut off abruptly, leaving Wooyoung with a sinking feeling that things were about to get even more complicated.

Chapter three

The excitement in the air was palpable. The crowd roared louder than he’d ever heard. Tonight was a real exhilaration. Surrounding the square ring were hundreds of people, yelling, sweating, cheering, but San only had eyes for one man. Wooyoung, huddled in the corner wearing his custom vibrant shirt. He gave San a wink, their code for everything was going well. That meant he’d had a good run of men placing bets. Against him, against San.

His opponent tonight was a relative unknown, Wooyoung called him Posh Boy as that was the only defining feature from the young man who wanted to play at being a fighter. Nobody expected him to beat The Mountain. The crowd were hungry for blood, hungry to see a well-to-do man get beaten to the ground.

There’d be many people disappointed. The agreement was to go the distance and then San lose at the end. That way people wouldn’t realise it was fixed. San knew how to pull his punches just enough to not end the fight too soon.

The ringing bell brought him back to the match at hand. One last match and they could stop for a while, could earn enough money that they could take a break. San exhaled slowly, faced the man in front of him, and lifted his fists. Just one fight, and then he and Wooyoung could go back to their van, order greasy take out and sleep. He could get through this no problem…

However, two minutes into the fight, San knew something was off. His opponent, the "posh boy," was moving strangely. He was supposed to be another nobody, an easy win on a normal day, but his movements held an air of unpredictability. San furrowed his brow, wondering if this was just a new tactic or if something more sinister was at play.

The crowd's deafening cheers and roars echoed in his ears, but he couldn't let the excitement distract him. He had a job to do, a performance to deliver. He had to make it look convincing, but he also needed to protect himself. It was a delicate balance.

As the fight unfolded, San cautiously observed his opponent. The young man's eyes were wild, his punches erratic, he was genuinely trying to hurt San. Left hook, right hook, dodge, swing.

The plan was to go the distance and then lose, not to face a man who seemed genuinely eager to inflict pain.

The first few rounds were a blur of punches, dodges, and close calls. San had to adapt quickly, changing his strategy to defend himself without making it obvious. He couldn't afford to let his guard down, but this wasn’t going the way he expected. The crowd's frenzy only intensified, their bloodlust growing with every exchange of blows.

In the middle of the ring, San's mind raced. He needed to signal Wooyoung, to let him know that something wasn’t right. He’d never felt nervous midfight, normally so confident in his own ability, but this young man was far stronger than he looked. Amidst the chaos and the oppressive gaze of the spectators, getting Wooyoung’s attention discreetly was an impossible task.

A painful punch to his ribs sent a shockwave of pain through his body, and he stumbled back. The crowd erupted with noise, their voices blending into a cacophony of rage and frenzy. San clenched his teeth, the pain fueling his determination to make it to the final round. This was the last fight.

In a brief lull in the action, he glanced at his partner, who was still watching from the corner with gritted teeth. He hoped Wooyoung would understand the urgency in his eyes. He was at real risk of getting hurt, could Wooyoung find a way out of this dangerous situation? San knew that the next punch could be even more devastating, and he couldn't afford to take any more chances.

The bell rang, signalling the end to the fourth round. One more to go. San's body ached, each blow etching a painful reminder on his skin. He knew he had to endure a little longer, just a few more hits, and he could let this act come to its scripted conclusion. The thought of a break, of the upcoming rest and spicy dumplings, fueled his determination. He could do this, just a few more hits and then he could go down, could let it end. Something dripped down his face and he wasn’t sure if it was sweat or blood. His eye was starting to swell and each breath was a stab in his side. Then, a cool stream of water splashed on his face, and he knew it was Wooyoung. His partner's eyes held both concern and a reassuring smile.

“You holding up, Sannie?” He asked, a smile belying the concern in his eyes. San wasn’t going to give up now.

“Doing just fine.” He wheezed.

Wooyoung squeezed his shoulder and rallied the crowd, shouting, "You got this, fuckin’ floor him. Who's the Mountain?"

“I’M THE MOUNTAIN!” San thundered, feeling hyped again. The crowd roared with him as he staggered to his feet, ready for one last round. He already knew the outcome, normally faking a loss was tricky to be believable, but in this one, he knew he’d welcome the respite.

His opponent, Posh Boy, was in a similar battered state, and something in his eyes sent shivers down San's spine. There was an intensity, a burning hatred, that went beyond the normal fighting adrenaline. Sanity seemed to hang by a thread, and the look in the man's eyes was unsettling. The hatred and the thirst for blood were all too real.

San couldn't let his guard down; he had to see this through to the end.

The fifth round began, and the deafening roars of the crowd echoed through the arena. San and his opponent circled each other, battered and bruised, but with a renewed intensity. He ducked a wild punch to his left, countered with a precise jab to the ribs, and then swept his leg in a quick kick that landed solidly on Posh Boy's knee. The surge of adrenaline was accompanied by a jolt of pain as his own knee slammed into the unforgiving tarp. It was a costly mistake, one that his weariness couldn't afford. As he struggled to rise and regain his composure, he noticed a flicker of commotion beyond the baying crowd.

A guardian.

Overriding his self-preservation instinct, which told him to never turn his back on an enemy, San turned to warn Wooyoung. He didn’t see the crushing fist that connected to the side of his head. Pain seared through his skull, and he fell heavily to the side, disoriented and aching. The world spun around him, and his vision blurred as he tried to comprehend what had just occurred. His eyes locked onto his partner’s. Wooyoung looked scared.

Another hit to his chest this time. San was confused. He was down. It should be over. It should be over. There was a guardian, they needed to go. He needed to warn Wooyoung.

Crack.

Another impact to his chest. Posh boy wasn’t stopping. Gasping for air, San curled his body defensively, attempting to protect his battered face. He needed to get up, to warn Wooyoung of the danger.

It was a race against time, but his body felt heavy, unresponsive.

A boot landed forcefully on his torso, knocking the breath from his lungs. Agony radiated through his chest, and he curled to protect his organs. He needed to warn Wooyoung, who was now rushing toward him, terror etched across his features.

‘Get up!’ his mind screamed to himself, but his body was slow and unresponsive.

The cheers of the crowd changed tempo. Sudden shrieks. Panic. Another kick to his head this time. Get UP San. Get out.

He tried. His limbs were boneless. His vision was tunnelling. The screams of the crowd were quieter, fading, replaced by a tinny high pitched whine inside his head. Wooyoung was still here. He needed to flee. San tasted copper at the back of his throat. Wooyoung, get away. He had to tell him. Run away! San’s body lay still, his vision dimming, and the cacophony of the crowd grew distant.He stopped being aware of the abuse raining down on his body from his opponent.

Crack… Wooyoung, please…

Darkness.

San's consciousness danced on the fringes of reality, submerged in a surreal world of disjointed sensations. The sounds of sirens and distant voices permeated the fog that enveloped his mind. He was cold, he hurt. He couldn’t breathe. Where was Wooyoung!

With his heart jackrabbiting San thrashed out. He couldn’t scream, something was in his throat.

"Stay with me," a stranger’s voice urged. "We're here to help." Voices spoke to him, spoke around him, he couldn’t comprehend more. A flush of cool liquid washed through his veins and San faded away.

“San! Wake up, wake up please!”

“I’m awake…” San mumbled through a haze of pain and confusion. His parched lips struggled to form the name, "Wooyoung," and he tried to reach out to ensure his partner's safety. But there was no response, and panic began to gnaw at his weakening resolve. “...’ooynng’” There was no response. San’s eyes were leaden but Wooyoung was calling to him. He needed to make sure his partner was okay… He cracked his opens open to slits.

His brow furrowed as he fought against the seductive pull of sleep, he needed to find Wooyoung. He turned his head slowly, searching for any sign of his partner, but the sterile hospital room offered no answers. He was alone.

With a herculean effort, San focused on the present, each breath a battle, each movement an excruciating challenge. He needed to find Wooyoung. There had been a guardian!

The hum of medical equipment filled the room, and the rhythmic beeping of a heart monitor echoed in the stillness. Tubes and wires snaked from his body to various machines, monitoring his vital signs. His chest was wrapped in bandages, and the sterile smell of antiseptic hung in the air. San tried to lift his hand but a cold weight tethered him to the bed.

He was handcuffed.

San's heart began racing, the monitor beating a staccato rhythm next to him. Where was Wooyoung?!

Something had gone terribly wrong, he needed to find Wooyoung. Had the guardian snatched him? Was he now going through reconditioning? What did that mean for San? How had he been spared going to the reconditioning centre? Groaning as the pain in his head began overcoming whatever painkillers were in his IV, San sobbed in frustration, he tried to wipe his tears but the cold metal handcuff tugged at his left wrist, rendering it immobile.

He needed to get out of here. He needed to get out of this handcuff.

Panic and frustration swirled within him as he desperately fought through brain fog and pain to come up with a solution to the steel restraint.

The hum and beep of medical equipment caught his attention and San shifted his gaze to the IV stand, its metal frame standing resolute beside his bed. A glint of inspiration illuminated his mind.

He needed to act, to escape these handcuffs and find Wooyoung. He needed to let the team know what happened and rescue him from the Reconditioning Centre. San couldn't afford to waste another moment. With renewed determination, he focused on the IV needle attached to his arm.

As he reached for the needle, the pain in his head served as a painful reminder of the ordeal he had endured. With trembling hands, he carefully detached the needle from the tubing, wincing as the tape securing it pulled at his skin. It was a fragile, makeshift tool, but it was his only hope. Yeosang was better at this sort of thing, but he’d insisted that everyone learn how to pick locks. San was grateful he’d paid attention to the lessons.

San turned his attention to the lock on the handcuffs. The needle's slender form seemed inadequate for the task at hand, but he had to try. He inserted it into the keyhole, his heart racing as he probed the mechanism. His fingers, weakened by the brutal fight and the drugs in his system, worked with painstaking precision.

Minutes passed like hours as he wrestled with the lock. The faint, rhythmic beep of the heart monitor provided a haunting accompaniment to his efforts and he felt every jagged twist and turn of the needle.

Suddenly, footsteps echoed on the tile floor outside his room. San froze, not daring to breathe until the footsteps receded. He needed to go. He refocused his efforts on the lock.

Then, in a moment of tense anticipation, the lock clicked. San's heart skipped a beat as he realised he had succeeded. The handcuff fell away, clattering to the side of the bed. Carefully, he leaned across and switched off the heart monitor, then bit by bit detached all the clips and tags attached to his body. Blood splattered as he carelessly discarded

He slowly sat up and had to pause as his vision went black.

“Come on, San,” he muttered angrily. He didn’t have time for weakness. He had to find Wooyoung. He swung his legs off the bed and stood up.

San’s body however, was still reeling from the drugs and abuse it had suffered. He fell, face first onto the cold hard floor. Pain jolted through his cheek and his face felt sticky and warm. With a ragged sob, San allowed himself a few seconds for despair to overwhelm him as hot tears dripped onto the floor to join the blood. Then, resolutely he struggled to his knees. Every second he wasted was time Wooyoung might not have.

Gripping the side of the bed, San climbed to his feet. Breathing heavily, he dug deep within himself for strength. He could do this. He took one step, then another. Then he straightened.

He could do this. Wooyoung needed him.

Gritting his teeth, San opened the door to his hospital room, and left.

Chapter Four

The corridor was sterile and white beyond San’s room. Tentatively he looked left and right, but thankfully there were no staff in the vicinity. Gripping his side, which felt like broken ribs he staggered to the window facing out to the city. He felt another short stab of despair when he saw the vista of the city below. It told him two things, one was that he was on a high floor of the hospital, which would make leaving a bit trickier as he had further to go, and two, it was nearing dawn, the sun was peeking beyond the high rise buildings. Things would start to get busier soon. He worried, he must have been in the hospital for quite a few hours at least, he hoped that it was the same day. That way he’d have a chance to find Wooyoung.

Spotting a sign for the stairwell, San moved carefully, a blend of anxiety and relief accompanying his steps as he didn’t encounter any staff.

However, fortune proved fickle. Upon swinging open the double doors to the stairs, San's eyes widened at the sight of a Guardian in the stairwell. Without thinking, adrenaline surged through him, propelling him into swift action. Without a moment's hesitation, he dashed forward and collided with the Guardian, sending the imposing figure over the railing and crashing down the stairs.

Peering over the railing, the resounding thud of the Guardian hitting the floor far below drew the attention of onlookers. Four faces, clad in Enforcer attire, stared back at him, accompanied by the ominous presence of a second Guardian who began making their way up the stairs.

What do I do? What do I do!? San thought desperately. He couldn’t go down. He turned to go back into the corridor where his room was, but a quick glance in the glass pane of the door showed staff coming down the corridor. He had no choice but to go up.

Panicked and with no time to spare, San raced up the stairwell to the roof, gasping with the exertion. As he burst onto the rooftop, he quickly assessed his surroundings. The first light of dawn painted the cityscape in hues of orange and pink, and the cool morning air stung his face.

The Guardian would be following him soon. He needed to think of something quick. There. He spied a loose metal pipe. It’s small and nowhere near strong enough to do big damage, but it was the best he had with no time. He scanned the roof for the fire escape that he hoped existed. There! At the far end! He dashed towards it, but he was exhausted and the pounding in his head amplified. He staggered. Then hands grabbed him from behind.

San yelled, turning to grapple with the faceless being trying to take him down. This wasn’t a fight he could win. Even at full strength Guardian’s were strong. There was something not human about them. They were powerful, emotionless and weakened as he was, he stood no chance. He tried anyway, twisting and straining to pull away from the being but the grip on his arms was vice-like, no matter how he tried to get free he couldn’t.

The Guardian forced him down to his knees and withdrew a carbon steel baton from its belt. San knew what was coming. One strike meant reconditioning. Two strikes were death. He closed his eyes and braced for the killing blow. I’m sorry, he thought sadly. The rest of the team would never know what happened to him, no one would know what happened to Wooyoung…

POP.

Thud.

The blow never came. San opened his eyes. The guardian was lying on the ground behind him, with a blossom of blood in his chest. The baton had rolled out of his limp grasp. He was dead. Somebody shot him. But who?

Hope sprang to life in his chest and San clambered back to his feet. There. On the opposing roof, a figure and a glimmer from a sniperscope. Hongjoong!

Hongjoong was here, and that meant the rest of the team was here! He wasn’t alone. San hadn’t dared to hope that there’d be a rescue. He could have cried with relief. How had they known? Could it be that Wooyoung had escaped?

He let out a whoop of joy. Hope bloomed within him, all he needed to do was get off this roof and everything would be okay.

San startled when a loud noise began wailing behind him. A siren. “Oh no,” he muttered. He bent to pick up the baton from the dead guardian then had to pause when he saw stars. A banging caught his attention. It was the door to the roof. Three more guardians emerged. Hongjoong wouldn’t be able to get them all.

San turned and ran.

“Hongjoong?! Hongjoong? What do you mean there’s commotion? What’s happening?” Wooyoung demanded into his earpiece. Through a speaker in the corner, a loud blaring siren began a constant wail. Yunho peered out of the room in a panic.

“We can’t stay here.” He shouted.

“I know that!” Wooyoung spat, terror overriding his emotions. What could they do? Where was San? His earpiece crackled, it was Yeosang.

“San’s on the roof. There’s been an alert issued for an assault on a guardian and escaped aggressor. There are guardians coming in force. You need to leave.” Wooyoung was already sprinting, Yunho close behind, his long legs covering the distance easily.

“We’re not leaving without San!” Wooyoung promised.

“Hurry.” Hongjoong said, his voice etched with worry. “There’s guardians behind him! I took one out just in time, but there’s too many. San needs you!”

Wooyoung didn’t think his feet could run any faster, but he proved himself wrong. Together he and Yunho burst through the double doors to the stairwell. There were footsteps below and above. Yunho cursed and Wooyoung followed his gaze beyond the railings. There were at least half a dozen enforcement officers coming up the stairs. How had it gone so wrong so fast? Feet pounding, they headed up towards the roof, praying they’d get there in time.

Wooyoung's mind raced with worry for San. He couldn't shake the fear that they might be too late, that the Guardians had already taken him down. They needed to reach the roof swiftly, but the steps seemed to resist their urgency, stretching endlessly upwards. The footsteps swarming below them seemed too numerous.

Finally, they emerged onto the rooftop, greeted by the first light of dawn painting the city in soft hues. The scene before them was chaotic. Three white clad Guardians were in front of them heading towards the edge of the roof. One of them had a bloodied arm. Before they could comprehend anything further a gunshot echoed and the Guardian fell to its news.

“Move it!” Hongjoong yelled in their ear, “I can’t get them all in time!” That’s when Wooyoung saw him, San, clad in his hospital gown, battered and bruised, staggering towards the edge of the roof. Next to Wooyoung, Yunho withdrew his firearm. It was low calibre, and was going to be much less effective than Hongjoong’s rifle. He raised the weapon but cursed, “I don’t want to risk hitting San!” He shouted. He ran forwards to try and get a better angle.

Wooyoung sprinted. He passed the body of a Guardian next to a small bit of pipe. Not realising it was the one that San himself had held earlier, he reached down and grabbed it, then continued running for the guardians bearing down on his best friend.

“SAN!” He screamed, swinging the pipe wildly connecting with the broad shoulders of the nearest Guardian. It stopped walking, then turned towards Wooyoung. Frantically Wooyoung swung again, feeling the pipe impact on the broad chest, but seeing no evidence of hurt on the Guardian. In his earpiece Wooyoung could hear Hongjoong screaming,

“What are you doing?!” But he couldn’t reply as a strong hand clasped around his throat, cutting off his air and raising him off the ground. There was a clank as the pipe fell from his grasp as he panicked and clawed at the hand choking him.

San couldn’t see, grey spots were filling the edges of his vision, his breath was ragged and his skull pounded with every heartbeat. The adrenaline coursing through his veins was running out and with Guardians in pursuit he was simply delaying the inevitable. Hongjoong wasn’t going to get them all. He was going to die.

But he wasn’t a quitter. He was going to make them work for it. He staggered towards the edge of the roof, towards the fire escape. He had to make it. A gunshot blasted behind him, then another. Hongjoong was doing his best.

“SAN!” Wait. That was Wooyoung’s voice. San turned clumsily and saw Wooyoung and Yunho running towards the remaining Guardians pursuing him. In mounting horror he watched Wooyoung attack one of them, only to have it turn around and grab him by the throat, lifting him clear off the ground. The second Guardian was heading towards Yunho, who was standing firm and offloading his pistol into it. The small calibre bullets didn’t so much as stagger it, the body armour was too thick. San choked out a warning but it wasn’t heard, as he saw the third Guardian, previously staggered from Hongjoong’s rifle, had gotten back to its feet and grabbed Yunho from behind.

San looked at the baton clasped in his shaking hand. He had to do something. He took a step forward.

Suddenly, an intense white light flared ahead of him. He staggered to his knees clutching his eyes, as his head throbbed with agony.

He heard yells. Footsteps running past him. Screams and shouts. A familiar voice yelled “Wooyoung!” Amidst the pain pounding behind his eyes San recognised that voice as Mingi’s. He groaned, trying to get back onto his feet. A hand touched his shoulder and he recoiled.

“Easy,” Seonghwa’s calming voice said in his ear. “We’re gonna get you out of here.”

“Woo-!” San said through gritted teeth, hanging onto consciousness by a fraying thread. Seonghwa pulled him closer,

“Jongho’s got him,” He said, “Don’t wo-” but the rest of Seonghwa’s words faded as a high pitched whine engulfed San’s hearing. Dimly aware that his legs had betrayed him, San's nerveless fingers released the baton, clattering as it hit the ground. His head lolled to one side, and a sense of weightlessness consumed him. He would have hit the ground but arms wrapped around him. Seonghwa was frantically calling his name. He wanted to answer but he was fading…fading…

San opened his eyes. He was in a bed in what looked like Yunho and Jongho’s garage. Yeosang was sitting beside him typing away on his favourite computer. His face was set in a frown. He noticed San was awake and offered a smile. He spoke but San couldn’t make out any words. San closed his eyes…

San opened his eyes. He saw Yunho and Mingi crouching around a tiny white table in the corner. Their faces were furrowed deep in concentration as they played a card game. As he watched, Mingi threw his cards onto the table in frustration and Yunho gave a bright laugh. He looked up and saw San. Shouting something, both Yunho and Mingi jumped to their feet and crowded San’s bed. They talked to him excitedly. San blinked, blearily, and closed his eyes.

San heard singing, a soft ballad that he recognised as his favourite. He opened his eyes. Jongho sat beside him, lost in emotion as he crooned softly. He noticed San and the singing abruptly stopped as he began peppering San with questions. San felt vaguely sad, he was enjoying the song… He closed his eyes.

San opened his eyes. There was a bustle in his room. Seonghwa was sweeping the floor. There was a big plastic bag full of wrappers and empty paper cups. He turned to San and his eyes lit up with relief. He came over to San and tenderly placed the back of his hand to San’s forehead. It was blessedly cool. San leaned into the touch and closed his eyes.

San opened his eyes. He felt a warm hand clasped in his. He looked down and saw a painted nail. He followed the hand up to the arm, and then up to his Captain’s face. Hongjoong was watching him, an odd broken expression on his face. He said San’s name. San didn’t respond. As he closed his eyes again, he saw a tear drip down Hongjoong’s cheek.

San opened his eyes. Wooyoung was reclined beside his bed, arms folded and eyes shut. His face was drawn, cheeks pale and sharp. San frowned, Wooyoung had lost weight, and he had so little to lose in the first place. He reached out to touch Wooyoung’s hand and the other startled awake.

“San?” He asked warily, San offered a small smile.

"You're awake?" Wooyoung asked, San looked at him in confusion,

"Why wouldn't I be?" He rasped, wondering if maybe he was still asleep. At his response, Wooyoung's expression brightened.

"You're awake!" He shouted, San scowled,

"Clearly I am." He said,. Wooyoung laughed, a peal of happiness that brightened the room, he jumped forward and clutched San's hand in his.

"Welcome back Sannie," he grinned, "You've woken up a few times now and simply stared at us like a zombie... This is the first time you've said anything!"

If anything, San was more confused.

"How long have I been asleep...?" Wooyoung sobered up, he ran a hand through his hair which was greasy and unkempt, a sure sign of worry. Even living in a van the man made sure his hair routine was maintained. He must have been worried.

"You've been out of it for three days. We were getting really scared, brain damage, you know... Yeosang said you just needed the rest." San lifted his hand to his own head, gingerly touching the side of his hair where previously it had been agony, the pain was still there, but muted. Wooyoung watched him with concern, "Does it hurt?" He asked, San slowly shook his head.

"I'm okay, I think. I'm sorry for worrying you." Wooyoung scoffed, startling San. He raised an eyebrow in question.

"You're sorry? God, San..." He paused, with alarm San noticed the other was crying. "I'm sorry!" Wooyoung cried, "I'm sorry for this whole thing, for making you fight, for leaving you when the Guardian came, for not getting back to you fast enough! We were nearly too late. If the others hadn't arrived when they did..."

"No, it's okay," San said quickly, "Woo, you didn't do anything wrong. I agreed to the fights, remember? And I wanted you to run when everything went wrong. I thought you'd been taken to the Reconditioning centre... I was so scared." He took a deep breath, wincing only slightly as his ribs creaked in protest. "I'm so glad you're okay." He reached up and brushed a limp bang away from Wooyoung's eyes. Wooyoung sniffed and clasped his hand above San's.

"Oh San, " He said, "Never thinking about yourself," San laughed breathlessly,

"Would always rather think about you." He winked, then looked down at the makeshift bed he'd woken up in. "This isn't the van?" He questioned, Wooyoung looked sheepish.

"The cat's out of the bag... The rest of the team know what we've been up to, the fights, the van." He said, San made a face,

"It was going to happen eventually." San said, "Does that mean we can't go back to the van?" Wooyoung shook his head,

"We've been banned I'm afraid." He grimaced, "Everyone has given me a full scolding individually about how we went about things... You're lucky you missed out on it. If you thought Hongjoong’s scolding was bad, try facing Seonghwa's disappointed face." San winced in sympathy.

"That's a shame." He said, "Sleeping in such close quarters meant I got to use you as a pillow." Wooyoung paused, a mischievous glint in his eyes, then gave San a wicked smile.

"That bed you're on looks pretty cramped, I reckon two people can’t fit on it." San grinned in response. Mindful of his ribs, he carefully shifted over to one edge, then patted the side next to him.

"Come here."

In the Heat of Combat

Things were looking up. They had a purpose.

Slavers. People to liberate. A reason beyond wanton destruction — beyond the hollow question of could versus should that had been haunting Jun for days. Who were they to decide who lived and died? Where was the justice in that?

But here. Here was justice with a clear face. Rescue the gnomes. Do something good. Maybe scrape a little of the debt off his soul.

He and Frey were pressed together inside the tank — a three-person vehicle with two people operating it, which meant a constant tangle of reaching over, ducking under, hands brushing the same levers a half-second apart. It should have been chaos. Somehow, it wasn't. Frey anticipated him. He anticipated Frey. They lurched forward in the same breath, and Jun seized a dwarf in the claw arm while Frey slammed them sideways into two more.

Good. This was good. Who needed Brian Styles and Star? They were handling it.

Then a dwarf across the field pressed a pickaxe to a gnome's throat.

Jun's mind went cold and quick. Four more dwarves on the field. Too many gnomes in the open. If hostage-taking worked once, every one of them would try it — and they couldn't protect all of them. They couldn't.

He made a call.

He turned the tank away. Let his body language read I don't care. Targeted the dwarf in front of him and swung the arm hard.

The sounds outside were muffled through the hull. He still heard it — the soft, terrible weight of a body hitting the ground. And then Frey's sharp intake of breath beside him, like something puncturing.

Shit. They'd called his bluff. He pushed down everything that tried to rise in his chest and focused. End it fast. End it before anyone else—

Frey vanished.

Jun still felt the ghost of him — the warmth that had been a constant pressure at his side for the last hour — and then it shifted. The door release clicked from an invisible hand, and Frey was gone. Out into the field, alone, without a word.

"Frey—?"

A pickaxe swung at his skull. Jun dropped below it, the blade ringing off the interior hull. A dwarf was inside the tank. Then a second. The space was too small for them to wind up properly, which was the only advantage Jun had — he kept moving, kept using the cramped geometry, but he was exhausted. The javelin wound from earlier screamed with every breath. He could feel the wrongness in his lungs, the wet rattle. His hands came away from the wall flecked red.

He couldn't fight like this.

Where is Frey?

He pushed the thought down. Frey had made a choice. People made choices in combat. That was— that was fine. That was fine.

Where is Star?

Where is Brian Styles?

How could Frey leave him?

The pickaxe came again. He twisted, felt it graze his shoulder.

He had enough left for one, maybe two spells. He could teleport. He could leave, and the dwarves would take the tank back, and all of this would have been for nothing. Or he could stay and bleed out in a metal box while two dwarves took turns trying to kill him. They would succeed before anyone could arrive to help. He was alone.

Jun was alone.

Frey had left him.

The idea arrived fully formed and immediately stupid.

If he couldn't keep the tank, then no one could.

Jun closed his eyes — just for a moment, just long enough to find the shape of it — the bulk, the weight, the heavy curl of tusks and the deep drum of a heartbeat larger than his whole chest. He reached for it.

The transformation took him like a wave. His body expanded into something enormous, and the tank screamed — metal peeling, seams splitting, rivets firing like bullets into the walls. Jun roared with it. He felt himself exceed every boundary the hull could offer and kept going, because the magic didn't stop for steel.

The dwarves screamed.

And then they didn't.

The tank folded outward in a shriek of tortured metal, and a mammoth stood in its wreckage, sides heaving, blood from the earlier wound still matting the fur beneath one great foreleg.

Jun shook his massive head.

Frey. He needed to find Frey.

Jun stepped back, “I don’t think that’s such a good idea…” He said carefully, Frey tossed back his gleaming hair, and his soft red lips smiled wide.

“Am I not attractive enough for you like this?” He stepped into Jun’s personal space, making the other man step back, clutching his broom to his chest like a ward.

“That’s not it,” He said, “but, you know, our stations are so different… What if there’s repercussions?” Frey licked his lips and leaned in close, stealing a soft kiss.

“What about them?”

…

“Oh, I am not going to hear the end of this.” Frey groaned from the window of his locked tower. Down below the Kingsmen had built a pyre, which they were tying a struggling, screaming Jun to. Witchcraft they’d called it. Seducing the crown prince. They’d burst into his room that morning, dragging a bleary eyed Jun from their bed and holding Frey back, “It’s for your own good Your Highness” they’d apologised, before locking the door.

Down below, they’d succeeded in securing Jun to the centre post before the King passed his judgement.

As the flames began to lick at Jun’s feet and he screamed, Frey considered the drop from his window. About 80 feet give or take. That should be enough. Desperate to stop hearing the screams of his beloved he sat up on the windowsill, facing his royal chambers, and pushed himself backwards.

Over the hundreds of lives they shared, there were always some similarities, some patterns.

For example, Jun was terrible for sacrificing for Frey. At last count, he had taken 5 bullets, and 3 swords meant for Frey, he had pushed the other out of the way of a dozen moving vehicles, and had been bitten by a zombie, a werewolf, a hungry cougar and even a rabid raccoon (that one had not been pleasant.)

In return, Frey had prevented countless incidents by taking out 7 would-be assassins, three riotous villages, two witch-hunts, and had rescued Jun from several pyres, and even one attempted cannibalistic ritual.

They had learned, through trial and error, that when one died, the other rarely lived longer than a month. The sudden loss, the void in their soul when the other perished, was unbearable. They wilted and lost the will to continue. When Frey died first, Jun would grieve, he’d write beautiful dirges, create sculptures and memorials and ensure that Frey’s presence remained in the world. When Jun died first, Frey would make the world regret. He would burn and bury anyone responsible and make sure they knew that this was the greatest mistake they could have ever made.

The first time it happened was a genuine mistake. A split second to slow to react and the Vampire was on him. He was slammed into the wall, knocking the breath from his lungs and he was sure he felt a rib break. He swung his arm down with his silver dagger, desperate to recover some control over the situation, but a strong grip shoved his arm back, and his dagger fell from his grasp.

He squeezed his eyes shut, not wanting to see, waiting to feel the fangs pierce his skin, but nothing happened.

A roar, a whistle of wind, a weightlessness as the body on him was flung to the side. Jun opened his eyes cautiously and saw a second demon with white hair and gold horns atop the first, ripping it's throat out with sharp claws.

Not wasting a moment, seeing that the hunt was not going his way, Jun fled.

The second time a vampire got the jump on him, he wasn't even expecting a hunt. He was just out getting a hotdog before dusk fell, when an ambitious vampire pulled him into an alley. Same again, the white haired vampire took out the first. Jun reached into his back pocket for his knife, ready to engage. The white-haired vampire snarled at him and vanished up the wall.

The third time, Jun was testing a hypothesis. The vampire in front of him was new, weak. She couldn't have been more than a year old, clumsy and aggressive in her attack. He could fight her off easily, vampire hunts like this were pretty much routine by now. Against his own better judgement he was curious to see if the white-haired vampire would appear again. Once was a coincidence, twice was unlikely, but three times? Three times meant there was more going on.

The vampire screamed and dashed for him, rather than sidestepping Jun let her collide and they both fell into a wall. She wasn't strong enough that he was in any danger, and his hand was coolly gripped on his knife. He waited.

Sure enough, there was a whistle of wind and the young vampire was thrown to one side, her neck torn out faster than he could see. However, Jun made a move to push off the wall; he was shoved roughly back, and a new body pushed against his.

The white haired vampire.

Jun hated vampires. He knew what they were, monstrous abominations. Abberant creatures that killed with no remorse. Inhuman. He was trained and conditioned to end them on sight.

But this creature pressed close to him. This couldn't be a vampire. He was... beautiful. Delicate features on rose pink skin, long soft eyelashes framing almond-shaped eyes... and the eyes, they were completely obsidian, but they glittered, and when a lithe hand reached out to grasp his throat he whispered,

“Oh…” The onyx eyes widened in recognition, before the hand dropped and the vampire stepped back. Jun lowered the dagger he’d been pointing the at the vampires sternum,

“Well, this is awkward...” Frey said.

They didn’t realise at their first Meeting that they were meant to be together. In fact, it took months of adventuring before Jun considered looking past the manipulative bard to see him for who he truly was, a kind and caring soul with an ironclad mask. And for Frey, he was attracted to the blue skinned sorcerer who wore his heart on his sleeve, but it wasn’t until they’d experienced horrors and nightmares together that he could touch Jun’s depths and see something more. They slew dragons and monsters together, saved villagers and fought gods, and when, in their cottage, holding each other in their marriage bed, Jun kissed Frey’s aged skin, held his frail hand, and made a Wish that they could do it all over again.

The crew of the Leviathan had embarked on countless amazing adventures among the stars, but today was different. Today, Frey was having a terrible day.

It all started when the star-routes he’d been working on had been accidentally deleted by the ship's AI. His frustration grew when the leftovers he’d been looking forward to for lunch had mysteriously disappeared. Then the zip to his favourite flightsuit tore, and he couldn’t find an alternative anywhere. To top it off, the electronics in the cargo bay had failed, leaving Frey with hours of tedious repairs or else condemned to darkness.

By the time Frey trudged back to their quarters, his rosy skin was tinged with a deep shade of purple, a sure sign of his frustration. Jun, who had been reading on the bed, sensed Frey's turbulent emotions and decided it was time to act.

With a gentle smile, Jun approached Frey, wrapping his slender arms around him. "Bad day?" he asked, his voice soothing and calm..

Frey slumped into Jun's embrace, feeling a wave of relief wash over him as he melted into the warmth of his lover's arms. "The worst," he admitted, his tail flicking restlessly behind him.

Jun kissed Frey's forehead and pulled him to their bed. "Well, we can't change what's happened, but we can make the rest of the night better."

As he spoke, he waved his hand, summoning a holographic projection of a starry night sky. It shimmered and twinkled with the beauty of distant galaxies and nebulae. Frey's eyes widened in awe.

Jun continued, "I thought we could spend some time together under the stars, right here in our own little corner of the universe." The side of his mouth curled up and he stroked a finger down Frey’s arms.

Frey's heart began to lift as he gazed at the holographic night sky. "That sounds amazing," he whispered, before his mouth met Jun’s.

As the hours passed, Frey's worries and frustrations melted away like distant asteroids burning up in a planet's atmosphere. He felt the warmth of Jun's love, the beauty of the universe, and the magic of the moment.

Later, underneath the holographic stars, with Jun sleeping by his side, Frey realised that even on the worst of days, there was always a bright and beautiful moment waiting to be discovered. This love was his constant, his guiding star in the vast expanse of space. Frey smiled, kissed Jun’s perspiration covered cheek and closed his eyes.

“Phew! That was a close one… Star said that if they’d been a metre to the left they’d have hit the flux capacitor.” Frey flung himself to the bed and began the long process of unlacing his boots. “He reckons we’ll need to make port to restock our fuel rods soon. The shields have taken a bit of a beating and are really sapping our supplies. Be nice to be planetside for a bit, don’tcha think?” he tossed one boot to the side and began on the second, “‘course, not sure which planets would be best. Obviously we should avoid the busiest ones, but Aurora isn’t too far, and they have the best spirits. Do you think if we’re careful we could go and rent a hotel room with a built-in karaoke… Jun?”

Jun hadn’t moved from the door. “Jun, are you listening?”

Jun stood ramrod straight, hands fisted and jaw clenched. He was staring resolutely at the floor, clearly not listening to a word Frey had said.

Frey got to his feet and approached,

“Jun, what’s wrong? Did you get hurt?” He reached for Jun’s hand but Jun snatched it out of reach.

“A close one.” Jun muttered quietly.

Frey raised an eyebrow, “Yeah, but it missed. No harm done. We’re all okay.” Jun pointedly looked at the deep mottled bruise forming on Frey’s cheek, where he’d fallen onto the console when the ship had been jolted. Frey touched it, “This?” he asked, “it doesn’t even hurt Jun, I’ve had worse waking up after a long night with you!” Clearly, it wasn't the right thing to say. Jun recoiled.

“I can’t keep doing this.” He said, and Frey felt an insidious sinking in his stomach. His heart skyrocketed as he struggled to comprehend the meaning.

“Doing what?” He asked warily. Jun gestured angrily ahead of him.

“This!” He snapped, “It was a close one this time, but what about next? Or the one after that!?”

“Then, we’ll deal with them.” Frey reasoned. “Fizzy showed me some blueprints of some shield enhancements. We’ll just spread the budget around so she can get the parts..”

Jun scowled, “That’s not enough. They’ll just get bigger guns. We’ve been lucky so far.”

Frey nodded, “Okay,” he said carefully, “Then we’ll lay low for a bi-”

“Thirty million credits!” Jun interrupted. “Thirty. Million.” He laughed bitterly. “There’s no chance we can lay low. The bounty on my head is high enough to buy a whole fucking spaceship. There’s no laying low. Not with half the universe looking to gain from this. It’s just a matter of time before one of them succeeds and you get caught in the crossfire.”

“What are you saying.” Frey asked cautiously. Jun looked at him, his eyes red rimmed and tense.

“What if I killed them all?” Jun asked flatly. Frey took a deep breath. Dangerous territory.

“You said you didn’t need to go down that road anymore.” he said, “...You said that you didn’t want to be that person anymore. You don’t have to be.” He reached again for Jun’s hand, and the elf let him take it. “Jun, I don’t want you to be that person anymore.”

The elf exhaled heavily, losing some of the tension.

“Okay then,” He said, and before Frey could sigh in relief, “-then I have to leave.” Stunned, Frey shouted,“What?”

Nodding in conviction, Jun withdrew his hand and strode to his wardrobe and pulled out a carrier duffel. “I need to leave.” He repeated. “As long as I’m here then bounty hunters will just keep coming.” Stuffing clothes in, Jun didn’t look at him.

“Then I’ll come with you.” Frey insisted. Jun shook his head, and Frey spit, “Bullshit, don’t say no. If you’re leaving, I’m leaving with you.”

Jun continued packing without looking at him,

“I’m leaving to keep you safe.” Frey angrily swiped the bag, tossing it to the floor. Creased shirts and trousers tumbled out. Jun gave him a doleful look.

“Don’t make this harder than it is.” He said, recoiling as Frey’s hand struck him across the cheek.

“Don’t be fucking stupid.” Frey said angrily, “We’ve only just got each other back. You spent YEARS looking for me, and now you’re what? Throwing it away? You don’t get to decide to leave.”

Jun touched the pinking mark on his cheek.

“I can’t lose you again,” he said quietly. “If you get hurt because of people coming after me, I just- I couldn’t bear it.”

“Well tough!” Frey shouted in his face, “And what? You think that just because you’re not on the ship anymore it’ll stop people coming for us? Thirty million credits, you said it yourself! They’ll use us to get to you. Don’t you think we’ll have a better chance if you’re actually fucking with us!” Tears sprung to his eyes and he rubbed them away. Jun looked at him in horror.

“You’re right…” Frey exhaled, he stomped over to the duffel on the floor and threw it roughly into the wardrobe. “Of course I’m right. Of all the dumbass ideas you’ve had.”

Jun didn’t move. “I’ll publicly turn myself in. No bounty, no issue.” Frey closed his eyes. He turned slowly to face his lover. “Don’t do it.”

Jun wasn’t listening. “I mean, that’s what the bounty’s for… to bring me to justice.”

“Don’t do it.” Frey repeated softly, but Jun continued, lost in his own thoughts.

“I’ve done crimes. I’ve killed… It’s only right that I be punished.”

“Please.” Jun met his gaze, his eyes were determined.

“It’s the only way,” Jun said, Frey shook his head, his cheeks were wet, his face hot.

“Don’t leave me. Please. I’m begging you.” He said, pitifully. Jun approached and went to cup Frey’s face but Frey slapped his hand away. “Don’t do it.” He said again.

“I’m sorry.” Jun replied.

And then Frey was alone in the room.
