"No. Absolutely not." Star walked around the table and sat down heavily. The ship was titanium and wouldn't have shifted an inch under full thrust, but Jun could have sworn the floor shook.

"Oh, please, Star," Frey wheedled. Jun had never seen him this earnest about anything. "It'll be so much fun, it's an easy job, and you'll have a good time, and pleeeeeeease." He dragged the last vowel out until it was nasal and unbearable. Star's scowl deepened.

"You're forgetting some major drawbacks," she said, counting them down on her fingers. "One, we have no way in. These shows are invitation only. Two, we don't have instruments. Three, we don't know how to play the instruments we don't have. Four, is it really a good idea to draw this much attention to ourselves?"

Frey grinned like he'd already won. Jun watched him keenly.

"Excellent, Star. Are those all your objections?" Star stared at her raised fingers, suddenly unsure, hunting for a fifth.

"One!" Frey pulled out his commpad. On it was an advert for The Sparrows' Debut Performance, alongside caricatures of what Jun could only assume was the crew. "Eddie already got us invitations." Fizzy and Brian Styles leaned in and nodded approvingly at their cartoon likenesses.

"Two!" He dove under the table and dragged out, with a scrape and a groan, a large rectangular crate. "Remember that big crate I bought on Commfour? Eheh." He flipped the clasps. The lid sprang open on two guitars and a keyboard.

"The drum set is already in my room," Brian Styles said. "I have been practicing."

"Three! Covered." Frey began handing out instruments. "I'm lead vocals, because I am clearly the best singer." Jun looked at the guitar in his hands and plucked a string. Nothing. He glanced at Frey, confused.

"Props," Frey said. "Twang them all day, nothing happens. We're running a backing track, so nobody actually has to play."

"Except me," said Brian Styles. "I have been practicing."

Fizzy hummed thoughtfully, crossed to the crate, and lifted out the keyboard. "Can this one work?"

Frey nodded and flicked a switch on the main display. The keyboard hummed to life. Fizzy pressed one tentative finger to a white key, and a clean note rang out. Then she set both hands down and played, something beautiful and absurdly technical. The others stared. Frey wore a look of almost manic glee. When she finished, Fizzy looked up and smiled.

"Gavin enjoys music, it seems."

"That leaves four," Star said flatly, though Jun could tell her resolve was cracking. The enthusiasm was contagious, and she clearly hated being the one to hold the line.

"Four!" Frey said. "The more attention we draw to the band, the less we draw to the actual scheme."

"This leaflet lists us as sorcerers," Brian Styles noted, with some concern.

"Exactly! That's the gimmick. What kind of idiot would openly claim to be a sorcerer?"

Jun said nothing, but raised an eyebrow.

"Five," Star tried, though even she seemed to hear how thin it sounded. "What happens when someone asks for a second song?"

"We refuse an encore," Frey said, without missing a beat. "Very rock and roll. Very mysterious. Sorcerers don't do encores."

"That's not a reason, that's just..." Star stopped and pressed her fingers to her temple.

"So can we do it?" Frey begged.

Star looked around the table: at Fizzy admiring the keyboard, at Frey's wide, plaintive eyes, at Jun's smile, and finally at Brian Styles, who had apparently kept drumsticks in his cloak the whole time and was now tapping out a quiet beat on the tabletop.

"I'm choosing my outfit," she said at last.

Jun felt nervous. That wasn't unusual. He felt nervous most days, an ingrained habit from a lifetime on the run, hiding from enemies he never saw. But this was a new kind of nervous. Thankfully, he wasn't alone with it.

Backstage, fingering the strings of his guitar, he was intensely aware of the revealing clothes Frey had insisted on. One of us has to show some skin, and you're so pretty, Jun!

Beside him, Fizzy kept fiddling with her braid, working so many strands loose from its ribbon that she'd ended up looking frazzled and rock-and-roll without meaning to. Even Star, who could walk into a room and make everyone in it aware she was in charge, couldn't hide the sweat beading at her hairline. She was still barking orders, but her usual certainty had dimmed a shade. Brian Styles hadn't let go of his drumsticks once, tapping a staccato rhythm against his thighs.

Only Frey seemed at ease. He strolled into the cramped green room greeting the stagehands like old friends, somehow already knowing all their names. Jun's breath caught when he saw him. Frey had tousled his hair and accentuated the bioluminescent freckles scattered across his face, and was that lip gloss? He still wore his full-body spacesuit, but now it was strung with belts, buckles and, inexplicably, glitter.

He crossed to Jun, winked, and laid a reassuring hand on his arm.

"You going to be okay?" he asked quietly.

Jun breathed in. His nerves must be showing. He looked down at the guitar he didn't need to play but had practiced anyway, then toward the muffled hum of the crowd settling in. They'd rehearsed. They sounded fine, he thought. But the lights, the noise, the sheer number of people overwhelmed every instinct he had to stay hidden and unnoticed. This was a different kind of danger, and Jun didn't yet know its shape.

"Jun?" A thread of worry had crept into Frey's voice. Jun realised he hadn't answered.

"I'm okay," he said, with a smile he hoped reached his eyes.

Frey's hand slid down his arm and took his. His fingers were cool. Jun hadn't noticed how hot and damp his own had become.

"You're going to be amazing. If you get nervous, just look at me, okay?" Frey swallowed hard enough that Jun caught it. Jun nodded. He could do that.

"Two minutes!" the stage manager called. Beyond the curtain, the first notes of the intro Frey had arranged began to play.

"LET'S DO THIS!" Star roared, whether for the crew's benefit or her own, Jun couldn't tell.

Frey squeezed his hand tightly, and Jun squeezed back, concentrating on his breathing as Frey let go and walked toward the stage as if he'd been born on it.

Jun straightened his collar, tugged his shirt down a fraction to show a little more chest, and followed him out.

Light. Sound. The bass hit him before he even saw the crowd, a pulse in his sternum, in his teeth, in the soles of his feet through the floor. Heat rolled off the lamps in waves, thick with sweat and ozone and something electric he couldn't name. The guitar strings bit cool into his fingertips, and none of it mattered, none of it made a sound, and somehow that made it easier. He couldn't get it wrong. He could only feel it.

Frey sang.

A born performer, a rock star, sweat glistening at his temples as he sang his heart out with pure, unguarded joy. And Jun got swept up in it. The current took him before he could think to resist. He jumped. He grinned so wide his face ached. He ran to the microphone and found the lyrics already waiting in his mouth, memorised by accident from a hundred rehearsals of Frey belting them out in the dining room. His voice cracked on a high note, and nobody cared. Nobody could even hear it.

The crowd was a wall of noise and light, faces blurring into one roaring shape. He couldn't pick out a single person, couldn't tell friend from stranger from threat, and for once that didn't frighten him. It felt like flying. It felt like the opposite of hiding.

Colours blurred. Time compressed and stretched in the same breath. His lungs burned, his throat went raw, his legs kept moving without being told.

Later, Jun wouldn't remember the setlist, or the size of the crowd, or whether they'd hit a single note right. He wouldn't remember walking offstage. What he would remember was the pink flush high on Frey's cheeks, the stage light caught on his smiling lips, and the half-second when Frey turned and locked eyes with him across the chaos, still singing, singing like he meant every word for Jun and no one else in the room.

Backstage, the set was done. The crowd had roared, and the crew of the Starling had performed as if they'd done this all their lives, rather than after two weeks of practice and a good deal of experience pretending to be something they weren't.

Jun was exhausted. He staggered to a flimsy wooden chair and dropped into it, then pulled the guitar strap over his head and let the instrument clatter to the floor. His blood sang.

Around him the others flopped into chairs in various states of collapse. Fizzy's hair was plastered down with sweat, but she looked relieved. The stage manager came in and quietly drew Star aside for a word. Frey dropped down next to Jun and grinned at him between gulps of water.

"Amazing," he said breathlessly, his voice rasping from all that singing. "Jun, it's a shame we're only doing the one set. You looked incredible up there."

Jun felt heat climb his cheeks, but before he could answer, Star's voice cut across the room.

"We're getting paid how much?!"

The next day, the crew gathered in the galley for a debrief. Most of them were still buzzing about the show. Only Brian Styles seemed to remember the actual goal: extracting the Books from the venue, whatever other nefarious business it got up to between legitimate shows.

Star stood at the head of the table, frowning, and waited until everyone had a coffee in front of them. Jun had made them all; he'd been voted, unanimously, the best at it, even by Brian Styles, who had not and could not taste. Then she pulled out a chair and perched on its back, boots on the seat.

"I had a talk with Desmin after you all left last night."

"First-name basis, huh?" Frey whispered to Jun, grinning.

"The one show earned us more than the last three jobs combined."

The crew whistled appreciatively. Frey looked like the cat who'd got the cream.

"I told you this was a good idea!"

Star nodded. "Which is why I've agreed to six more shows."

The room went quiet. She looked, for a moment, a little less sure of herself. "What? The ship needs a new air recycler. It's starting to smell like farts."

"So. Six more shows," Frey drawled, lounging along the back of the comm panel. Jun looked up from his book and idly checked that Frey hadn't pressed any buttons.

"Hmm," he agreed. He was at a really good bit: the lead was about to confess his feelings to his romantic interest. Then a tail whipped down and pushed the book into his chest, hiding the page. Jun shot Frey an annoyed look, but Frey was grinning devilishly, eyes sparkling.

"I saw you up there, you know," Frey said. Jun raised an eyebrow. "You loved it. Loved the attention, loved having all eyes on you."

Jun clicked his book off and set it aside. "They weren't all on me. We're a band. They were watching everyone."

Frey slid further down the panel until his upside-down head was practically in Jun's lap.

"They were watching you, Jun. You were divine."

Then, with a dexterous flip, he catapulted backwards out of the deck.

Jun stared at the doorway for several minutes. When Frey didn't come back, he sighed and picked up his book again.

The air recycler was ordered before the credits had even cleared. The rest of the money, Star decreed, would go on "professional development," a phrase she pronounced like it tasted faintly of engine oil.

"Real instruments," Frey translated, delighted. "She means real instruments."

"I mean the props are embarrassing," Star said. "If I'm going to stand in front of a thousand people and pretend, I'd like the pretending to at least be accurate."

She took the second guitar. Within a day she was holding it like a weapon she was still deciding whether to trust, glaring at the fretboard as though it owed her money.

Practice happened in the galley, because the galley had the best acoustics on the ship and the coffee. Fizzy taught scales with the patience of someone who had, at some point, been taught them herself, though when Jun asked, she only smiled and said Gavin had opinions about fingering. Brian Styles hammered the drum kit in the cargo bay, a perfect metronome with no groove whatsoever, until Frey sat beside him for three afternoons saying "looser, looser, feel it, no, looser," and one evening the beat finally swung. Brian Styles stopped mid-fill and stared at his own hands.

"I have been practicing," he said, very quietly, like a man discovering religion.

Jun learned in the evenings, cross-legged on the floor of the comm room with the guitar in his lap and Frey's tail curled loosely around his ankle, which was apparently just where it liked to be now. Frey corrected his grip with cool, patient fingers. Three chords became four. His fingertips went hard and sore and then hard and fine, and one night he strummed something that was unmistakably a song, and Frey whooped so loudly Star yelled from three rooms away.

"Sorry!" Frey yelled back, not sorry at all.

The second show was in a converted cargo hangar, all steel beams and fog machines. Jun's guitar was live this time, and he could hear it, thin and slightly behind the beat but there. Every time he found the right chord, something small and fierce lit up in his chest.

Star played through the whole set with an expression of grim concentration and hit every note. Afterwards, in the green room, she stared at her hands and said, "Huh," in a voice so soft that Fizzy pretended not to hear it.

Halfway through the second chorus, Frey held the microphone out toward him, one eyebrow raised. Well?

Jun hesitated. He'd been mouthing the words for two shows now, and this time the backing track was quieter, someone had been nudging the vocals down. He stepped in and sang the line with Frey.

It was small. A half-verse, no more. But when their voices met, something in Frey's face went bright and startled, and he grinned at Jun over the mic like he'd been handed a gift.

The crowd screamed. Jun looked at his shoes, then back up, and found Frey already looking at him. He smiled.

By the third show, the backing track was down to a whisper. Frey had cut it back by degrees, show after show, until the band was mostly carrying itself, and nobody had said a word about it, as if saying it out loud might make the spell break.

Fizzy's solo drew a wave of applause so loud it cut her off. She looked genuinely surprised. Brian Styles kept the beat steady and warm, and twice Jun caught him throwing the sticks in the air, catching them with the same finesse he did in combat. Star had started to prowl the stage, hair whipping, throwing shapes with her guitar that Jun suspected she'd practiced in the mirror and would deny under oath.

And Jun sang. He didn't decide to. It just happened, the way the current had taken him that first night, except now he knew how to swim in it. A harmony under the chorus. A line traded back and forth with Frey, mid-bridge, Frey's voice high and bright, Jun's lower and steadier, the two of them wound around each other. On the last chorus he found himself on the edge of the stage with Frey's shoulder pressed against his, both of them leaning into the same microphone, and the crowd was a single roaring thing and he was not afraid of it.

Frey turned his head. Their faces were very close. He was sweating and flushed, freckles glowing faintly in the stage light, and he didn't sing the next line, he just looked at Jun, then at the microphone, then back, with the ghost of a smile.

Jun knew what he meant. Now?

He smiled back. Now.

They came in together on the last line, perfectly on the beat, and let it ring out over the crowd.

The lights went out. The audience shrieked for more, and somewhere in the dark Jun heard Star mutter, "No encore, no encore, sorcerers don't do encores," like a mantra.

Backstage, still laughing, still shaking with adrenaline, Frey caught his eye across the crowded room. Neither of them said anything.

They didn't need to.

It started, as most disasters did, with Jun trying to look up how to play a bridge in a minor key.

He'd typed the band's name into the search bar to see whether anyone had posted a tutorial for their own set list. Instead, the book gave him a page of results he didn't understand. There were tags. There were word counts. There was a small, cheerful icon that said Mature Audiences.

"Someone's written about us," Jun said aloud, before his brain had caught up with his mouth. "There's a whole... they're stories, Frey, there's hundreds of..."

Frey's head appeared over the back of the couch so fast it was almost a jump cut.

"Fanfiction?" His eyes went enormous. "Oh, Jun. Oh, we've made it."

"I haven't read any of it yet."

"That's fine, that's wonderful, that's what the crew is for." Frey vaulted the couch, tail whipping, and was already yelling down the corridor. "GALLEY! EVERYONE TO THE GALLEY! BRING SNACKS! THIS IS NOT A DRILL!"

Five minutes later, they were assembled. Star had coffee, Fizzy had a blanket, and Brian Styles had pulled out a small notebook and a pen, which he clicked with grave professionalism. Jun sat at the head of the table clutching his book with the expression of a man about to defuse a bomb.

"Right," Frey said, rubbing his hands together. "Read the first one."

Jun scrolled to the top result and cleared his throat. "'Sparrows in the Night, chapter one.'" He read the first paragraph in silence, and then the second. His ears began, slowly, to turn pink.

"Out loud, Jun."

"I don't think I... I really don't think I should."

Frey plucked the book neatly from his hands, scanned the screen, and his eyebrows climbed steadily toward his hairline. "Oh," he said, delighted. "Oh. Okay."

"What?" Star demanded. "What is it?"

"Let's try another." Frey swiped. Read. Swiped again. His grin widened by degrees. "Interesting. Let's go with this one."

He swiped a third time. A fourth. By the fifth, the galley had gone very quiet.

"They're all like this," Frey said. "Every single one. Every story is..." He gestured vaguely at the air, at the general concept. "It's all smut."

"There is a surprising amount of erotica written" Brian Styles observed, tapping his pen against the notebook, "in such a short time."

"We've been famous for less than a month!"

"Yes. That is what I find impressive. It suggests dedication."

Jun put his face in both hands. "There's a tag system."

"Ooh," Fizzy said, leaning in. "What are the popular pairings?"

There was a pause. Jun spoke into his palms, very quietly.

"Sorry, what was that?" said Frey, who had clearly heard.

"It's us," Jun mumbled, peeking out between his fingers. "Top pairing is... us. Me and you. By a lot."

Frey stared at him. Then he pressed a hand to his chest, and Jun watched, fascinated, as the tips of his freckles glowed a soft, unmistakable pink.

"I... well," Frey said, and for once seemed to have nothing to add.

"What about me?" Star demanded, leaning across the table. "Who am I with?"

Frey scrolled. "Uh. Everyone, mostly. There's a lot of variety."

Star barked a laugh, loud enough to make Fizzy jump. "I would crush any of you. I would kill you with my thighs."

"Some of them seem to be aware of that," Fizzy said, staring at her own commpad. "That's the plot of a few of these."

"Good. Correct. Respect the thighs."

Brian Styles cleared his throat. “I have seen online that facsimiles of humans can be purchased that are anatomically suitable for these sorts of endeavours.”

There was a long, ringing silence.

"Some of them," he continued, "seem to have moving parts and audio output."

Fizzy made a small strangled noise into her blanket. Star put her forehead down on the table and shook with silent laughter. Frey, meanwhile, had gone completely still, staring at the screen reading intently.

"What?" Jun asked, alarmed. "What is it? Is it worse?"

"No, it's..." Frey turned the book around to show him one line, and Jun read it, and immediately wished he hadn't. "It's incredibly well written!"

Brian Styles wrote something in his notebook and underlined it twice.

As Jun turned to peer at what Brian Styles’ could possibly be writing he almost missed Frey clicking ‘bookmark’ on the highest rated fic called, “Wings”. Aghast, he turned to look at Frey who only winked.

Although Jun’s cheeks were magically blue, he was sure they’d turned a bright pink.

The show went well, of course, each time the venues getting bigger and brighter, the crowds getting louder. They were viral Jun had heard someone say. And it was fun, until it wasn’t.

The stage door was a mistake. Jun understood that the moment the stage manager pushed it open and the noise hit them like a wall.

Nobody had mentioned a crowd. The venue had a proper back entrance, a loading dock and a cordon of bored security, but the cordon had been a suggestion, not a barrier, and now there were at least two hundred people pressed against the rails, phones held aloft like tiny lanterns. Someone had a banner. Someone had painted the Starling's hull on a bedsheet, slightly wrong.

"Oh, they like us," Fizzy said, sounding faintly alarmed.

"Keep moving," said Star. She'd pulled her hood up and was already cutting a path through the crowd, elbows loose, the way she walked into every room she had no intention of losing. "Smile, wave, don't stop. Ship's forty metres."

It was fine, at first. It was even nice. A girl thrust a marker at Brian Styles and he signed her arm with such solemn precision that she burst into tears. Someone shouted a proposal to Fizzy and she blushed to her ears. Jun kept his head down and his hands in his pockets and felt, distantly, that the roar of it was almost bearable.

Then the faces started to separate.

That was the trouble. On stage they'd been a blur, one great warm animal. Up close they were individuals: a boy with a bruise on his chin, a woman crying openly, a man holding his phone at Jun's face from six inches away. Jun counted exits without meaning to. He had forgotten he was technically a fugitive, but seeing all these people left him feeling incredibly vulnerable.

"FREY!"

The scream came from the left, high and ragged and utterly without shame. Frey turned toward it, already smiling, his hand halfway up in a wave, and a young elven woman broke under the rail and threw herself at him.

She got both hands on his sleeve first.Then his chest. Tackling him to the floor. Frey was stunned.

"I love you, I love you, I've been to every show, I know you, you know me, you looked at me, you looked at me—" She reached for the zip on his spacesuit…

Frey made a sound Jun had never heard from him. It wasn't a shout. It was small and thin, the kind of noise a person makes when the floor drops. His whole body locked. His tail went stiff, and the freckles across his face flared a hard, panicked white, so bright they cast shadows.

Something hot and bright moved under Jun's skin.

It came up through his chest and down his arms and gathered at his fingertips. It would be so easy. A push, a flicker, and she'd be on her back ten feet away, and Frey would be free. His hand had already begun to lift.

Two hundred phones.

Every one of them was pointed at this spot. Every one was recording. Somewhere in the back of his head, the old voice, the one that had kept him alive for a lifetime on the run, said very calmly that this was exactly the sort of thing his enemies were looking for.

Jun closed his hand into a fist. Biting his lip, trying to force the magic down.

Then Star was there. She had turned around at the first scream and marched forward. She picked up the girl by the scruff of her neck and threw her to one side.

“No.” She shouted, her voice cutting through the noise. “No touching. We are leaving.”

Jun dashed forwards and helped Frey to his feet. The tiefling was trembling and Jun put an arm around him. Frey leant into him.

“Just look at me,” he murmured, “You’ll be alright Frey.” Head down, Frey silently nodded. Feeling Brian Styes and Star flanking them, the crew made their way to the ship. As they broke away from the crowd, Jun turned and saw the elven woman, standing, staring at him with an expression of hate.

Nobody spoke for the first ten minutes.

The galley was too bright and too quiet. Jun made coffee because it was something to do, and set a cup in front of Frey, who wrapped both hands around it and didn't drink. Fizzy draped a blanket over his shoulders without a word. Brian Styles sat with his drumsticks in his lap, motionless, which was somehow worse than the tapping.

The fanfic still sat open on Jun's comm on the counter. Several hours ago it had been the funniest thing that had ever happened to them. Now he looked at it and felt faintly sick. Somewhere out there, hundreds of people knew Frey's face and thought they were entitled to the rest of him too.

Star had been standing at the head of the table with her arms folded, quiet for once. When she finally spoke, her voice was flat and level, the captain's voice.

"We’re contracted for six, that was number five. We finished the job. We take the money, we fix the ship, and then we disappear." She looked around the table, meeting each of their eyes in turn. "One more show?"

"One more show," Frey echoed. He sounded very tired, and very young.

Jun reached over and, slowly, giving him time to pull away, laid his hand over Frey's on the table. Frey didn't move it.

Outside the hull, muffled by metal, the crowd was still chanting.

The warm-up for their last show felt different.

The band gigs had been fun. They were a break from the usual jobs, the ones that involved subterfuge, danger and inevitable explosions, and a chance to build a different set of skills. They were good at it, and people loved them. But Jun had always known it couldn't last. There was the scrutiny, and the risk that someone would realise he was a sorcerer. There was Fizzy's father, who might work out which side of the universe she was hiding on, and Brian Styles' maker, who might come to claim his property, and the countless people they'd stolen from. It had been a reckless stint, and the girl at the stage door had proven it needed to end.

In the mirror, Frey was carefully tousling his hair, fronting as best he could. But Jun saw how his eyes flicked toward the door every time the crowd roared. He'd enjoyed it, but he was glad this was the end. They would vanish into the night with mostly fond memories and a ship that smelled of lavender.

"Two minutes!" the stage manager called.

Star whistled, and the crew drew into a huddle around her. She looked at each of them in turn, and her gaze lingered on Frey.

"This is the Sparrows' final performance. Let's make it memorable."

"Aye, captain!" they shouted, and then they were on stage.

Straight away, Jun felt something wrong. A twinge between his shoulder blades, as though someone were standing too close behind him. The lights were bright, the familiar drumbeat rolled in, and he shook the feeling off. He put on a big smile and let his fingers find the chords he'd practiced over and over, the somatic shapes of the song, more muscle memory than thought.

He glanced at Frey, who was beaming and singing like he was having the time of his life. Frey turned and winked, inviting him, once more, to share the mic.

Jun stepped toward him and felt a jolt. Pain, a rush of heat in his shoulder, like he'd been rammed with something red-hot. He wondered, idly, whether he'd got too close to the electrics.

Then he saw Frey's face. The horror in his eyes, the colour draining out of it, said something was very wrong.

Distantly, Jun was aware that the music had distorted and stopped. The lights had changed angles. They were above him now. He was on his knees. The fire in his shoulder was spreading, and he moved his neck sluggishly to look down.

That was a lot of blood.

Arms wrapped around him. Frey swam into his vision, shouting, but Jun couldn't hear a word. At the edge of his sight, Brian Styles sprinted across the stage and launched himself off it in a swan dive into the crowd. There were screams, then another gunshot. Someone grabbed Jun under the arms, and he added his own voice to the noise.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry! Jun, we have to move you, we have to get you off the stage." Star sounded stressed. Jun sagged in her grip. Frey had hold of his hands.

"Come on, Jun, you'll be fine, you'll be fine." His voice was cracking. Funny, Jun thought. It never did that until the end of a show, and they'd only just begun.

"My guitar..." he mumbled, trying to see where he'd dropped it.

Fizzy stood in the middle of the stage with a very large gun in her hands, shouting orders at the crowd. Where had she kept that?

He followed her gaze and saw Brian Styles with his arms locked around a young elven woman who was screaming, though Jun couldn't make out the words. Frey looked over, and he swore.

"I guess," he said, shakily, "we were just too good at our jobs."

"No. Absolutely not." Star sat down heavily in her chair. Jun slid a cup of coffee across the table to her, wincing only a little as the movement pulled at his healing shoulder.

"Oh, pleeeeease," Frey wheedled, leaning across the table until he was practically in her cup. "Think about it, Star."

"We are not joining a theatre troupe."

"But we'd be so good at it." Star gave Jun a grateful nod and took a long swallow of black coffee.

"I know."

"And the money's..."

Jun shifted in his chair to set his own cup down, and the movement tugged at the stitches. He hissed through his teeth before he could stop himself.

It was barely a sound. But Frey's head whipped round, and Jun watched the grin slide off his face.

"Sorry. Sorry." Frey sat back properly, and his tail curled tight around the leg of his chair. He looked at the bandage, then at Star, who was watching him over the rim of her cup with an expression Jun couldn't quite read. "No. You're right. Forget it."

Star lowered the cup slowly. "Who are you, and what have you done with Frey?"

Frey heaved a sigh. "It was a dumb idea. All my ideas are dumb. I never stop to think what they'll cost."

Jun scratched the back of his head, suddenly awkward. "I like your dumb ideas."

He flexed two fingers, barely a gesture and on the galley wall, his guitar hanging from its hook shivered, and its strings began to move on their own, picking out a soft, unsteady melody. It was the finale of their set, the one he and Frey had sung together.

Frey stared at it. Across the table, Star's mouth twitched, and she quietly became very interested in her coffee.

Frey didn't say anything. He just smiled, slow and helpless, and under the table his tail uncurled from the chair leg and wound carefully, gently, around Jun's ankle.

End <3

The Sweet Hereafter

The bustling market was a labyrinth of stalls and colourful wares, a cacophony of voices and vibrant scents that assaulted the senses. Jun, his heart pounding with a mix of excitement and nervousness, navigated through the crowds, discreetly searching for a particular item.

His eyes landed on a small booth tucked away in a corner, its shelves adorned with an array of handmade soaps and lotions. A hint of citrus fragrance wafted through the air, drawing him closer. He smiled. Citrus was Frey's favourite scent— he’d mentioned it on a previous excursion, and Jun had filed that away in his memory for now. Frey had been looking pretty down lately, and a little gift might just be the thing to cheer him up.

Approaching the booth, Jun's gaze darted around, ensuring no one from his crew was nearby, especially a pink skinned, white haired someone. He didn't want to spoil the surprise. He examined the array of soaps on offer and the little labels that indicated what their scent was. He was sorely tempted by the nernoleaf lotion from the planet Yeosang, the smell on that was unique to the individual as the chemicals tied into positive memories. However the hefty price tag on that was more than he could possibly afford. He studied the different soups, looking for a simple citrus scented one, starting to feel a little overwhelmed by the sheer quantity and variety on offer.

The shopkeeper, an elderly halfling woman with kind eyes and weathered hands, noticed Jun's hesitance. She smiled, her voice warm and gentle. "Looking for something in particular, dear?"

Jun's cheeks flushed with a mix of embarrassment as he nodded. "I’m looking for something uh, citrusy? A strong one if you have anything like that?” He rubbed the back of his hair and peeked around to make sure nobody he knew was nearby.

The woman's eyes twinkled with curiosity, a hint of understanding in her gaze. She reached beneath the counter and produced a small box. "Ah, I see. A special someone, is it?"

Jun's eyes widened, startled by her perception. He stammered, trying to find the right words. "Y-Yes, someone very special. He loves citrus scents."

The soap-maker's smile grew wider, a touch of mischief in her eyes. "Well, I have just the one for you then. This soap is infused with the essence of sweet yuzu and lemons, a burst of sunshine in every wash, and it’s been mixed with a tiny sprig of nernoleaf, not enough to invoke memories, but just enough to make washing a… more pleasurable experience.” She winked, but Jun was looking for the price tag.

He was delighted to see it was perfectly in the range he was looking to spend. "Thank you so much. This is perfect!”

As Jun paid for the soap and carefully tucked it away in his satchel. The double meaning in the halflings' words suddenly hit him and he felt a flush rise in his cheeks. Was she implying…? He stared at the bag in his hands, did buying this soap have implications?? Did people buy each other soap together? What if this soap was a couple's sort of gift? Was that why it was under the counter? He whipped it out of the bag and studied the packaging, looking for any indication that he’d be making a social faux pas. What if it was, and he gave it to Frey and then Frey thought that he…

What if gifting it meant that Frey thought he’d want to shower together?! Jun’s eyes strained as he stared intently at the small box in his hands, trying to discern every possible meaning behind giving his friend an innocuous bar of soap. Oh gods, how could he give it now?!

“Hey, there you are! I’ve been looking all over for you!” A familiar cheery voice burst into his awareness and Jun scrambled to put the box bag into his back. He turned and smiled at Fizzy as the young woman skipped over to him. She was laden with bags, and her cheeks had a warm blush as she’d obviously been running around. “Come on Jun, are you finished shopping? The boys are at The Ragged Rook getting first drinks in. Let’s go!” Jun smiled and nodded, offering to take a couple of her bags off her and carry them, and together they headed back down the street.

Neither of them noticed the figure watching them from the shadows.

In all the years of his long life, Jun had never travelled to the Northern mountains where Star had lived. Not for a fear of cold, his own home had been on the edge of Frostfire Ridge where the winters were harsher than most. He was no stranger to cold, but he was feeling a little reserved about going to the Rokkoss mountains… He’d never not go, not when the man he called a friend had asked for his help, but Jun was still a little wary.

He wasn’t sure his team knew his ‘secret’, but he knew they wouldn’t care. Very rarely had such an eclectic group of people found friendship with each other, a blue elf, a goliath, a lizard, a tiefling-but-not-quite, and a walking boat?? The knowledge of him actually being a dark elf wouldn’t phase them. They’d never actually questioned his lineage, maybe they just didn’t care, and thought some elves were genuinely bright blue. In fairness, they cared more about his fae heritage, but that’s only because it had caused danger to them, and even then, they made jokes but still let him stick around.

So Jun wasn’t sure why he wasn’t open about some of the niggles that came with his heritage, why he’d gravitated towards Saltmarsh, with its mild weather and lukewarm sun. Bright light made his eyes hurt. It made him squint and tear up and he couldn’t see much at all when the sun was at its brightest. As a young elf on the farm, he’d suffered through, glad for the winter months when the daylight hours were few and he could work outside all day. He’d endured the summer months, relying on sunset and sunrise to get most of his work done.

As an adult he’d adapted, living in places like Saltmarsh with cloudy skies, and thankfully, on the times when he and his team had needed to explore or go out, they had been in a dungeon or swamp or underground in a mushroom cavern, so he wasn’t even more of a liability. How was he going to cope in the mountains, with blinding white snow? Star had waxed lyrical about how dangerous everything was up there, and how they were likely to have to fight a bunch of… yetis? They were going to get into a fight, no doubt. Jun didn’t want to let them down!

He wasn’t sure why he accompanied Frey to the clothing shop. He had no gold (thanks Eddie….) but the group had said they’d cover the costs of getting him a coat, to which he was incredibly thankful. He had no qualms about theft, years of poverty and struggle had crushed that morality out of him, but he didn’t want to resort to it in Saltmarsh where he somehow had gained a positive reputation.

It was valuable definitely, but if they were headed to an icy climate, the capability of having an extra fire spell was priceless… His hands touched the little skull on a chain around his neck. The amulet of thought detection.

Useful? Yes, but not without some morality concerns. Expensive? Definitely. Brian Styles had helped him purchase it, but he’d understand, or simply not care. Self indulgent sickfic

They called it the Nightmare Sickness, or just the Nightmare. It was a widespread illness that travelled through the air, and had made its way into almost every planet in the galaxy, only the most rural cities remained unexposed. Luckily, most planets had a plan in place for infection, there were widespread vaccines available, and thankfully the Nightmare had low impact on children, and it could only be caught once in a lifetime. Often parents would subject their children to the Nightmare Sickness when they were young to get it out of their system. Symptoms from the Nightmare were varied, but culminated in a burning fever and vivid hallucinations, causing the sufferer to experience waking nightmares (hence the name). In adults, the fever was difficult to treat and only responded to a very specific and expensive medication. In poor cities, adult sufferers were often left to ‘burn out’ screaming and out of their mind with terror.

There was a movement to eradicate the Nightmare Sickness and philanthropists often donated the vaccines and medicine to poor planets who were experiencing pandemics.

This was the case with planet Franklin. It was an old mining planet, but the ores had long since run dry. The only thing it had going for it now was an old salt mine as their chief export. The inhabitants eked out a hard living, and unfortunately on the latest inspection, the auditors brought with them the Nightmare Sickness, which had previously not been seen on the planet for nearly thirty years. A whole generation of the village had become sick simultaneously.

This was where the Leviathan came in.

Jun was walking to the hold, wondering where the crew where, they were due to land within the hour.

“How much is all this worth again?” He heard Frey ask, as the tiefling eyed the two crates secured firmly in the hold. Brian Styles paused strapping down the crates as he calculated,

“3.72 million credits.” Frey let out an appreciative whistle.

“That’s like 10 times what we’re getting paid for this, are you sure we couldn’t… you know.” He gave Brian Styles an elbow and a wink. Brian Styles looked at him blankly. “You knowwww.” Frey drawled.

“He knows, Frey” Jun’s disapproving look had Frey stepping away from the crates and plastering a big smile on his face,

“Ah, you know I wouldn’t really!” Frey grinned, “But, these vials are worth a lot, what if a few went missing or broke along the way.” Jun frowned.

“Each vial is potentially a life saved.” He said, “We can’t put a price on that.”

“We’re already getting paid more than the standard courier rate.” Brian Styles interjected and Frey slouched back on the nearest crate, clearly aware he was outnumbered.

“Yeah, but that’s because we’re going to a plague zone,” he complained, “clearly warrants hazard pay.” Jun frowned, but for a different reason this time,

“You’ve had the sickness though, right?” he asked, “You can’t catch it again…?” Frey waved a hand dismissively,

“Yeah, swept through the mines when I was about five or six. Never bothered me much, I just remember feeling tired and sweaty, but that wasn’t much different from working. At least when I got sick I got to have a couple of days in bed.”

Amidst the eerie ambiance of the dimly lit, fungus-infested tunnels, Star and Frey persisted in their hushed squabble, seemingly impervious to the constant, wary glances and hushed warnings from their newest companion, Mrs O. Jun trailed behind, lost in thought.

He’d thought his life was more complicated since joining the group but nothing compared to the last few days. Like a riderless cart careening down a hill, Jun had long since lost control of anything in his life.

First they were trapped by fire with no escape. Then they were in the feywild! Losing Fizzy…

He’d barely had a chance to grieve before they were tasked with what? Saving the Feywild?

Then they killed a fucking dragon! A dragon! And now they were going to infiltrate a camp full of giants accompanied by this strange-talking furry fungus woman. What had his life become?

But, it wasn’t all bad… Despite his propensity to see the worst in every situation, he couldn’t deny he’d been touched by the pool…He’d seen a glimpse of his former life, and in that fleeting moment, he had been reminded of the profound love he'd once known, a love so warm and gentle that his heart ached with the bittersweet pang of its absence.

It had been twenty years… men were born and grown and killed in that time, but he could still remember her face, lined with age, looking at him with nothing but kindness. Her voice, croaky with time and use, soft as she hummed her favourite melody. He had one picture of his parents, but a picture could never capture the tenderness of her caress, the gentle smile and the way she threw her head back with easy laughter.

The pool had gifted him that moment. In the midst of this dismal cave, filled with decay, rot, and macabre reanimations, Jun had been graced with the vision of his mother once more. He saw her tucking him into bed, gently stroking his hair, and pinching his cheeks with affection. Gods he missed her.

“-Un? Jun?”

Frey's voice snapped Jun back to the present. The tiefling was snapping his fingers in front of him, a peculiar expression on his face. "Ah, you're back with us. Thought the fungus spores had finally claimed your brain—because, you know, that's a legitimate concern," Frey quipped, a mischievous grin playing on his lips.

Jun rolled his eyes. "What do you want?"

Frey cast an exaggerated look around to ensure no one was eavesdropping, then leaned in conspiratorially, his voice a low, hushed whisper. "Well, I'm just curious, you see…" He gave his bag a teasing shake. "What was so important about those jellyfish that it made our neurotic elf break his own rules? What did you see?"

Jun frowned, hesitating for a moment before replying, "Nothing."

Frey's eyes lit up with intrigue as he leaned even closer. "Ahhh, come on," he cajoled, his voice barely audible. "If you tell me, I'll let you take a peek. Tell me that's not an offer you'd like." He waggled his eyebrows with a devilish grin, observing the scowl forming on Jun's face. The elf abruptly halted in his tracks, grappling with an internal struggle.

"Alright, fine," he conceded, his tone begrudging. "Come closer." Frey eagerly closed the distance. Jun leaned in and, with a sly grin, said, "I saw something truly amazing—a pair of jellyfish with the most exquisite, rounded, perky, and flawless... bioluminescent tendrils you can imagine."

“And you are okay then, with this? With him making the choice to shoot at that freighter without even checking if there were civilians on board!” Star demanded, shooting a questioning glance at Frey.

“Oh course I am.” Frey responded, trying to keep his voice level. “It’s what Jun thinks is best.”

“Really?” Star narrowed his eyes. “Pretty sure if it was my plan you would have big problem. I have big problem!”

“Oh give it a rest Star, he knows what he’s doing, let’s just do what he asked.” Frey snapped as he turned his back to Star and walked away. But the knot twisting in his stomach let him know that Star was right.

“Can you believe Star.” Jun scowled as Frey entered their quarters. “All he does is argue and try to undermine me.” He paused, raising an eyebrow at Frey’s silence,

“I mean, you know this is the best way, right? “Jun questioned turning his full attention to Frey. Alarmed to be put on the spot, Frey nodded. Clearly he wasn’t convincing. Jun’s brow furrowed,

“What? You don’t agree?” Frey shook his head, feeling foolish,

“No, it’s great. It’s a great plan… but it’s just..”

“Just what?” Jun prompted darkly. Frey felt a shudder run down the nerves in his spine.

“Nothing.” He finished, lamely. The elfs eyes darkened.

“Are you scared of me now?” He questioned in a low hush.

“No, don't be ridiculous.” Frey retorted, rolling his eyes

“Then what is it?”

Silence hung between them as Jun scanned his partner for any of his usual tell tale traits. Feeling the scrutiny of Jun’s gaze Frey averted his eyes off to the side, not wanting to make eye contact, telling Jun all he needed to know. His expression was stormy as he paced the small room,

“So you’re just scared to disagree with me?”

Frey didn’t verbally respond, but brought his shoulders to his ears in a deep shrug as he continued glaring off to the side. He felt like a scolded child.

“What are you so worried I’ll do? You never had an issue disagreeing with me in the past. Or telling me my ideas were stupid. In fact I’m pretty sure you enjoyed it.” Jun punctuated his words with twitching fingers, an unconscious habit that only happened when he was frustrated. Frey took a deep breath, desperate to de-escalate the conversation.

“Maybe I can just see that you’re right, even if I don’t agree with the way you’re going about it”

“What’s that supposed to mean?” Jun’s voice was low. He stopped pacing, instead standing above Frey, looking down at him. Frey hated it.

“Nothing. Can we please just drop it, Jun.” He hated how his voice was strained, it sounded like pleading.

Jun’s voice was rising as well, and his fingers were twitching and curling. “No. Not until you tell me why you’re so worried.”

“Because you might leave me!” Frey shouted.

Jun recoiled in shock.

Taking a deep breath Frey attempted to regain his composure. With watering eyes he tried explaining. “I’m worried that if I don’t go along with your ideas you might leave me...”

Jun’s mouth was agape and his eyes were wide in shock. “W-Why would you think I would ever do anything like that?” He asked.

“I don’t know.” Frey squirmed trying to think of a way to get himself out of the conversation. “Things have just changed… You’ve changed. I’m not sure that I’m really needed anymore, and you’re so sure of everything… I don’t want to get in your way.” Jun looked stricken, he sat heavily on the cot next to Frey.

“I’m just trying to keep everyone safe.” He said quietly, he clasped his hands together.

“I know!” Frey interjected “... And I appreciate it. But sometimes, the way you go about things… It’s a bit extreme. It’s not like how we used to do things.”

Jun tried to interrupt but Frey silenced him with his hand. “Look, I know things are different now, and you’ve been doing the best you can, so I’d never disagree with you in front of the team. I’m just trying to be useful to you and be on your side.

Jun’s face filled with sympathy at Frey’s words. Shuffling closer to the Tiefling he tenderly held Frey’s hands in his. Frey noticed they were a lot more calloused than he remembered and felt another stab in his heart at how things were different. Jun squeezed Frey’s hands gently and gave a weak smile. “You don’t have to agree with me to be useful. You’re the most important person to me regardless of whether you agree or not. You’re an important part of this team Frey.”

“Jun...” Frey whispered quietly, turning his head to look at the cane propped by the door, “We both know I can barely walk down the corridor without needing assistance.” He felt a familiar anger surge through him, frustration at his frail body and the burden he was on the team. Jun let go of Frey’s hand, and lifted his fingers to tenderly touch Frey’s chin, tilting his face towards him. His eyes were soft now, all traces of his earlier anger vanished. He cupped Frey’s cheek gently.

“Oh Frey,” He breathed, “I’m sorry for making you feel that way. A lot of things have changed, but not everything…” He pressed a quick kiss to the tear that was making its way down Frey’s cheek. “Nothing about the way I feel about you has changed. You’re everything to me. I know my methods have been a little…” Jun struggled to find the words

“Insane?” Frey offered, feeling his heart skip a beat as Jun laughed.

“Yeah, I guess. I need you to disagree with me, to pull me up if I get carried away.” Frey nodded. Jun sighed leaning into him a little, not too much that it might strain Frey’s still healing body. “Awful things have happened Frey,” he said, “To you, me, to everyone. We’re all still healing and it will take time. I’m just grateful to have you back with me.”

For the first time since he’d been rescued, Frey thought they might be okay.

Jun trailed behind the group as they followed the mysterious centaur deeper into the feywild, trying hard to conceal just how hard his heart was beating. He had thought he was in the feywild earlier, but now he could see that he had been wrong. There was no mistaking this was the Feywild. His blood felt shot through with electricity, dancing under his skin and he felt adrenaline rushing through his body which he wasn’t sure whether it was the magic of the area, or just the sheer consistent terror he was experiencing.

He did not want to be here.

For years his magic had been a tool, a weapon, just like a razor sharp knife. He could wield it to help others, to save lives and protect those closest to him, but just like a knife, it could easily pierce his own flesh if he wasn’t careful. And it had. There were deaths in his past that whilst he didn’t directly held the blade, he was nevertheless responsible.

His magic was capricious and dangerous. Now he was in the place where it came from. The Feywild.

His parents had told him tales, never go there, they warned, they’ll try and take you. And what was that the centaur said? He was destined? What the fuck did that mean?

He didn’t want any of this.

Grinding his palms into his eyes, Jun once again missed his parents and the life they’d shared together.

Quiet.

Peaceful.

Back then the magic had been a joy! It had been something to play with, at nights he would cast dancing lights to light up his mother’s knitting, or to entertain their cat, delighting as she would chase them across the stone floor.

Back then he and his magic were fun and carefree..

Now they were a weapon. Jun sniffed harder as a few tears escaped. Annoyed with himself he rubbed at his face even more furiously. Thankfully he was at the back of their group, as his comrades bickered good naturedly amongst one another, whispering theories about the world around them, and whether centaurs should wear pants, and if they did would it cover all four legs, or just the two back ones…

However, the newest member of the group, the tiefling who had just invited himself along, merry-as-you-go Frey turned back and caught Jun’s eye. Fearful, Jun stood straighter and offered a grim smile, praying that the other wouldn’t say anything. Thankfully, the rose skinned man just gave him a wink, and without breaking eye contact, plucked a triskelion shaped flower from the bushes and tucked it behind his decorated ear. He turned his back to Jun and carried on walking with fluid steps, the lute on his back tapping gently with the motion, thin tail swishing with a flourish.

Distracted, Jun felt a stab of annoyance! What was he doing touching things? And so flagrantly! Was Frey doing it deliberately to wind him up? After everything Jun had said about respecting their surroundings and being careful. That tiefling was going to get himself killed! Ugh!

Frustrated, he hurried up to catch up to Frey and snatched the flower from his ear, tossing it to the undergrowth to the side. He scowled, but the tiefling just gave him a big smile, patted his cheek gently and carried on after the group, leaving Jun feeling bewildered… but no longer lost in his own thoughts.
